Introduction.name: Introduction
Introduction.text:
@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.zF3HpVtMqPZgeAQu classes="noborder"]

The far-ranging story of conflicts toldin the World of Warcraft game—as well as in the other works in the Warcraft line—offers limitless possibilities for adventures in a D&D campaign. You can use the information in this chapter to craft a campaign within the ongoing official timeline of the world of Azeroth, to timewalk through different eras of play (perhaps with Chromie’s help), or to build a new storyline unique to your campaign. Other sources of Warcraft lore (including those mentioned in this book’s introduction), as well as your own World of Warcraft experience, can help you fill in the details.

This chapter details the conflicts that drive the main storylines of World of Warcraft and a selection of the game’s most iconic dungeons for you to incorporate into your own adventures.

Adapting Azeroth.name: Adapting Azeroth
Adapting Azeroth.text:
As you craft adventures for a Dungeons & Dragons campaign set in the world of Azeroth, you can find plenty of inspiration in World of Warcraft’s quests, dungeons, raids, and storylines. When adapting quests from WoW for the D&D game, keep in mind the following principles about how a tabletop roleplaying game differs from an MMO:

Avoid the Grind. Repetitive tasks are more fun in online games than they are at a table with friends, and MMO characters fight more monsters than D&D characters do. Avoid quests that involve gathering numerous unimportant objects from slain enemies and quests that involve killing a lot of monsters until a particular item drops as treasure by random chance.

Make a Difference. A D&D adventure should give characters the opportunity to make a difference in the world. Focus on MMO quests that advance the story of the game or significantly change the world.

Make Success Last. When the characters accomplish something, don’t reset that accomplishment. While MMO characters frequently repeat adventures, D&D players will be frustrated if everything their characters accomplish is undone so they have to do it again. If characters venture into a dungeon multiple times, change the dungeon between visits so the players can see the effects of what their characters did previously.

Shine a Spotlight. The characters in a D&D campaign are the stars of their story, and they shouldn’t be overshadowed by other adventurers or even famous figures like @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowThrallGZRj1Vq]{Thrall}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowAnduinWrynnEj]{Anduin Wrynn}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowJainaProudmiL]{Jaina Proudmoore}, or @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowSylvanasWinqT]{Sylvanas Windrunner}. Let the characters in your campaign enjoy the spotlight and be the heroes that Azeroth needs.

Minimally Multiplayer. Most D&D games have no more than four or five adventurers, with the rest of the world populated by nonplayer characters and monsters controlled by the DM. That means characters can’t put loot they don’t want up in the auction house for other players to buy—so customize treasure so it’s useful for the players at your table.

Introduction.text:
@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.rzpdsiEiHQ5BFYsN caption=false classes="noborder"]

The knightly Order of the Argent Dawn is dedicated to protecting Azeroth from the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowConflictsOfAz.JournalEntryPage.mOeoKWAu3OOx8LP9]{Burning Legion}, the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowConflictsOfAz.JournalEntryPage.YRwQ3wrLM22odUUP]{Scourge}, and other forces that seek to destroy the world. Neutral in the continual conflict between the Alliance and the Horde (and generally Neutral Good in alignment), the Argent Dawn calls both factions allies in its higher purpose of resisting these forces of evil. The order’s headquarters is Light’s Hope Chapel, in the Eastern Plaguelands—a beacon of hope and comfort in a barren and twisted land—and the knights operate across the Plaguelands and anywhere evil rears its head.

In addition to pursuing quests assigned to them by the Argent Dawn, characters can increase their Renown Score by killing powerful Fiends and Undead and bringing evidence of the monsters’ destruction to Argent Dawn agents.

Argent Dawn Renown Perks.name: Argent Dawn Renown Perks
Argent Dawn Renown Perks.text:
Increasing your Renown Score with the Argent Dawn gives you the following additional benefits.

Argent Dawn: Friendly

Prerequisite: Renown 3+ with the Argent Dawn

You receive the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.items.Item.wowBlessingOfArg]{Blessing of Argent Will}. This Blessing gives you Advantage on saving throws to avoid or end the Charmed condition caused by a Fiend or Undead. You lose the Blessing if your Renown Score with the Argent Dawn falls below 3.

Argent Dawn: Honored

Prerequisite: Renown 10+ with the Argent Dawn

If you spend a Long Rest in Light’s Hope Chapel or another Argent Dawn sanctuary, you gain a Charm that lasts for 7 days or until you use it. The Charm allows you to cast @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplHealingWor]{Healing Word} once.

Argent Dawn: Revered

Prerequisite: Renown 25+ with the Argent Dawn

You receive the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.items.Item.wowBlessingArgen]{Blessing of Argent Fortitude}. This Blessing gives you Immunity to the &Reference[Poisoned apply=false] condition and Poison damage. You lose the Blessing if your Renown Score with the Argent Dawn falls below 25.

Argent Dawn: Exalted

Prerequisite: Renown 50+ with the Argent Dawn

For a cost of 15,000 GP, the Argent Dawn will add a magical property to any Rare magic item you are attuned to. While attuned to the item, you have Resistance to one of the following damage types (chosen when the property is added): Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, Necrotic, Poison, Psychic, Radiant, or Thunder. The item’s rarity then increases to Very Rare.

Overview.name: Overview
Overview.text:
For Level 17–20 Characters • The Scourge

Azjol-Nerub, the old kingdom of the nerubians, lies in ruin. This arachnid people once dwelled in glorious cavern-cities carved through the stone of North­rend by enslaved jormungar worms. But times have changed. After the Lich King swept through Azjol-Nerub and reanimated the dead in his wake as his Scourge minions, the surviving nerubians fled deeper into the earth. Their tunneling awakened a greater evil: the faceless minions of the Old God Yogg-­Saron. Faced with war from above and below, a group of living nerubians called the Azjol-anak hid underground, plotting the downfall of both the Scourge and the Faceless Ones, as well as the reclamation of their lost realm.

Azjol-Nerub Adventures.name: Azjol-Nerub Adventures
Azjol-Nerub Adventures.text:
Use the suggestions in the Azjol-Nerub Adventure Hooks table to create adventures there. Multiple hooks could be active at once, creating a main quest and a side quest.

Azjol-Nerub Areas.name: Azjol-Nerub Areas
Azjol-Nerub Areas.text:
@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.YeNBZ57PeL4eSUWB caption=false classes="float-right size-three noborder"]

The characters will likely travel through the following areas of Azjol-Nerub in the listed order:

Gilded Gate. Ice caves lead to a locked gate guarded by six @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowNerubianCryYE]{Nerubian Crypt Fiends} (see chapter 7) and a towering nerubian sage called @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowKrikthirtheTz]{Krik’thir the Gatewatcher} (see “Azjol-Nerub Characters”). Krik’thir holds the key to the gate; the lock is complex (1 minute to pick) and of superior quality (DC 20).

Web-Choked Chasm. A slender bridge leads across a chasm but is broken halfway across. A wall of webs blocks further progress to the east, but a makeshift floor spun from webs allows characters access to a tunnel that spirals downward to the northeast. Halfway down, the characters are attacked by six @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowNerubianCryYE]{Nerubian Crypt Fiends} (see chapter 7) that rush down the long staircases in the west of the chamber from their barracks (not shown).

Hadronox’s Lair. The spiraling tunnel leads down to a funnel web where @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowHadronoxS7qle]{Hadronox} (see “Azjol-­Nerub Characters”) waits for prey. Bones are piled into vast mounds beneath the stairs.

Passage of Lost Fiends. At the bottom of the funnel web, some 100 feet below the bridge from the Gilded Gate, a 300-foot drop leads through centuries of nerubian architecture to the depths of the Brood Pit.

Brood Pit. In the Brood Pit, thousands of nerubian eggs, already infected with undeath, prepare to hatch into new warriors for the Lich King. A @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowNraqiFaceleeQ]{N’raqi Faceless One} (see chapter 7) called Herald Volazj (see “Azjol-Nerub Characters”) meditates at the bottom, watched by two @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowNerubianCryYE]{Nerubian Crypt Fiends} (see chapter 7) brood keepers. Volazj psychically communes with Yogg-Saron while awaiting an audience with Anub’arak.

Throne of the Traitor King. @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowAnubarakLx3lz]{Anub’arak} (see “Azjol-­Nerub Characters”) dwells here, guarding the exit into Icecrown. A circular platform stands in the middle of the room; its top is 50 feet above a floor of webs. When the characters enter, he is burrowed into the platform, waiting to ambush anyone who crosses. Two @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowNerubianVen2W]{Nerubian Venomancers} (see chapter 7) lurk in the webs below.

Resting in Azjol-Nerub.name: Resting in Azjol-Nerub
Resting in Azjol-Nerub.text:
Back-to-back boss battles can exhaust the characters quickly, forcing them to rest. Nerubian structures are built into the cliffs above and below what’s shown on the map. By ascending or descending 100 feet, the characters can find an empty room to rest in. The characters must make a DC 15 Dexterity (Stealth) check to try to conceal themselves during a Short Rest or a DC 25 check during a Long Rest.

Interrupting a Rest

If more than half the party fails this check, their rest is interrupted by a patrol of four @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowNerubianCryYE]{Nerubian Crypt Fiends} (see chapter 7).

Azjol-Nerub Characters.name: Azjol-Nerub Characters
Azjol-Nerub Characters.text: Azjol-Nerub’s key NPCs are mostly minions of the Lich King, but those who fight the Scourge could become unlikely allies of explorers. These NPCs are presented in the order they’re most likely encountered.

Hadronox.name: Hadronox
Hadronox.text:
“SKREEEEEE!”

During the fall of Azjol-Nerub, nerubian viziers released a single spider that would one day grow to challenge the unyielding forces of the Lich King. Hadronox was instilled with a desire to avenge the fallen and reclaim its home from any that dare threaten it.

Anub’arak’s minions fight relentlessly (but fruitlessly) to drive Hadronox from their realm. When the characters breach the Gilded Gate, these minions turn to fight the characters. Hadronox temporarily acts as the characters’ ally against Anub’arak’s minions—but only for a moment. Hadronox craves the taste of fresh flesh.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowHadronoxS7qle statblock caption=false classes="double-column hide-in-embed"]

Seer Ixit.name: Seer Ixit
Seer Ixit.text:
“Our enemies believe us vanquished. We will show them the consequence of their ignorance.”

Seer Ixit, who might serve as a quest giver for this dungeon (see “Azjol-Nerub Adventures”), is an ambitious and resilient sorcerer with an enormous ego and an uncommon fondness for surface folk. He dreams of reviving the Nerubian Empire by banishing the Faceless Ones and annihilating the Scourge, starting with Traitor King Anub’arak. His dreams can be achieved only with the aid of the Alliance or the Horde.

@UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowSeerIxithEJ76]{Ixit} is a Nerubian Venomancer (see chapter 7).

About Azjol-Nerub

Introduced in the Wrath of the Lich King expan- sion, Azjol-Nerub is a dungeon designed for five characters of great power. The dungeon’s story is part of the ongoing war against Arthas, the Lich King. By preventing him from enslaving the living nerubians of Azjol-Nerub, the characters simul- taneously gain powerful allies and rob Arthas of potential Undead reinforcements.

As presented here, Azjol-Nerub incorporates elements of a related dungeon, Ahn’kahet, called the Old Kingdom. While the focus of adventures in Azjol-Nerub is overthrowing the undead Trai- tor King Anub’arak, adventures in Ahn’kahet (the lower reaches of an ancient subterranean city) include the n’raqi and the malign influence of Yogg-Saron.

Anub’arak.name: Anub’arak
Anub’arak.text:
“I was king of this empire once, long ago. In life I stood as champion. In death I returned as conqueror. Now I protect the kingdom once more. Ironic, yes?”

The Traitor King of the nerubians, Anub’arak, fought tirelessly against the Scourge until his death. Now, the prideful king is a lapdog of the Lich King, guarding Azjol-Nerub from Alliance and Horde forces that would use it as a passage into Icecrown, as he once did. Anub’arak throws himself recklessly into every fight, perhaps hoping to die and finally be free of the Lich King’s domination.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowAnubarakLx3lz statblock caption=false classes="double-column hide-in-embed"]

Krik’thir the Gatewatcher.name: Krik’thir the Gatewatcher
Krik’thir the Gatewatcher.text:
“This kingdom belongs to the Scourge. Only the dead may enter!”

When the Scourge first came to North­rend, Krik’thir was in charge of defending the gates of Azjol-Nerub. He fell in battle against the Scourge forces, and he was raised to undeath. He still holds the key that grants access to the lower reaches of the ancient city, but now he guards it for the Scourge.

Herald Volazj.name: Herald Volazj
Herald Volazj.text:
“Gaze into the void. It is the perpetuity in which they dwell.”

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.xSfkFw6Yy5k86tDV caption=false classes="noborder float-right size-three"]

The will of Yogg-Saron is mighty. The Old God has sent his herald, a @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowNraqiFaceleeQ]{N’raqi Faceless One} (see chapter 7) called Volazj from depths of the fallen nerubian kingdom of Ahn’kahet to cull the beleaguered nerubians and annihilate anyone foolish enough to threaten the Old God.

CR 23: @UUID[.sQa6C6h11x1195NE]{Bronze Dragonflight Dragon}, @UUID[.hKjF6BYRWJKUDe4p]{Ragnaros}, @UUID[.Ap4IohwjR27e1muD]{Sylvanas Windrunner}

CR 24: @UUID[.E0R7aBAs6xKNukZc]{Illidan Stormrage}

CR 25: @UUID[.HtscVm1fdlzer43M]{Lich King Arthas}

Abomination.name: Abomination
Abomination.text:
@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.M0I9iKTZEiDkAN8N caption=false classes="noborder"]

Unholy Combination of Stitched Dead Flesh

Habitat: Any; Treasure: Arcana

Abominations are flesh constructs made from the reanimated body parts of mutilated corpses. Held together by loose stitching and pieces of metal and bone, they reek of death and disease, dangling entrails and dripping fluids from open wounds as they bound relentlessly forward, cleavers in hand. Though their lolling heads and gaping mouths appear almost joyful, they are driven by little more than their desire to carve through and consume flesh, whether it belongs to the living or the dead.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowAbominationK5 statblock caption=false classes="double-column hide-in-embed"]

Black Dragonflight.name: Black Dragonflight
Black Dragonflight.text:
@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.96QGqLCH4rP7VYvb caption=false classes="noborder"]

Warders of the Earth Corrupted to Evil

Habitat: Mountain, Swamp; Treasure: Any

The black dragonflight has power over earth and flame and was charged in ancient times with protecting the deep places of the earth. This flight was corrupted by the whispers of the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowConflictsOfAz.JournalEntryPage.QX2LRHkL98AMmC55]{Old Gods} imprisoned beneath the earth and fell to evil. The dragons now lair in sweltering, desolate places such as Blackrock Mountain and Dustwallow Marsh, ruled by the children of Deathwing that revel in mortal suffering. The corrupted black dragons are the enemies of every other dragonflight, especially the noble @UUID[.DmsSoir1i1hgTyRj]{red dragonflight}.

Who would have thought someone named Deathwing would bring about so much destruction?

—Chromie

Blue Dragonflight.name: Blue Dragonflight
Blue Dragonflight.text:
@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.Gr9lHgFxBY61ohri caption=false classes="noborder"]

Protectors of Ancient Magic

Habitat: Arctic; Treasure: Any

The blue dragonflight was devastated by the evil Deathwing and his @UUID[.jnGTp7LiVzQO8DTY]{black dragonflight}. Now led by Kalecgos, the Steward of Magic, the blue dragonflight is enjoying a resurgence, and these dragons’ magical powers are awesome to behold. Their freezing breath and gargantuan claws have been the death of many foolish intruders in Azeroth’s mountains and arctic regions.

Bronze Dragonflight.name: Bronze Dragonflight
Bronze Dragonflight.text:
@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.OhHCGoN0MTBEdP0a caption=false classes="noborder"]

Guardians of Time

Habitat: Desert; Treasure: Any

Ruled by Nozdormu the Timeless One, the bronze dragonflight guards the timeways of Azeroth. These stoic guardians maintain the delicate balance of past, present, and future, and they can facilitate time travel by opening time portals. The people of Azeroth often see bronze dragons as cold and unfeeling, since the dragons prefer not to interfere in mortal affairs.

Bronze dragons’ enemies, the infinite dragonflight, are led by Murozond, a version of Nozdormu from an alternate timeline that seeks to “perfect” the timeline by altering key moments in history. Infinite dragonflight dragons use the same statistics as bronze dragonflight dragons.

Doomguard.name: Doomguard
Doomguard.text:
Brutal Destroyer from the Burning Legion

Habitat: Planar (Twisting Nether); Treasure: Individual

Powerful and deliberate, doomguard are winged demons of the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowConflictsOfAz.JournalEntryPage.mOeoKWAu3OOx8LP9]{Burning Legion} known across the cosmos for their brutality. Also called ered’ruin, doomguard are devoted to their pit lord masters and revel in the destruction of worlds.

Doomguard sport furry, cloven-hoofed legs and formidable horns. Soaring through the skies, they swoop down to ram into foes or shake the earth with thunderous stomps.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowDoomguardXS6A statblock caption=false classes="double-column hide-in-embed"]

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.f9ijMD2UKF6B8u8V caption=false classes="noborder"]

Fel Imp.name: Fel Imp
Fel Imp.text:
Gleeful Demon of Fel Flames

Habitat: Planar (Twisting Nether); Treasure: Individual

Through all time and space, there’s more power hidden in the smallest things than you will ever know.

—Chromie

Fel imps are mischievous demons that cackle with glee while immolating their foes in fel flames. They are the weakest forces of the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowConflictsOfAz.JournalEntryPage.mOeoKWAu3OOx8LP9]{Burning Legion}, but their small size leads enemies to underestimate the power of their firebolts.

Fel imps are the easiest demons for Warlocks to bind and control, making them common familiars for those who make pacts with the Burning Legion.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowFelImpEEKWKFi statblock caption=false classes="double-column hide-in-embed"]

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.yQ8EqJ4EmImrsBaG caption=false classes="noborder"]

Anduin Wrynn.name: Anduin Wrynn
Anduin Wrynn.text:
@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.cr0CR2YCzgTtimvG caption=false classes="float-right size-three noborder"]

King of Stormwind and Commander of the Alliance

Anduin Wrynn is the king of Stormwind. Beloved by his people, the Young Lion has been the target of assassination, manipulation, and kidnapping attempts all his life, yet it never stopped his kind heart from seeking peace between @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowTheAlliance00]{the Alliance} and its foes.

His bold and martial father, King Varian Wrynn, died horribly at the hands of the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowConflictsOfAz.JournalEntryPage.mOeoKWAu3OOx8LP9]{Burning Legion}, testing tender Anduin’s mettle when he took the throne in the midst of a demonic invasion. Now that the existential threat of the Legion has been defeated, the old tensions between the Alliance and @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowTheHorde00000]{the Horde} have reignited. Anduin must ask himself: Can he still lead his people peacefully when friends and foes alike clamor for war? Can he be true to his own heart, when his allies long for him to be his father?

This stat block and character description represents Anduin as the king of Stormwind, as he appears in Battle for Azeroth and beyond.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowAnduinWrynnEj statblock caption=false classes="double-column hide-in-embed"]

Alleria Windrunner.name: Alleria Windrunner
Alleria Windrunner.text:
@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.vQBbOR8hxqxHKN5a classes="size-three float-right noborder" caption=false]

Void-Infused Elf Who Guides Her Kin

The eldest Windrunner sister, Alleria is a light in the darkness for her people—or perhaps she is darkness within the light. @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowTheAlliance00]{The Alliance} knows her best as a hero of the Second War, venerated alongside her peers with a towering statue in Stormwind City’s Valley of Heroes. Like them, she was thought to have died in Outland.

Alleria and her husband, the human paladin Turalyon, became warriors of the Light and journeyed deep into the Twisting Nether to fight the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowConflictsOfAz.JournalEntryPage.mOeoKWAu3OOx8LP9]{Burning Legion} on far-flung worlds. In this time, Alleria dabbled in forbidden magic, and gained the power of @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowTheWorldOfWar.JournalEntryPage.39WbPfMoJEVvbg15]{the Void}. She returned to Azeroth after forty years away, though the time dilation of the Twisting Nether made it like a thousand years of war to her. Though she was feared by the Army of Light, she was admitted into the Alliance and trained a cohort of elves to welcome shadow into their own bodies and become @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowElf0000000000.JournalEntryPage.RMfuWvj6ufycMJo0]{void elves} like her.

Though still at odds with her husband, Alleria has tried to rebuild her bond with her estranged son, Arator, and her former homeland of Quel’Thalas. More than anything, she craves connection, as her desire for enough power to protect those she loves inevitably drives them away. She swears she can remain in control of her Void powers, but those close to her fear that her control will fail.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowAlleriaWindf2 statblock caption=false classes="double-column hide-in-embed"]

Felhound.name: Felhound
Felhound.text:
@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.0Ovb2PlnSkvzvPHI caption=false classes="noborder"]

Demonic Hound with a Nose for Magic

No! Bad doggie … hound … fel … thing! Get your tentacles off my codex!

—Chromie

Habitat: Planar (Twisting Nether); Treasure: None

Felhounds are demonic canines used by pit lords to sniff out sources of magic. Unlike most demons, which are born of corrupted mortals, felhounds are shaped from raw fel energy.

Felhounds feed on magic, and they are fond of draining the energies of hapless wizards with the grasping tentacles on their back, then ripping the wizards’ bodies to shreds.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowFelhoundNi2CR statblock caption=false classes="double-column hide-in-embed"]

Furbolgs.name: Furbolgs
Furbolgs.text:
@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.KNsn0p88GtOGnQo7 caption=false classes="float-right size-three noborder"]

Bearlike People of Secluded Woodlands

Habitat: Forest; Treasure: Individual

Bearlike furbolgs live in family groups across northern Kalimdor, Northrend, and several island regions. They fought alongside night elves and tauren against the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowConflictsOfAz.JournalEntryPage.mOeoKWAu3OOx8LP9]{Burning Legion} in the War of the Ancients, though they prefer to live separate from other peoples. Furbolg traditions involve shamanic control of the elements. Some furbolgs have been corrupted and fallen under the sway of the Burning Legion, the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowConflictsOfAz.JournalEntryPage.QX2LRHkL98AMmC55]{Old Gods}, or the Primalists. (Use the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-monster-manual.actors.Actor.mmCultist0000000]{cultist} stat blocks from the Monster Manual for these furbolgs.)

Green Dragonflight.name: Green Dragonflight
Green Dragonflight.text:
@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.9IJ7LaJbak6Rj7Rs caption=false classes="noborder"]

Graceful Protectors of Life and Nature

Spending time with the green dragonflight always makes me sleepy.

—Chromie

Habitat: Forest, Planar (Emerald Dream); Treasure: Any

Green dragons serve nature and uphold the balance between mortal creatures and the ever-evolving world. The green dragonflight, originally ruled by the dreaming Aspect Ysera, holds a special love for the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowElf0000000000.JournalEntryPage.C4fRQxnWgEHPPK1W]{night elves} and their druids. Though most green dragons live in the mystical dimension known as the Emerald Dream, some roam ancient forests where the veil between Azeroth and the Dream is thin.

This connection makes green dragons susceptible to the corrupting evil of the Emerald Nightmare. A Nightmare-corrupted green dragon has blackened scales pushed apart by pulsing red veins. Its stat block has the following changes:

  • It has Resistance to Necrotic damage instead of Acid damage.

  • Its Emerald Gas Breath action deals Necrotic damage instead of Acid damage (but still deals Poison damage).

Illidan Stormrage.name: Illidan Stormrage
Illidan Stormrage.text:
@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.F1wSmy6vDEpT6J2k caption=false classes="noborder"]

First of the Demon Hunters

Illidan Stormrage is the first demon hunter and bears a demon hunter’s sinister wings, curling horns, and fel-green eyes. Originally a powerful night elf mage, he was dubbed “The Betrayer” for aiding the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowConflictsOfAz.JournalEntryPage.mOeoKWAu3OOx8LP9]{Burning Legion} during the War of the Ancients and was imprisoned for ten thousand years by his twin brother, Archdruid Malfurion Stormrage.

Unknown to his brother or his beloved, Tyrande Whisperwind, Illidan sought the Legion’s power to wield it against them and save his people. Now free from his imprisonment, he has fled into the Twisting Nether to evade his pursuers. There, he trains other elves as demon hunters and leads raids against the Burning Legion across the cosmos, but he trusts no living soul, mortal or demonic.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowIllidanStor7Y statblock caption=false classes="double-column hide-in-embed"]

Ancient of War.name: Ancient of War
Ancient of War.text:
Protector of Nature in Tree Form

Habitat: Forest; Treasure: Relics

Ancients of War are protectors of nature and guardians of life that take the form of giant sentient trees. Though they can appear to be ordinary trees when motionless, they hold deep wisdom, cultivated over lives that last for thousands of years and preserved through memories that are as long as their roots are deep. Ancients can sense disturbances in the world through their roots and provide power and protection to those who would keep the world and its natural places safe.

Ancients of War bear bark like iron scarred with the marks of ten thousand years of battles. They patrol the deep forests of Kalimdor with their night elf allies and lead the charge against those who would defile their domain.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.qKvxAuQTRbPg9AzL caption=false classes="noborder"]

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowAncientofWa1o statblock caption=false classes="hide-in-embed"]

Felguard.name: Felguard
Felguard.text:
Foot Soldier of the Burning Legion

Habitat: Planar (Twisting Nether); Treasure: Individual

Conscripted from the demonic mo’arg species, felguard serve as the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowConflictsOfAz.JournalEntryPage.mOeoKWAu3OOx8LP9]{Burning Legion}’s rank-and-file soldiers. They are fearless and unwaveringly loyal to Sargeras’s godlike will.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowFelguardtHf0N statblock caption=false classes="double-column hide-in-embed"]

Infernal.name: Infernal
Infernal.text:
Mindless Construct of Flame and Fury

Fel burning rocks that crash to the ground: super not cool!

—Chromie

Habitat: Planar (Twisting Nether); Treasure: None

Infernals are crafted by mighty demons and summoned by warlocks’ magic. Falling to the earth as yellow-green, molten meteorites, infernals exist only to destroy every living thing in their path. Infernals have destroyed entire cities before their energies dissipated back into the Twisting Nether.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowInfernal6pGoe statblock caption=false classes="double-column hide-in-embed"]

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.W1jPeVav2nASvUJl caption=false classes="noborder"]

Jaina Proudmoore.name: Jaina Proudmoore
Jaina Proudmoore.text:
The Most Powerful Archmage Alive

Jaina Proudmoore’s people called her the Daughter of the Sea. She left behind her life in the nautical kingdom of @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowHuman00000000.JournalEntryPage.b5Jfulr9rBcvQYN9]{Kul Tiras} to study under the greatest archmages of the age in @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowHuman00000000.JournalEntryPage.6Qdz0upjGNKOEfUj]{Dalaran}. After the Third War, she became a legendary archmage of the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowKirinTor00000]{Kirin Tor} but has been forced to guard her heart, lest she suffer the pain of betrayal once more.

Jaina’s hopes for peace died during the Cataclysm, when the bloodthirsty new Warchief of the Horde, Garrosh Hellscream, bombed her city of Theramore into oblivion. @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowTheHorde00000]{The Horde} was no longer to be trusted, despite her friendship with @UUID[.ov9oiUlPla63ZejV]{Thrall}. From this nadir, she must discover who she truly is: the icy-hearted archmage she has been forced to become or the hopeful person she once was.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.owOliAVgDVni0H8B caption=false classes="noborder"]

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowJainaProudmiL statblock caption=false classes="double-column hide-in-embed"]

Moonkin.name: Moonkin
Moonkin.text:
Moon-Blessed Guardian of Sacred Nature

Habitat: Forest; Treasure: None

Moonkin, which resemble an antlered cross between a bear and a large owl, are believed by many to have been made by the moon goddess Elune to guard her sanctuaries. Moonkin often work alongside night elves and the @UUID[.wWBP2j6xQk2Tc6AZ]{green dragonflight} to purify moonwells, defend against corrupted @UUID[.gpaXzuJeSb0dZxx6]{furbolgs}, and halt deforestation. Moonkin are generally peaceful, but they lash out when nature is unbalanced by
evil magic.

Moonkin carry the blessing of Elune, giving them a deep connection to the moon. Through Elune’s blessing, they share the grace and beauty of their druidic magic with those they encounter and can call on Elune’s power to strike those who act contrary to her purpose.

Wildkin

Wildkin are a lesser form of moonkin, less infused with @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowTheWorldOfWar.JournalEntryPage.Jm2kfPalxs8mphjd#elune]{Elune’s} magic and more like wild beasts than druidic protectors. Use the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-monster-manual.actors.Actor.mmPrimevalOwlbea]{Primeval Owlbear} stat block in the Monster Manual for ordinary wildkin.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowMoonkin4Vvu2H statblock caption=false classes="double-column hide-in-embed"]

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.4elxxZ6y6IE85Y7z caption=false classes="noborder"]

Lich King Arthas.name: Lich King Arthas
Lich King Arthas.text:
@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.JJgrLUXJAzFlmm4C caption=false classes="noborder"]

Heir to the Frozen Throne

The day Arthas was born, the forests of Lordaeron whispered his name. Under strict tutelage, the beloved prince bloomed into a mighty paladin, but pride festered in his noble heart. He thought himself capable of singlehandedly protecting Lordaeron from threat. Yet when he was outmatched, he discarded his allies and sought power at any cost.

That power came to him in @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.items.Item.wowFrostmourneKA]{Frostmourne}, the cursed blade of Ner’zhul the Lich King. He took the blade to end the Cult of the Damned that spread an plague of undeath across his land, but he became the Lich King’s pawn. In the end, he engulfed his homeland in the plague he sought to save it from, and in time he even donned the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.items.Item.wowHelmofDominAS]{Helm of Domination}, which contained the Lich King’s spirit.

With Arthas’s body and soul merged with the will of the Lich King, it’s unclear whether a trace of his former self remains. He seems utterly remorseless, but it’s possible some trace of the paladin he used to be is still capable of mercy.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowLichKingArtFi statblock caption=false classes="double-column hide-in-embed"]

Murlocs.name: Murlocs
Murlocs.text:
@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.FWcSBbcIYre6VjHO caption=false classes="float-right size-three noborder"]

Amphibious People of Coastal Waters

Habitat: Coastal; Treasure: Individual

Since murlocs emerged from the oceans of Azeroth, these amphibious, piscine raiders have been steadily moving inland, forming communities along the banks of freshwater lakes and rivers. Murloc communities are close knit and insular, defending against conquest with simple weapons and elemental magic.

Murlocs were once forced to serve the @UUID[.Tog74lVhgL5a8Jo6]{naga} as disposable workers and warriors, and their emergence onto land might be driven by a desire to avoid that fate.

Though some dismiss murlocs as pawns in larger conflicts, and very few understand the murlocs’ primary language, Nerglish, murlocs are strategic fighters who use their ability to breathe, maneuver, and fight in both air and water to their advantage. Murlocs are also willing to sacrifice for one another, using sheer numbers to make up for their individual weakness.

Nozdormu says I have the memory of a murloc, which is why I always write things down.

—Chromie

Naga.name: Naga
Naga.text:
Sinister Serpentine Servants of the Old Gods

Habitat: Coastal, Underwater; Treasure: Individual

The naga were once @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowElf0000000000.JournalEntryPage.C4fRQxnWgEHPPK1W]{night elves}, Highborne followers of Queen Azshara. After the War of the Ancients, Queen Azshara pledged herself and her followers to the Old God N’Zoth, who transformed them into aquatic minions. The naga vaguely resemble to their elven forms, with humanoid arms and torsos and long, snaky tails. Male naga have snakelike heads, while female naga have humanlike heads but often have four or more arms.

Nerubians.name: Nerubians
Nerubians.text:
Spiderlike Heirs of an Ancient Realm

Habitat: Any; Treasure: Arcana

Can I just say I ’m glad you survived the … oh, wait. That hasn’t happened yet.

—Chromie

Nerubians are intelligent humanoid spiders whose once-powerful kingdom was decimated by the Scourge, leaving them either scattered across the world or turned to undead in the service of the Lich King. The nerubians evolved from the aqir, the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowConflictsOfAz.JournalEntryPage.QX2LRHkL98AMmC55]{Old Gods}’ insectile servitors, after the aqir’s rule was overthrown by trolls. Then early nerubians founded great kingdoms: Azj-Kahet, deep within the sunken continent of Khaz Algar, and @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowAzjolnerub000]{Azjol-Nerub}, which extended beneath the surface of Northrend.

The nerubians of Azjol-Nerub lived in peace for thousands of years until the Lich King Ner’zhul and the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowConflictsOfAz.JournalEntryPage.YRwQ3wrLM22odUUP]{Scourge} conquered Northrend. The nerubians bravely resisted the Lich King’s armies, resisting his plague of undeath and psychic Domination powers and holding the line against the Scourge’s relentless advance, but Azjol-Nerub eventually fell to the Lich King’s power. Most nerubians were either destroyed or killed and then raised into undeath, becoming crypt fiends. Those who survived remain scattered in small groups that have vowed to one day defeat the Scourge and retake their lost underground realm.

Pit Lord.name: Pit Lord
Pit Lord.text:
@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.SDcUa79ihHuPMCIN caption=false classes="noborder"]

Hulking General of the Burning Legion

Habitat: Planar (Twisting Nether); Treasure: Individual

The pit lords who fanatically serve Mannoroth the Destructor are some of the most cruel, barbarous butchers to ever roam the trackless wastes of the Great Dark Beyond. Also called annihilan, these hulking demons love only to kill and bring sorrow to living creatures. Pit lords will stop at nothing to uphold the will of the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowConflictsOfAz.JournalEntryPage.mOeoKWAu3OOx8LP9]{Burning Legion}.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowPitLord9YhVsw statblock caption=false classes="double-column hide-in-embed"]

Quilboar.name: Quilboar
Quilboar.text:
@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.jGlfdL1vnmOFp5yd caption=false classes="float-right size-three noborder"]

Boar-Like People with Protective Spines

Habitat: Desert, Hill; Treasure: Individual

Believed to be the mortal descendants of the demigod Agamaggan, a mighty boar felled during the War of the Ancients, quilboar resemble humanoid boars with a row of razor-sharp spines down their backs. They often make their homes among the large patches of thorn-covered vines on Azeroth that are believed to have been grown from Agamaggan’s blood, though they have attacked nearby creatures and communities to expand their territory. Quilboar are fearless and aggressive.

The Razorfen is the mightiest quilboar tribe, and its expansion across the Barrens has driven countless smaller clans into Durotar, Mulgore, and beyond, forcing them into conflict with the Horde. The Death’s Head tribe, seeking supremacy over not just the Horde but their own kin, allied with the Scourge and willingly gave themselves to undeath.

See the “Furbolgs, Murlocs, and Quilboar” sidebar in @UUID[.kPbBD95KtUwPa7y7]{Murlocs} in this chapter for suggestions on other Humanoid stat blocks to use for quilboar NPCs.

Ragnaros.name: Ragnaros
Ragnaros.text:
@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.h1Vr9QTeLrDIUECn caption=false classes="noborder"]

The Firelord, Elemental Ruler of the Firelands

Didn’t we meet fighting Ragnaros’s forces on Mount Hyjal? Was that the first time we met? Or will it be the last?

—Chromie

Ragnaros is the most infamous of the four great @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowConflictsOfAz.JournalEntryPage.DUxMQYjqDUIm5sGd]{elemental lords} (see chapter 6). Like the other elemental lords, Ragnaros warred against the Old Gods when they first came to Azeroth but eventually succumbed to their corrupting influence and became one of their mightiest servants. The titan keepers imprisoned Ragnaros on the Elemental Plane, but after millennia of rulership over his fiery prison, he was summoned back to Azeroth.

The @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowDwarf00000000.JournalEntryPage.Ctzza0M3S3xta3Gv]{Dark Iron dwarves} accidentally called Ragnaros forth in a last-ditch effort to win a war against the other dwarven clans. Ragnaros’s volcanic reemergence devastated the land for miles around and created the ashen peak of Blackrock Mountain, which now looms over @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowTheAlliance00.JournalEntryPage.w20Iuh5ocASVxvhS]{Stormwind} and @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowTheAlliance00.JournalEntryPage.oyPozuVXGusZiqIe]{Ironforge}. The Firelord is pyroclastic devastation incarnate. He sees all mortals as insects and can’t be reasoned with or bewitched. Ragnaros’s worshippers include flamewakers (use the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-monster-manual.actors.Actor.mmSalamander0000]{Salamander} stat block in the Monster Manual) and the Dark Iron clan.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowRagnarosjY03L statblock caption=false classes="double-column hide-in-embed"]

Red Dragonflight.name: Red Dragonflight
Red Dragonflight.text:
@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.RwYubSSqWLByMSL6 caption=false classes="noborder"]

Noble Dragons Charged with Protecting Life

Habitat: Any; Treasure: Any

The red dragonflight, ruled by Alexstrasza the Life-Binder, is noble and honorable. Dragons of this flight consider themselves the protectors of life. They often protect sacred areas and items, seeking to keep them from lesser beings. Their mission is to destroy existential threats to life, and they have aided in wars against the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowConflictsOfAz.JournalEntryPage.QX2LRHkL98AMmC55]{Old Gods}, the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowConflictsOfAz.JournalEntryPage.mOeoKWAu3OOx8LP9]{Burning Legion}, the @UUID[.HtscVm1fdlzer43M]{Lich King}, and the black dragon aspect Deathwing—their most hated enemy.

Red dragons are likely to be allies to heroes of both @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowTheAlliance00]{the Alliance} and @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowTheHorde00000]{the Horde}, though some red dragons have been turned to evil by the Old Gods’ corrupting whispers.

Satyrs.name: Satyrs
Satyrs.text:
@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.Tp93lST0uxwX3WVh caption=false classes="float-right size-three noborder"]

Ancient Elves Corrupted by Fel Forces

Habitat: Forest; Treasure: Arcana

The first satyr was a Highborne @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowElf0000000000.JournalEntryPage.C4fRQxnWgEHPPK1W]{night elf} named Xavius, a servant of Sargeras during the War of the Ancients. As punishment for Xavius’s failures, Sargeras destroyed the elf and remade him in a demonic form, with goatlike horns and hooves, shaggy fur, and brutal claws. Xavius’s curse spread through his allies and followers, and these satyrs now live in sects with varying allegiances. They loathe their night elf kin above all else, and most of them remain devoted servants of the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowConflictsOfAz.JournalEntryPage.mOeoKWAu3OOx8LP9]{Burning Legion}. A few, though, have followed Xavius’s example and turned to the worship of the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowConflictsOfAz.JournalEntryPage.QX2LRHkL98AMmC55]{Old Gods}.

Shivarra.name: Shivarra
Shivarra.text:
Bigger isn’t always better, and I don’t know that six arms are any better than two. Sometimes they’re just nastier.

—Chromie

Towering Priest of the Burning Legion

Habitat: Planar (Twisting Nether); Treasure: Individual

Devout and exceedingly charismatic, shivarra are demonic priests who shared the news of Sargeras’s dread and powerful vision. They are the driving heart of the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowConflictsOfAz.JournalEntryPage.mOeoKWAu3OOx8LP9]{Burning Crusade}.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowShivarraP00zc statblock caption=false classes="double-column hide-in-embed"]

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.P3A8MameG8Fjjs6C caption=false classes="noborder"]

Sylvanas Windrunner.name: Sylvanas Windrunner
Sylvanas Windrunner.text:
Vengeful Banshee

The thirst for vengeance festers within the shadowy heart of Sylvanas Windrunner, the Banshee Queen. Her hatred is first for the @UUID[.HtscVm1fdlzer43M]{Lich King}, Arthas Menethil, who slew her and bound her soul into eternal servitude, then for the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowConflictsOfAz.JournalEntryPage.YRwQ3wrLM22odUUP]{Scourge} who slaughtered her people. And last, for all the living.

The Dark Lady of the Forsaken has committed terrible atrocities in the name of revenge. Her cruelty grew after the Lich King’s demise, as she fell further into nihilistic despair. Hundreds of thousands of people died on her orders and were raised as her undead soldiers. Ultimately, she repented and accepted judgment for her evils and now dwells within the Shadowlands, freeing souls as eternal penance.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.1nDwS0Q5wCBmVAbY caption=false classes="margin-center noborder"]

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowSylvanasWinqT statblock caption=false classes="double-column hide-in-embed"]

Thrall.name: Thrall
Thrall.text:
Liberator of the Orcs and Guardian of the Elements

Thrall is a great example of how you can’t let other people define you.

—Chromie

The first orc to be born on Azeroth after @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowTheHorde00000]{the Horde} invaded through the Dark Portal, Thrall was an orphan of the First War and grew up in an orc internment camp. His hard life has made him stern but kind. As a leader and a shaman, he teaches his people to pursue coexistence over conflict, with both the other peoples of Azeroth and the wild elements that govern the world.

After many battles, Thrall retired to Outland to live a simple life away from war. In time, Thrall’s old friends reminded of his duty to his people, and he joined the Horde Council. He wields Dra’gora, an axe he forged in his seclusion—for even then, he knew he would one day return to defend his people.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowThrallGZRj1Vq statblock caption=false classes="double-column hide-in-embed"]

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.JWCsbvQYkpXdNaFA caption=false classes="noborder"]

Voidwalkers.name: Voidwalkers
Voidwalkers.text:
@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.4SVRNqTDE2RGcQsh caption=false classes="float-right size-three noborder"]

Creatures of Incarnate Void

Habitat: Planar (Twisting Nether); Treasure: None

Voidwalkers are creatures of the Void, hulking figures made of pure shadow in hues of black, purple, and blue with glowing violet eyes. They are often adorned with bracers or pauldrons.

Black Dragonflight Whelp.name: Black Dragonflight Whelp
Black Dragonflight Whelp.text:
Black dragonflight whelps are murderous little creatures that dwell near volcanoes, hot springs, and geysers. They smother prey in their magma breath and pick the meat from the globs of scalding lava.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowBlackDragonpP statblock caption=false classes="hide-in-embed"]

Black Dragonflight Drake.name: Black Dragonflight Drake
Black Dragonflight Drake.text:
Black dragonflight drakes use their magic to heat objects made of earth or stone. They can momentarily melt stone into magma and reshape it before it cools. These drakes delight in stalking and disorienting prey.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowBlackDragonzH statblock caption=false classes="hide-in-embed"]

Black Dragonflight Dragon.name: Black Dragonflight Dragon
Black Dragonflight Dragon.text:
Fully matured black dragonflight dragons terrorize the lands of Azeroth from the skies and manipulate society by shape-shifting into humanoid disguises. A black dragon wearing a mortal visage usually has jet-black hair and red eyes.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowBlackDragonf7 statblock caption=false classes="double-column hide-in-embed"]

Blue Dragonflight Whelp.name: Blue Dragonflight Whelp
Blue Dragonflight Whelp.text:
Blue dragonflight whelps display uncanny intelligence for their age. Rather than attacking an ice fisher, a blue whelp might ask to pool their knowledge, striking a deal to share the fish they catch.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowBlueDragonfXY statblock caption=false classes="hide-in-embed"]

Blue Dragonflight Drake.name: Blue Dragonflight Drake
Blue Dragonflight Drake.text:
Members of the blue dragonflight are devoted students of the arcane arts. Blue dragonflight drakes learn to create and dispel magical effects, protecting their secrets from prying mages.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowBlueDragonfdr statblock caption=false classes="hide-in-embed"]

Blue Dragonflight Dragon.name: Blue Dragonflight Dragon
Blue Dragonflight Dragon.text:
Blue dragonflight dragons view themselves as stewards of the arcane, and they disdain mortals who misuse their gifts. Noble blue dragons take the role of sagely mentors to mortal mages—for example, Kalecgos long worked with the Kirin Tor in a mortal visage. Cruel and jealous blue dragons such as Cyanigosa try to dominate and punish mortals for their misuse of magic.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowBlueDragonfwR statblock caption=false classes="double-column hide-in-embed"]

Bronze Dragonflight Whelp.name: Bronze Dragonflight Whelp
Bronze Dragonflight Whelp.text:
Bronze dragonflight whelps are patient. They stand still for hours on end in the middle of the desert, waiting for prey to pass before striking out with maw or claw. Many travelers mistake these whelps for statues.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowBronzeDrago7R statblock caption=false classes="hide-in-embed"]

Bronze Dragonflight Dragon.name: Bronze Dragonflight Dragon
Bronze Dragonflight Dragon.text:
Mature bronze dragons task themselves with maintaining the one true timeline of Azeroth. They keep close to humanoid civilizations, watching for travelers from other timelines or those who seek to alter the timeways.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowBronzeDragoHk statblock caption=false classes="double-column hide-in-embed"]

Bronze Dragonflight Drake.name: Bronze Dragonflight Drake
Bronze Dragonflight Drake.text:
Many a villain has tried to bend a bronze dragonflight drake to their will, hoping to take advantage of the creature’s prophetic magic while the drake is still young. Such opportunists quickly learn the error of their ways when the bronze drake shreds and sears their skin with its red-hot sand breath.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowBronzeDragoLa statblock caption=false classes="hide-in-embed"]

Furbolg Totemic.name: Furbolg Totemic
Furbolg Totemic.text:
Furbolg totemics are shaman who use totems for healing and offense.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowFurbolgTote8y statblock caption=false classes="double-column hide-in-embed"]

Furbolg Ursa.name: Furbolg Ursa
Furbolg Ursa.text:
Ursas are warrior leaders in furbolg tribes, larger than their kin and empowered by elemental magic.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowFurbolgUrsaCk statblock caption=false classes="hide-in-embed"]

Green Dragonflight Whelp.name: Green Dragonflight Whelp
Green Dragonflight Whelp.text:
Members of the green dragonflight raise their whelps in the Emerald Dream whenever possible. There, a whelp learns to appreciate and spread the beauty of nature in all its forms by observing cycles of birth and death.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowGreenDragonKP statblock caption=false classes="hide-in-embed"]

Green Dragonflight Drake.name: Green Dragonflight Drake
Green Dragonflight Drake.text:
Emerging from the Emerald Dream, green dragon­flight drakes are wise enough to take action in Azeroth. They often ally with older dragons, night elf druids, and ancients of lore to eliminate evil cults and invading demons with nature magic.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowDrakeGreenDDs statblock caption=false classes="hide-in-embed"]

Green Dragonflight Dragon.name: Green Dragonflight Dragon
Green Dragonflight Dragon.text:
The mightiest of the green dragonflight battle the minions of the Old Gods and shape-shift into mortal visage forms to ally with humanoids. This battle against the Old Gods puts green dragons at risk for corruption by the Emerald Nightmare, which was created by one of the Old Gods’ greatest champions.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowDragonGreentj statblock caption=false classes="double-column hide-in-embed"]

Murloc Forager.name: Murloc Forager
Murloc Forager.text:
Murloc foragers live near the edges of bodies of water, spending most of their time searching for food in the mud and shallow waters. Of all murlocs, foragers are the most likely to be found outside of a group, and they often serve as an early warning system to their community, drawing would-be attackers to the water’s edge for their fellow murlocs to ambush.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowMurlocForagnO statblock caption=false classes="hide-in-embed"]

Murloc Oracle.name: Murloc Oracle
Murloc Oracle.text:
Oracles lead groups of other murlocs, using magic to defend and heal their allies. Murloc oracles are more willing than other murlocs to attempt communication with those who don’t speak Nerglish.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowMurlocOraclQJ statblock caption=false classes="double-column hide-in-embed"]

Furbolgs, Murlocs, and Quilboar

In addition to the stat blocks presented in this chapter, any of the Humanoid stat blocks in the Monster Manual can be furbolgs, murlocs, or quilboar. For murlocs, add a Swim Speed equal to the creature’s Speed plus 10 feet and the Amphibious trait from the stat blocks here.
