Naga Myrmidon.name: Naga Myrmidon
Naga Myrmidon.text:
Myrmidons are hulking male naga who serve as front-line warriors in battles against the naga’s enemies. They wield tridents with attached ropes that allow them to pull foes into melee range.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowNagaMyrmidobm statblock caption=false classes="double-column hide-in-embed"]

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.tK7UKhrMzHpg0hiD caption=false classes="noborder"]

Naga Sea Witch.name: Naga Sea Witch
Naga Sea Witch.text:
Sea witches are female naga who wield the magic of stormy seas.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowNagaSeaWitctF statblock caption=false classes="hide-in-embed"]

Naga Siren.name: Naga Siren
Naga Siren.text:
Sirens are among the most powerful naga spellcasters, channeling the cold of the marine depths into mighty frost magic.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.oi0D6HsOt7SQsjrZ caption=false classes="margin-center noborder"]

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowNagaSireng7YN statblock caption=false classes="hide-in-embed"]

Nerubian Warrior.name: Nerubian Warrior
Nerubian Warrior.text:
Nerubian warriors use their arachnid limbs to quickly scurry across the ground and climb onto walls and ceilings, maintaining their balance even in treacherous terrain. When attacking, they use the two arms on their humanoid torso to claw at their enemies, and these warriors often rely on their webbing to encase or restrict their foes, leaving them motionless and helpless.

The few nerubians who survived the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowConflictsOfAz.JournalEntryPage.YRwQ3wrLM22odUUP]{Scourge} have organized a rebellion called the Azjol-anak to retake @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowAzjolnerub000]{Azjol-Nerub}. Their bitterness over the loss of their kingdom has made many distrustful of anyone who isn’t nerubian, and they attack whoever they come across without restraint or warning.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowNerubianWarfV statblock caption=false classes="double-column hide-in-embed"]

Nerubian Venomancer.name: Nerubian Venomancer
Nerubian Venomancer.text:
Nerubian venomancers use their lethal toxin as one of their primary weapons. Venomancers’ mastery of poison extends to their webbing, which is toxic to those held within its grasp. Venomancers are quick to assault non-nerubians, driven by their rancor over their lost and scattered kingdom.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowNerubianVen2W statblock caption=false classes="double-column hide-in-embed"]

Nerubian Crypt Fiend.name: Nerubian Crypt Fiend
Nerubian Crypt Fiend.text:
Though the Lich King couldn’t infect the nerubians with his plague of undeath, he raised many dead nerubians using necromancy, turning them into crypt fiends. Crypt fiends wear the remnants of the cloth that they were mummified in and rake at their foes with their powerful claws. Crypt fiends use their webs to incapacitate their enemies, whose life force is sapped by the powerful necrotic energy in the webs’ strands.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowNerubianCryYE statblock caption=false classes="double-column hide-in-embed"]

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.JYGAcRD5P3SCpTfG caption=false classes="noborder"]

Quilboar Thornweaver.name: Quilboar Thornweaver
Quilboar Thornweaver.text:
Quilboar thornweavers bear thorns they believe grew from the body of their demigod progenitor Agamaggan. Their magic uses those thorns, calling on the spirits of nature to protect their territory.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowQuilboarThoNL statblock caption=false classes="double-column hide-in-embed"]

Ragnaros’s Lair.name: Ragnaros’s Lair
Ragnaros’s Lair.text:
Ragnaros transforms any place he dwells into an echo of the Plane of Fire. Rock melts into pools and streams of lava, flames dance through the air, and toxic smoke bursts from vents in the ground.

The region surrounding Ragnaros’s lair is scarred and scorched, creating the following effects:

Extreme Heat. Temperatures within 1 mile of the lair are comparable to a scorching desert, subjecting creatures to @UUID[Compendium.dnd-dungeon-masters-guide.content.JournalEntry.dmgDmsToolbox000.JournalEntryPage.xgLA30rErlkjIPAK#extreme-heat]{extreme heat} (see the Dungeon Master’s Guide).

Sulfurous Vapors. Toxic gases seep up from the ground within 1 mile of the lair. A creature that finishes a Long Rest in that area must succeed on a [[/save 15 con]] saving throw or have the &Reference[Poisoned] condition for 1 hour.

These effects are permanent scars left on the terrain by Ragnaros’s presence.

Red Dragonflight Whelp.name: Red Dragonflight Whelp
Red Dragonflight Whelp.text:
Although red dragonflight whelps are small, their fiery breath is mighty. These creatures’ sense of justice leads them to take on larger foes in the name of good. Red dragonflight whelps almost never flee from a fight, for their pride hasn’t yet been tempered by the wisdom of age.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowRedDragonfl8O statblock caption=false classes="hide-in-embed"]

Red Dragonflight Drake.name: Red Dragonflight Drake
Red Dragonflight Drake.text:
Red dragonflight drakes heal tainted lands across Azeroth. By breathing streams of blazing fire across the terrain, these drakes incinerate withered plant life and bring growth from the ashes. When need is greatest, these drakes allow mortal heroes to ride and fight on their backs.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowRedDragonflmH statblock caption=false classes="hide-in-embed"]

Red Dragonflight Dragon.name: Red Dragonflight Dragon
Red Dragonflight Dragon.text:
Members of the red dragonflight are considered the most noble dragons of Azeroth, sworn to protect all life. But their benevolence should never be misunderstood as weakness; they are capable of terrible destruction, outweighed only by the life-giving power that suffuses their fiery breath.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowRedDragonfl0G statblock caption=false classes="double-column hide-in-embed"]

Felsworn Satyr.name: Felsworn Satyr
Felsworn Satyr.text:
Felsworn satyrs wield the fiery power of the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowConflictsOfAz.JournalEntryPage.mOeoKWAu3OOx8LP9]{Burning Legion} as its devoted agents. They are fierce enemies of night elves, using their magic to devastate night elf communities.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowFelswornSatn1 statblock caption=false classes="hide-in-embed"]

Shadowstalker Satyr.name: Shadowstalker Satyr
Shadowstalker Satyr.text:
Shadowstalkers are satyrs who wield the subtle magic of @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowTheWorldOfWar.JournalEntryPage.39WbPfMoJEVvbg15]{the Void}, using that power to lurk in the darkness and strike enemies from hiding.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowShadowstalkXv statblock caption=false classes="hide-in-embed"]

Voidwalker.name: Voidwalker
Voidwalker.text:
Warlocks highly prize ordinary voidwalkers as servants because of their ability to both attract and withstand enemy attacks.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowVoidwalkerBzr statblock caption=false classes="hide-in-embed"]

Voidcaller.name: Voidcaller
Voidcaller.text:
Voidcallers are magic-wielding voidwalkers that appear to be draped in rotting cloth. From their shoulders hang two lanterns, which are said to bridge the realm of the living and that of the dead and sometimes attract wayward ghosts. The lanterns hang from a glowing crystalline structure that hovers over and around the voidcaller’s shadowy form.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowVoidcaller4Qq statblock caption=false classes="hide-in-embed"]

N'raqi.name: N'raqi
N'raqi.text:
@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.c8ZWRR8qkCFaajss caption=false classes="noborder"]

Faceless Emissaries of the Old Gods

Habitat: Any; Treasure: Individual

I’ve seen both a past and a possible future with the Old Gods in charge and faceless ones everywhere. That was enough for me.

—Chromie

After the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowConflictsOfAz.JournalEntryPage.QX2LRHkL98AMmC55]{Old Gods} embedded themselves deep within Azeroth, their inky essence slowly seeped from their bodies, eventually coalescing into the n’raqi. Also called the Faceless, n’raqi dwell in shadows and cast eldritch spells in the dread tongue of Shath’Yar from tentacle-draped mouths. They are unflinchingly loyal heralds of the cosmic evils to whom they owe their existence. Whether they are marshalling the Old Gods’ followers into armies, aiding cults, or doing the Old Gods’ personal bidding, n’raqi are intelligent, dangerous, and powerful.

Lesser n’raqi called k’thir lurk in the shadows, often disguised as humans, and manipulate mortals’ minds. These n’raqi use the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-monster-manual.actors.Actor.mmMindFlayer0000]{Mind Flayer} stat block from the Monster Manual, and they speak Shath’Yar.

N'raqi Faceless One.name: N'raqi Faceless One
N'raqi Faceless One.text:
The most common n’raqi, faceless ones telepathically communicate with nearby creatures. Whispering into the minds of those around them, they become like gods to the weak minded and invaluable tools to those blessed with otherworldly insight. They attack both through their minds and with the strength of their two pseudopods, one of which is always much larger and more fully formed than the other.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowNraqiFaceleeQ statblock caption=false classes="double-column hide-in-embed"]

N'raqi Faceless General.name: N'raqi Faceless General
N'raqi Faceless General.text:
Faceless generals, also called C’Thraxxi, lead the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowConflictsOfAz.JournalEntryPage.QX2LRHkL98AMmC55]{Old Gods’} armies and defend their strongholds. Each C’Thrax has a deep well of magical ability, which it deploys to rip through the minds of those who get in its way, often leaving nothing more than drained husks in its wake. Even death is not a final end for these harbingers of doom; cultists have often tried, sometimes successfully, to awaken long-dead C’Thraxxi through sinister rituals and offerings of blood.

A faceless general’s hulking form is covered in chitinous plates. Both its arms end in heavy pincers, and crablike legs sprout from its back, almost resembling wings. Each individual C’Thrax has its own unique characteristics, often reflective of the particular Old God it serves. For example, the Fury of N’Zoth has many eyes on its head and upper body, much like the Old God N’Zoth, while Warbringer Yenajz, drawn to Kul Tiras by the corruption of the Tidesages, has a mantle of teeth around its head that suggests the maw of C’Thun.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowNraqiFacelemp statblock caption=false classes="double-column hide-in-embed"]

Beyond Azeroth.name: Beyond Azeroth
Beyond Azeroth.text:
Not all adventures that begin on Azeroth stay on Azeroth. Explorers, soldiers, archaeologists, and treasure hunters of particular skill—or particular misfortune—sometimes find themselves thrust beyond the existence they know to other realms and planes.

World of Warcraft has brought adventurers to other worlds beyond Azeroth. The world of Draenor, the birthplace of orcs and ogres, was shattered after the Second War, leaving only the broken realm of Outland drifting like flotsam in the Twisting Nether. The world of K’aresh, home of the ethereals, was all but destroyed by the void lord Dimensius and is similarly broken. Argus, the original home world of the eredar, became the stronghold of the Burning Legion.

Adventurers have also visited other planes of existence. The Elemental Plane was constructed after the ancient war between the keepers and the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowConflictsOfAz.JournalEntryPage.QX2LRHkL98AMmC55]{Old Gods} as a dimensional prison to hold the elemental lords and their servants. The Emerald Dream represents the untouched natural world of Azeroth. And the Shadowlands are the realms of the dead.

Overview.name: Overview
Overview.text:
@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.Xrk1r58rGjX7dn9v caption=false classes="noborder"]

For Level 5–10 Characters • The Old Gods

The ruins of Lathar’Lazal have become a nest of evil. Once a temple of Elune on Ashenvale’s rain-drenched west coast, it has been defiled by the Twilight’s Hammer, worshippers of the Old Gods. They were drawn to the ruin by a slithering scion of their slumbering masters: Aku’mai the Devourer.

To protect this burgeoning evil power, the cultists have allied with the naga and murlocs who occupy this ruin, threatening both the Alliance and the Horde.

Blackfathom Deeps Areas.name: Blackfathom Deeps Areas
Blackfathom Deeps Areas.text:
The characters will likely travel through the following areas of Blackfathom Deeps in the listed order.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.3hZZfcMErG4Z9p8w classes="noborder"]

Blackfathom Deeps Adventures.name: Blackfathom Deeps Adventures
Blackfathom Deeps Adventures.text:
Use the suggestions in the Blackfathom Deeps Adventure Hooks table to draw adventurers there.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.tables.RollTable.wowBlackfathomcS caption=false rangeLabel="1d4" resultLabel="Adventure Hook" rollable nameStyle="h4" no-toc]

Treasure.name: Treasure
Treasure.text:
When the characters overcome an encounter, roll [[/r 2d6]] on the Blackfathom Deeps Treasure table. When they defeat a boss listed below, roll 4d6 or choose a treasure labeled with the boss’s name.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.tables.RollTable.wowBlackfathomol caption=false rangeLabel="4d6" resultLabel="Treasure" rollable nameStyle="h4" no-toc]

Blackfathom Deeps Characters.name: Blackfathom Deeps Characters
Blackfathom Deeps Characters.text: The leaders of multiple factions of villains lurk within this corrupted grotto. They’re listed in the order they’re most likely encountered.

Sample Encounters.name: Sample Encounters
Sample Encounters.text:
Use the Blackfathom Deeps Encounters table to help craft planned encounters for key locations within each area of the dungeon. You can also roll on the table if characters make enough noise in the dungeon to attract guards from nearby areas to investigate.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.tables.RollTable.wowBlackfathom2Q caption=false rangeLabel="1d20" resultLabel="Encounter" rollable nameStyle="h4" no-toc]

Ghamoo-Ra.name: Ghamoo-Ra
Ghamoo-Ra.text:
“Grrrooooooooakk!”

When the Twilight’s Hammer cult took over Blackfathom, its followers tormented a snapjaw for years until it became vicious. Naming the beast Ghamoo-Ra, the cultists trained it to defend their shrine. If attacked from beyond its island, it pursues its attackers to the edge of the Pool of Ask’ar area, then retreats into the water and takes a Short Rest.

Lady Sarevess.name: Lady Sarevess
Lady Sarevess.text:
“Armed and unbound? My servants have failed, then. No matter, a lively death will please my masters greatly!”

Lady Sarevess is a self-proclaimed student of Queen Azshara, who created the naga long ago through a pact with the Old God N’Zoth. Lady Sarevess is obsessed with re-creating Queen Azshara’s communion with the Old Gods. Sarevess disdains the Twilight’s Hammer but lends them her strength and the might of her naga warriors so she can plunder the cultists’ arcane lore.

Gelihast.name: Gelihast
Gelihast.text:
“Mrr? Mrr! Mrrrglglglgl!!”

The Old Gods called, and Gelihast answered, forcing his way into Blackfathom Deeps and slaughtering nearly a dozen surprised Twilight’s Hammer cultists. Impressed by his brutality, the cult allowed him to stay, and he built his own shrine to offer sacrifices to the ominous presence in the temple ruins.

Gelihast’s Blindlight murlocs think they control this cave, unaware that the Twilight’s Hammer tolerates them only so long as they deter invaders.

Twilight Lord Kelris.name: Twilight Lord Kelris
Twilight Lord Kelris.text:
“Who dares disturb my meditation? I could all but hear the fathomless dreams of Aku’mai.”

An orc shaman-turned-warlock named Kelris Doomfang found a three-headed monster in Blackfathom Deeps, Aku’mai, while fleeing justice. He became convinced it was a herald of the Old Gods’ return to Azeroth and was determined to control it. Kelris gathered a sect of the Twilight’s Hammer to the depths, and he supervises the monster’s growth, feeding it his own subjects to satisfy its wild hunger.

Aku’mai.name: Aku’mai
Aku’mai.text:
@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.wQo3KnuyTETDk2gX caption=false classes="sepia" classes="noborder"]

This three-headed ancient evil carries within it a seed of the Old Gods’ power. Lady Sarevess believes it is the spawn of N’Zoth and a key to opening his nightmare realm of Ny’alotha. Aku’mai is feared by all for its relentless savagery and insatiable hunger—but the wise fear it because all who look on it hear the whispers of the Old Gods.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowAkumaipHWGdqQ statblock caption=false classes="double-column hide-in-embed"]

Drowned Sacellum.name: Drowned Sacellum
Drowned Sacellum.text: This half-flooded grotto is filled with crumbling kaldorei ruins. Characters who touch the water alert murlocs of the Blindlight tribe lurking below the surface, which rush to begin combat.

Pool of Ask’ar.name: Pool of Ask’ar
Pool of Ask’ar.text:
Naga warriors patrol the waters of this pool, always alert for aquatic invaders.

Central Island. @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowGhamooRaGHNKc]{Ghamoo-Ra} (see “Blackfathom Deeps Characters” below) attacks any intruders on this island. When Ghamoo-Ra attacks, two @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowNagaMyrmidobm]{Naga Myrmidons} (see chapter 7) come to investigate from 30 feet away. If a character enters the water while fighting Ghamoo-Ra, there is a 50 percent chance each round the disturbance attracts another Naga Myrmidon.

North Cavern. The naga witch @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowLadySarevesNC]{Lady Sarevess} (see “Blackfathom Deeps Characters” below) conducts rituals at her bone-strewn altar, guarded by two Naga Myrmidons (see chapter 7).

South Cavern. Night elf Sentinels Aluwyn and Relwyn Shadestar and trainee Issara are tied up here to be sacrificed on Sarevess’s altar, guarded by a @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowNagaSireng7YN]{Naga Siren} and a @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowNagaMyrmidobm]{Naga Myrmidon} (see chapter 7).

Blindlight Grotto.name: Blindlight Grotto
Blindlight Grotto.text:
Murlocs and naga patrol the Blindlight Grotto, kept in tenuous peace by their alliance with the Twilight’s Hammer. The northernmost cave is the lair of Gelihast (see “Blackfathom Deeps Characters”) and ten Murloc Foragers (see chapter 7) who attend him. If Gelihast is slain here, his altar to the Old Gods reacts to this tribute, giving each character a Charm of Heroism (see the Dungeon Master’s Guide).

About Blackfathom Deeps

Blackfathom Deeps is a classic dungeon from the original World of Warcraft, originally designed for five characters of moderate level. In its first incarnation and as presented in this chapter, the dungeon focuses on the naga’s budding alliance with the Twilight’s Hammer cult.

After the Cataclysm, a new Twilight’s Hammer leader came to Blackfathom, fed Twilight Lord Kelris to Aku’mai, and displaced most of the naga. In this era, the dungeon is populated with @UUID[Compendium.dnd-monster-manual.actors.Actor.mmCultistFanatic]{Cult Fanatics}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-monster-manual.actors.Actor.mmElementalCulti]{Elemental Cultists}, and @UUID[Compendium.dnd-monster-manual.actors.Actor.mmWaterElemental]{Water Elementals}, though the Blindlight murlocs are still numerous. Ghamoo-Ra remains in the ruins, stubbornly resisting the Twilight’s Hammer’s attempts to turn the turtle into a weapon. The other dungeon bosses include these key characters:

Domina is a Forsaken Cultist Hierophant with the Undead type. She sacrificed Sarevess to Aku’mai after the naga failed to protect the cult’s operations and now occupies Sarevess’s cave.

Executioner Gore is an orc Gladiator who specializes in dragging screaming innocents to the altar for sacrifice to Aku’mai. He lurks in the Moonshrine Ruins and might come to Thruk’s aid if combat breaks out near the entrance.

Subjugator Kor’ul is a n’raqi (Mind Flayer) that was charged with bringing Blackfathom Deeps under the cult’s firm control. Kor’ul slew Gelihast first, and the murlocs in Blindlight Grotto are now under Kor’ul’s command.

Thruk is an ogre lord (Hill Giant) who is focused on killing the Guardian of the Deep and claiming its treasure. The Guardian of the Deep is a monstrous crab (Chuul) that displaced Old Serra’kis from the cave beneath the Moonshrine Sanctum. Thruk is most often encountered near the entrance to the Moonshrine Ruins, trying to lure the crab out of the depths.

Twilight Lord Bathiel was once mortal, but the power of the Old Gods transformed him into an elemental ascendant (use the Marid stat block; Bathiel doesn’t have access to Wish).

Moonshrine Ruins.name: Moonshrine Ruins
Moonshrine Ruins.text:
Once-majestic bridges stretch over a vast pool toward a ruined moonwell, the centerpiece of this former temple to Elune. Members of the Twilight’s Hammer patrol the entrance to their inner sanctum.

An underwater cave lies hidden under the platform leading into the Moonshrine Sanctum. A huge threshadon called Old Serra’kis, a creature similar to a plesiosaurus (use the Giant Shark stat block), lurks in that cave and rarely emerges.

Moonshrine Sanctum.name: Moonshrine Sanctum
Moonshrine Sanctum.text:
When the naga took over the Moonshrine Sanctum, they erected a statue of Queen Azshara; when the Twilight’s Hammer seized the temple, the cultists kept the statue, for Azshara communed with the Old Gods. Twilight Lord Kelris (see “Blackfathom Deeps Characters” below) makes sacrifices on an altar here, then offers the bodies to Aku’mai.

Lair Doors. Behind the altar are stone doors that open when all four braziers are lit (see below).

Ritual Braziers. Twilight Lord Kelris’s rituals corrupt the elements with the power of the Void. Four ritual braziers at the corners of the altar must be lit to open Aku’mai’s door. On Initiative count 20 of each round of combat with Kelris, one of these braziers lights with purple flame, summoning Kelris’s allies in unoccupied spaces within 20 feet of the altar, split between the east and west sides of the area:

First Flame: Eight makrura (Giant Crabs)

Second Flame: One snapjaw (Archelon)

Third Flame: Eight makrura (Giant Crabs)

Fourth Flame: Two Water Elementals

Once all four braziers are lit, the doors open. If Kelris dies before they are all lit, the characters can light them without summoning any more creatures.

Aku’mai’s Lair.name: Aku’mai’s Lair
Aku’mai’s Lair.text: A dank cavern filled with the bones of countless sacrifices leads to an inky pool where Aku’mai (see “Blackfathom Deeps Characters” below) awaits fresh tribute.

Introduction.name: Introduction
Introduction.text:
Named for Cenarius—the demigod who trained Malfurion Stormrage, the first druid—the Cenarion Circle is a worldwide order keeping watch over Azeroth’s druids and protecting the natural balance. Since the end of the Third War, the circle has accepted druids from both the Alliance and the Horde, reflecting a generally Neutral alignment. In the druidic sanctuary of Moonglade, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowElf0000000000.JournalEntryPage.C4fRQxnWgEHPPK1W]{night elf} and @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowTauren0000000]{tauren} druids live and work in harmony, and in recent years, druids from other peoples—Kul Tiran @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowHuman00000000]{humans}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowWorgen0000000]{worgen}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowTroll00000000]{trolls}, and even @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowHaranir000000]{haranir}—have joined the ranks of the Cenarion Circle. The order is still led by Cenarius himself, with the involvement of Malfurion and the tauren druid Hamuul Runetotem.

There’s no time like the present to start saving the future!

—Chromie

The Cenarion Circle is most active in Kalimdor. Besides Moonglade, which is inaccessible to anyone but circle members, the order also has a base in Desolace (Karnum’s Glade). It has launched expeditions into Silithus, the Plaguelands, and Outland, and its members are on the forefront of any effort to preserve, protect, or restore nature.

Adopting the Druid class, either at character creation or through multiclassing, increases a character’s Renown Score with the Cenarion Circle by 3.

Cenarion Circle Renown Perks.name: Cenarion Circle Renown Perks
Cenarion Circle Renown Perks.text:
Increasing your Renown Score with the Cenarion Circle gives you the following additional benefits.

Cenarion Circle: Friendly

Prerequisite: Renown 3+ with the Cenarion Circle

You can spend 30 days with a trainer to learn Druidic or gain proficiency in Nature (see the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowTheAlliance00.JournalEntryPage.atJHGssGcTvG0dWQ]{Training} sidebar earlier in this chapter).

Cenarion Circle: Honored

Prerequisite: Renown 10+ with the Cenarion Circle

If you spend a Long Rest in a Cenarion Circle sanctuary, you gain the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-dungeon-masters-guide.equipment.Item.dmgCharmOfRestor]{Charm of Restoration} (see the Dungeon Master’s Guide).

Cenarion Circle: Revered

Prerequisite: Renown 25+ with the Cenarion Circle

You receive the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.items.Item.wowWildguardBles]{Wildguard Blessing}. This Blessing gives you Advantage on saving throws against spells. You lose the Blessing if your Renown Score with the Cenarion Circle falls below 25.

Cenarion Circle: Exalted

Prerequisite: Renown 50+ with the Cenarion Circle

You carry the title Guardian of Cenarius. For a cost of 2,000 GP, you can purchase a Cenarion war hippogryph mount (@UUID[Compendium.dnd-monster-manual.actors.Actor.mmHippogriff0000]{Hippogriff}). If your Renown Score falls below 50, you lose the title, and your mount no longer obeys your commands.

Introduction.name: Introduction
Introduction.text:
@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.YILZPG1iMivd4VN2 class="noborder"]

Creating a character for a game using this book begins with choosing a class. World of Warcraft offers thirteen classes, each with a variety of specializations. Each class and specialization maps to certain choices of features from the Player’s Handbook plus new options in this book. Three sidebars in the next few pages—@UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowDeathKnight00.JournalEntryPage.gL82O0Vn607HF94R#hero-classes]{Hero Classes}, “Specialization,” and “Other Class Options”—provide more general information.

World of Warcraft Classes.name: World of Warcraft Classes
World of Warcraft Classes.text:
The thirteen World of Warcraft classes described in this book are summarized below:

@UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowDeathKnight00]{Death Knight}. Straddling the line between life and death, death knights emphasize debilitating curses and sinister magic.

@UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowDemonHunter00]{Demon Hunter}. Demon hunters are haunted outcasts who wield fel magic.

@UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowDruid00000000]{Druid}. Druids are shape-shifters with an affinity for plants, animals, and the magic of nature.

@UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowEvoker0000000]{Evoker}. Evokers unleash devastating draconic spells on enemies and healing magic on allies.

@UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowHunter0000000]{Hunter}. Hunters are at home in the wilderness and have a special connection with beasts. Hunters rely on weaponry and pets to deal damage.

@UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowMage000000000]{Mage}. Mages are magic-users who learn their craft through intense research and study. They wield a potent array of offensive and defensive spells.

@UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowMonk000000000]{Monk}. Monks are known for their skill in hand-to-hand fighting, including unarmed combat.

@UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowPaladin000000]{Paladin}. Paladins are heavily armored defenders whose holy magic heals wounds and combats evil.

@UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowPriest0000000]{Priest}. Priests express their faith by serving the people as healers and champions.

@UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowRogue00000000]{Rogue}. Rogues sneak around enemies and attack while hiding to finish foes quickly.

@UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowShaman0000000]{Shaman}. Shaman wield elemental magic against their foes.

@UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowWarlock000000]{Warlock}. Warlocks wield demonic magic, including summoned demons, to curse and immolate foes.

@UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowWarrior000000]{Warrior}. Warriors are heavily armored fighters who strive for perfection in combat.

Introduction.name: Introduction
Introduction.text:
@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.qtvS8lUQUmsRHJuc classes="noborder"]

Many different peoples call @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowWorldOfAzerot]{Azeroth} home. Some are native to its lands, while others have settled there from far-flung worlds. Most of these peoples have aligned themselves with either @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowTheAlliance00]{the Alliance} or @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowTheHorde00000]{the Horde}.

When you make a character to adventure on Azeroth, choose a background from the Player’s Handbook, then choose one of the species described in this chapter. Your choice of species might also give you a starting Renown Score with one of Azeroth’s @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowFactionsAndRe]{factions}.

Species

  • @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowDracthyr00000]{Dracthyr}

  • @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowDraenei000000]{Draenei}

  • @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowDwarf00000000]{Dwarf}

  • @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowEarthen000000]{Earthen}

  • @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowElf0000000000]{Elf}

  • @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowForsaken00000]{Forsaken}

  • @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowGnome00000000]{Gnome}

Languages.name: Languages
Languages.text:
When choosing languages for a character in a World of Warcraft campaign, use the tables here instead of the ones in the Player’s Handbook. Your character knows either Common (if they belong to @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowTheAlliance00]{the Alliance}) or Orcish (if they belong to @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowTheHorde00000]{the Horde}), plus two languages you roll or choose from the appropriate table—@UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.tables.RollTable.wowAllianceLany4]{Alliance Languages} or @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.tables.RollTable.wowHordeLanguaR4]{Horde Languages}. If the origin you choose isn’t affiliated with either faction, you can choose your three starting languages from either table. (At least one of the common languages of the Alliance and the Horde—Common or Orcish—is recommended.)

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.tables.RollTable.wowAllianceLany4 caption=false rangeLabel="1d12" resultLabel="Language/Origin" rollable nameStyle="h4" no-toc]

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.tables.RollTable.wowHordeLanguaR4 caption=false rangeLabel="1d12" resultLabel="Language/Origin" rollable nameStyle="h4" no-toc]

The Rare Languages table lists languages that are either secret or derived from other planes of existence and thus less widespread on @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowWorldOfAzerot]{Azeroth}. Some features let a character learn a rare language.

The First Ones, the enigmatic architects of the entire cosmos, left fragments of language that are akin to mathematics and largely incomprehensible to mortals. Kalimag, the language of elementals, is equivalent to Primordial in D&D, and Shath’Yar, the language of the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowConflictsOfAz.JournalEntryPage.QX2LRHkL98AMmC55]{Old Gods}, is equivalent to Deep Speech.
