Overview.name: Overview
Overview.text:
@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.3OrOFmh3qpcOe5MQ caption=false classes="float-right size-four noborder"]

For Level 1–4 Characters • Alliance Versus Horde

Deep within the Deadmines, the Defias Brotherhood plots Stormwind’s downfall. These tunnels wind beneath the gold-mining town of Moonbrook in Stormwind’s border province of Westfall. Amid the chaos of the First War, the mines were occupied by orcs and ogres, then were abandoned for years until the Defias Brotherhood arrived.

The Defias Brotherhood was once the Stonemasons Guild of Stormwind, which rebuilt the city after it was razed by the Horde in the First War. The guild was a symbol of hope among the common folk. But when the corrupt nobles of Stormwind refused to pay them for years of labor, the guild started a riot that swiftly turned bloody. In the chaos, Queen Tiffin Wrynn was slain by a stray stone, and the bereaved King Varian outlawed the guild.

Edwin VanCleef, the guild’s leader, tied a red bandanna over his mouth—a symbol of the innocent blood shed by corrupt nobility—and swore to raze the city. He forged the ragtag guild into the Defias Brotherhood, and his vow of vengeance against the nobility devolved into a reign of terror. He and his followers allied with gnolls and extorted the common folk to fund a weapon to destroy Stormwind City: a Juggernaut battleship being constructed in secret in the Deadmines. VanCleef’s red-masked thugs coordinate kidnappings, smugglings, bribes, and assassinations across Alliance lands and are unwittingly in league with the dragon Onyxia.

Deadmines Adventures.name: Deadmines Adventures
Deadmines Adventures.text:
The Defias Brotherhood has spread its tendrils through the heart of the Alliance. Its brigands bleed the villages of Goldshire, Lakeshire, Darkshire, and beyond and funnel the money to contractors working on the Juggernaut. Roll on or choose from the Deadmines Adventure Hooks table to determine how the characters learn of this conspiracy.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.tables.RollTable.wowDeadminesAdr7 caption=false rangeLabel="1d4" resultLabel="Adventure Hook" rollable nameStyle="h4" no-toc]

Sample Encounters.name: Sample Encounters
Sample Encounters.text:
Use the encounters tables here to help craft planned encounters for key locations within each area of the dungeon. You can also roll on the tables if characters make enough noise in the dungeon to attract guards from nearby areas to investigate. The Mine Tunnels Encounters covers the mines on the west half of the map, and Ironclad Cove Encounters covers the cove and ship on the east half of the map.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.tables.RollTable.wowMineTunnelsxD caption=false rangeLabel="1d4" resultLabel="Encounter" rollable nameStyle="h4" no-toc]

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.tables.RollTable.wowIroncladCovHC caption=false rangeLabel="1d4" resultLabel="Encounter" rollable nameStyle="h4" no-toc]

Treasure.name: Treasure
Treasure.text:
When the characters overcome an encounter, roll [[/r 2d6]] on the Deadmines Treasure table. When they defeat a boss listed below, roll 4d6 or choose the treasure labeled with the boss’s name.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.tables.RollTable.wowDeadminesTrQa caption=false rangeLabel="4d6" resultLabel="Treasure" rollable nameStyle="h4" no-toc]

About the Deadmines

The Deadmines dungeon has been part of World of Warcraft from the launch of the game, and its story has roots in the very first Warcraft game. In its original version and as presented here, it is the lair of the Defias Brotherhood under that group’s original leader, Edwin VanCleef. During the Cataclysm, the dungeon’s story advanced: Edwin VanCleef was slain, but his young daughter took his place and adopted his mission of revenge—fueled still further by watching her father die at the hands of adventurers. (Vanessa VanCleef uses the same stat block as her father.)

Besides the VanCleef family, some other personnel changes took place in the Deadmines:

Glubtok, a two-headed ogre mage (Large Mage Apprentice with the Giant creature type), took over Rhahk’Zor’s role as foreman.

Helix Gearbreaker took over for Sneed in the Mast Room. Instead of a shredder, Helix (Goblin Boss) is guarded by a hobgoblin called the Lumbering Oaf (use the Bugbear Stalker stat block).

Foe Reaper 5000 now keeps watch over the Goblin Foundry. An improved version of the earlier prototypes, this one uses the Scarecrow stat block and is aided by molten slags (Magmins).

“Captain” Cookie has usurped the position of Captain Greenskin, though the worgen Admiral Ripsnarl (Werewolf) commands the Juggernaut.

Deadmines Areas.name: Deadmines Areas
Deadmines Areas.text:
The characters will likely travel through the following areas of the Deadmines in the listed order.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.4GBPh9cNfsZFguKI caption=false classes="noborder"]

Deadmines Characters.name: Deadmines Characters
Deadmines Characters.text: Edwin VanCleef works with contractors from the Venture Company and Bloodsail Buccaneers, listed here in the order they’re most likely encountered.

Mast Room.name: Mast Room
Mast Room.text:
Sneed’s lumber mill turns Duskwood pines into timbers for building ships. If intruders attack, Sneed (Goblin Boss) leads the defense from inside Sneed’s Shredder (see “Deadmines Characters”). His six Goblin Minions clamber onto a mast hanging from the ceiling and hurl bombs (from a stash of twelve), using the following action:

Throw Bomb. The goblin throws a bomb at a point it can see within 60 feet. Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 12, creatures in a 5-foot-radius Sphere centered on that point. Failure: 10 (3d6) Fire damage. Success: Half damage.

Collapsed Passage.name: Collapsed Passage
Collapsed Passage.text:
The dwarves Wilder and Eugene Thistlenettle led a mining expedition into what they thought was an abandoned mine a few months ago. The tunnel collapsed, and only Wilder escaped. The Defias avoid this area, claiming they can hear the weeping of lost prospectors. Indeed, Eugene Thistlenettle (Wight) and his crew (Ghouls) are now Undead.

This passage leads east to a tower overlooking Ironclad Cove. It also leads south to a 30-foot drop into the cold water of a flooded cave.

Goblin Foundry.name: Goblin Foundry
Goblin Foundry.text: Gilnid’s foundry smelts the ore from the mine’s upper levels into engines and artillery. An enormous crucible suspended from the ceiling pours molten metal into molds and discharges the slag into drains. A crew of Goblin Minions and Bandits patrols here, but they flee or surrender once Gilnid (see “Deadmines Characters”) activates his prototype Foe Reapers (use the Animated Armor stat block, except their Slam attack deals Slashing damage).

Mine Tunnels.name: Mine Tunnels
Mine Tunnels.text:
Winding tunnels connect the entrance of the dungeon, the Mast Room, the Goblin Foundry, and Ironclad Cove. Heavy iron doors (AC 19, HP 72, open DC 20) separate these areas from the mines.

Laborers. Dozens of captive Stormwind citizens (Warrior Infantry) toil for Foreman Rhahk’Zor (see “Deadmines Characters”) who patrols the northern tunnels. These laborers aid the characters in killing Rhahk’Zor if they are freed. Their Speed is reduced to 5 feet by a ball and chain on their ankles, which can be removed by taking the Utilize action and making a successful DC 13 Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) check using Thieves’ Tools.

Blasting Barrels. Every 20 feet along the tunnel walls are wooden barrels of blasting powder (AC 10, HP 5, Vulnerability to Fire damage). They explode when destroyed, dealing 11 (2d10) Fire damage to creatures and objects in a 5-foot-radius Sphere.

The Juggernaut.name: The Juggernaut
The Juggernaut.text:
The Juggernaut’s crew serves under Captain Greenskin and his tauren first mate, Mister Smite, who in turn report to Edwin VanCleef for the duration of their contract. Destroying the Juggernaut won’t stop VanCleef, nor will killing him stop his minions from using the Juggernaut—only doing both will end this threat.

Reaching VanCleef. Edwin VanCleef (see “Deadmines Characters”) is in his cabin on the top deck. He is scheming with Mister Smite (Warrior Veteran) and two Goblin Warriors. The characters face one random encounter as they climb the scaffolding outside the ship.

Sabotaging the Juggernaut. Captain Greenskin and Cookie oversee the skeleton crew constructing the Juggernaut’s steam engine and cannons. The characters face one random encounter in the ship’s interior. Damaging the ship’s engines or arsenal alerts Captain Greenskin (see “Deadmines Characters”) and Cookie (a Murloc Oracle; see chapter 7). They arrive after 2 rounds and fight.

Ironclad Cove.name: Ironclad Cove
Ironclad Cove.text:
At the Deadmines’ deepest point is Ironclad Cove, a cavern large enough to fit an ogre village. A series of locks has flooded the cavern, allowing goblin engineers to construct the nearly completed Juggernaut. The docks leading to the Juggernaut are crawling with Defias laborers (Bandits) and Bloodsail Buccaneers (Pirates) hired to crew the ship. Flocks of parrots (Blood Hawks) swoop overhead, hunting for intruders.

To board the Juggernaut, the characters must defeat or avoid three random encounters (from the Ironclad Cove Encounters table). They can avoid encounters by sneaking past or bluffing their way in with disguises (see the sidebar “The Subtle Approach”).

Sneaking Aboard the Juggernaut. The stacks of cargo on the pier make good hiding places. If the characters successfully hide, they evade one random encounter.

Disguises and Suspicion. The Defias and the Bloodsail pirates mistrust each other and avoid interacting. If the characters each wear a red bandanna or a pirate hat and succeed on a DC 10 Charisma (Deception) check, they evade one random encounter by being ignored.

Exits. A footpath tunnel on the eastern wall leads to the southern coast of Westfall. The sea gate that occupies the entire northern wall leads through a series of locks to another sea gate on the northwest coast of Stranglethorn.

The Subtle Approach

The Deadmines is a good example of some of the principles outlined in the “Adapting Azeroth” section at the beginning of this chapter. In Dungeons & Dragons, a dungeon isn’t necessarily just a gauntlet of combat encounters. Since characters can interact with the world in any way they can imagine, sometimes they concoct clever solutions to the challenges presented in a dungeon and take the adventure in unexpected directions. As the Dungeon Master, you might need to think on your feet to adapt to their plans.

For example, players might come up with a plan to reach Edwin VanCleef without fighting his entire pirate crew—they disguise themselves as pirates and plant a rumor that turns the crew against the Defias. It’s up to you to determine how this plays out, relying on the guidelines in the “Resolving Outcomes” section of the Dungeon Master’s Guide. If the characters’ disguises are successful and they plant a convincing rumor, probably requiring more than one successful Charisma (Deception) check, they might spark a brawl between the pirates and the Defias brigands.

Foreman Rhahk’Zor.name: Foreman Rhahk’Zor
Foreman Rhahk’Zor.text:
“VanCleef pay big for your heads!”

Foreman Rhahk’Zor is a brutish ogre grappler who betrayed his kin in the Deadmines when VanCleef arrived. He cares only about wealth and power and will sacrifice anyone to ensure his own survival.

Remember your first time in the Deadmines? I remember it like it was tomorrow.

—Chromie

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowForemanRhahxo statblock caption=false classes="hide-in-embed"]

Edwin VanCleef, Defias Kingpin.name: Edwin VanCleef, Defias Kingpin
Edwin VanCleef, Defias Kingpin.text:
“Lapdogs, all of you!”

Edwin VanCleef’s sinister charisma was honed by Matthias Shaw, the head of Stormwind Intelligence (SI:7). VanCleef refused this calling, though, for the humble trade of a guild organizer, to better the lives of the common folk. If his cunning hadn’t been polluted by vengeance, he could have truly changed the world for the better.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowEdwinVanCle0Y statblock caption=false classes="double-column hide-in-embed"]

Sneed and His Shredder.name: Sneed and His Shredder
Sneed and His Shredder.text:
“I made this beauty to cut down Ashenvale old growths, but there ain’t no reason why she can’t fell you, too!”

Sneed (@UUID[Compendium.dnd-monster-manual.actors.Actor.mmGoblinBoss0000]{Goblin Boss}) was a logging engineer for the Venture Co. in Stranglethorn when Edwin VanCleef hired him to build his Juggernaut. Sneed runs the Mast Room from his bipedal, tree-felling shredder.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowSneedTJeij57K statblock caption=false classes="hide-in-embed"]

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowSneedsShred0W statblock caption=false classes="hide-in-embed"]

Captain Greenskin and His Crew.name: Captain Greenskin and His Crew
Captain Greenskin and His Crew.text:
“Avast, ye swabs! Repel the invaders!”

The Juggernaut’s captain is a disgraced buccaneer called Greenskin. He doesn’t trust Sneed and Gilnid but doesn’t mind captaining the ship they’re building.

Captain Greenskin’s stat block is below. His first mate is Mister Smite, a tauren @UUID[Compendium.dnd-monster-manual.actors.Actor.mmWarriorVeteran]{Warrior Veteran}. His cook is Cookie, a @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowMurlocOraclQJ]{Murloc Oracle} (see chapter 7).

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowCaptainGreeuo statblock caption=false classes="hide-in-embed"]

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowMisterSmitedw statblock caption=false classes="hide-in-embed"]

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowCookieJWlfXOb statblock caption=false classes="hide-in-embed"]

Gilnid and His Prototype Reapers.name: Gilnid and His Prototype Reapers
Gilnid and His Prototype Reapers.text:
“Anyone want a break? Too bad! Back to work, oafs!”

Gilnid was renowned in Booty Bay for his unusually large size and for making mechanical bodyguards. He was exiled after his machines went haywire and slaughtered their charges. The Defias found him and paid him well to arm the Juggernaut; Gilnid is using the money to fund his pet project, a harvest golem called the Foe Reaper 4000. Early prototypes of the Foe Reaper guard the foundry. Gilnid is a coward who taunts his foes from behind his reapers.

It’s fun to watch Cookie, knowing what’s in store for the humble murloc.

—Chromie

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowGilnidXx1rAop statblock caption=false classes="double-column hide-in-embed"]

Death Knight.name: Death Knight
Death Knight.text:
@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.lmXdEteZ6un2bD0e caption=false cite=false classes="size-four margin-center noborder"]

The Lich King Ner’zhul created death knights from fallen warriors and paladins to serve as undead, immortal lieutenants of the Scourge in the Third War. Arthas Menethil was the first of these death knights, and after Arthas became the Lich King, the power of the death knights only grew stronger. (See @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowConflictsOfAz.JournalEntryPage.YRwQ3wrLM22odUUP]{The Scourge} in chapter 6 for more information.)

During the invasion of Northrend, a company of death knights was freed from the Lich King’s control. These knights claimed a flying necropolis as the headquarters for the Knights of the Ebon Blade. Under the command of Highlord Darion Mograine, they dedicated themselves to the protection of Azeroth. After Bolvar Fordragon took on the Lich King’s mantle, he ordered his lieutenants, the Four Horsemen, to call forth a new generation of death knights to join the Ebon Blade.

Death knights engage their foes in melee, supplementing weapon attacks with unholy magic. They drag foes into one-on-one conflicts and wield their magic to draw enemy attacks and prevent enemies from fleeing their grasp.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.MxtHyAk59gzFhntH caption=false classes="noborder"]

Playing a Death Knight.name: Playing a Death Knight
Playing a Death Knight.text:
Death knight is a hero class, which means you typically must start play at level 3 or higher (see the “Hero Classes” sidebar). To play a death knight, choose the Paladin class from the Player’s Handbook and the Oath of the Ebon Blade subclass, described below. This subclass alters some of your core Paladin class features beginning at level 1.

Creating a Death Knight

When you add the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.classes.Item.phbpdnPaladin000]{Paladin} class to your character sheet you will be given the option to pick between the Paladin and the Death Knight.

As a death knight, you can choose one of three specializations by inscribing the corresponding rune on your weapon using your Runeforging feature: Blood, Frost, or Unholy.

Blood Specialization

With the Blood rune, you are a dark guardian who manipulates and corrupts life energy to sustain yourself in the face of an enemy onslaught. The following choices will help you focus on this specialization:

Level 3. Choose Greataxes, Greatswords, or Mauls for your Weapon Mastery feature. Choose @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbfstIntercepti]{Interception} for a Fighting Style feat.

Feats. Consider the following feats at higher levels: @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftCharger0000]{Charger}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftCrusher0000]{Crusher}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbfstGreatWeapo]{Great Weapon Fighting}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftGreatWeapon]{Great Weapon Master}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftHeavyArmorM]{Heavy Armor Master}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftPiercer0000]{Piercer}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftSlasher0000]{Slasher}, and @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftTough000000]{Tough}.

Frost Specialization

Wielding the Frost rune, you are an icy harbinger of doom, channeling runic power and delivering vicious weapon strikes. The following choices will help you focus on this specialization:

Level 3. Choose Light Hammers or Scimitars for your Weapon Mastery feature. Choose @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbfstTwoWeaponF]{Two-Weapon Fighting} for a Fighting Style feat.

Feats. Consider the following feats at higher levels: @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftCharger0000]{Charger}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftCrusher0000]{Crusher}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftDualWielder]{Dual Wielder}, and @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftSlasher0000]{Slasher}.

Hero Classes

Three of the World of Warcraft classes—death knight, demon hunter, and evoker—are hero classes, meaning that they are typically available only to characters starting at level 3 or higher. In the story of World of Warcraft, characters with these classes are already experienced and powerful adventurers by the time they enter the game.

The death knight and the demon hunter classes are represented by subclasses (the Oath of the Ebon Blade Paladin and the Demon Hunter Ranger, respectively) that alter the character’s base class. With your DM’s permission, you can start as a level 1 character of one of these classes, but your subclass choice is fixed when you make the character.

Playing an evoker doesn’t alter the base Sorcerer class, but it slightly alters the Draconic Sorcery subclass.

Unholy Specialization

With the Unholy rune, you become a master of death and decay, spreading infection and controlling undead minions. The following choices will help you focus on this specialization:

Level 3. Choose Greataxes, Greatswords, or Mauls for your Weapon Mastery feature. Choose @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbfstGreatWeapo]{Great Weapon Fighting} for a Fighting Style feat.

Feats. Consider the following feats at higher levels: @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftCharger0000]{Charger}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftCrusher0000]{Crusher}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftGreatWeapon]{Great Weapon Master}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftPiercer0000]{Piercer}, and @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftSlasher0000]{Slasher}.

Oath of the Ebon Blade (Paladin Subclass.name: Oath of the Ebon Blade (Paladin Subclass)
Oath of the Ebon Blade (Paladin Subclass.text:
@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.classes.Item.wowpdnOathEbonBl inline]

Level 1: Death Coil

This feature replaces the Lay On Hands feature of the Paladin class.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.classes.Item.wowpdnDeathCoil0 inline]

Specialization

Every class in World of Warcraft offers options for specializing in different aspects of the class’s powers and features. In this book, those specializations are reflected in these ways:

Subclass Features. The Oath of the Ebon Blade subclass’s Runeforging feature reflects the three death knight specializations, allowing a character to choose a new specialization with every level gained.

Feat and Spell Selection. Some specializations are represented with different Fighting Style feats; the difference between an arms warrior and a protection warrior is largely a matter of the weapons they use and the corresponding Fighting Styles. Similarly, mage specializations are reflected in the character’s spell selection, along with feats that enhance different spells.

Subclass Choice. Often, specializations point to different subclasses within the same class. For example, the monk specializations of brewmaster, mistweaver, and windwalker map to three different Monk subclasses.

Demon Hunter.name: Demon Hunter
Demon Hunter.text:
@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.I9FrieyC6g7I39fI caption=false cite=false classes="size-four margin-center noborder"]

The first demon hunter was @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowIllidanStor7Y]{Illidan Stormrage}, a night elf sorcerer (and brother of Archdruid Malfurion Stormrage) who betrayed his people and all of Azeroth during the War of the Ancients, the first invasion of the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowConflictsOfAz.JournalEntryPage.mOeoKWAu3OOx8LP9]{Burning Legion}. Secretly planning to learn the Legion’s secrets in order to undermine the demonic forces from within, Illidan mastered the Legion’s magic and received magical gifts from the fallen titan Sargeras.

Following Illidan’s example, demon hunters (often called Illidari) sacrifice their sight, family ties, and personal aspirations in exchange for fel power they use to battle the Legion. They begin their training by slaying a demon, eating its heart, and drinking its blood, allowing them to tap into demonic powers. Their physical sight is replaced by a supernatural sense, which at short range lets them perceive the truth of illusions and see hidden enemies. But their demonic features incite revulsion and dread among other people.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.rFnbbgJzFBIIqDe1 cite=false classes="noborder"]

Playing a Demon Hunter.name: Playing a Demon Hunter
Playing a Demon Hunter.text:
Demon hunter is a hero class, which means you typically must start play at level 3 or higher (see the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowDeathKnight00.JournalEntryPage.gL82O0Vn607HF94R]{Hero Classes} sidebar earlier in this chapter). To play a demon hunter, choose the Ranger class from the Player’s Handbook. Your subclass, the Demon Hunter, alters some of your core Ranger class features.

Creating a Demon Hunter

When you add the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.classes.Item.phbrgrRanger0000]{Ranger} class to your character sheet you will be given the option to pick between the Ranger and the Demon Hunter.

All demon hunters in World of Warcraft lore are elves (@UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.origins.Item.wowsptBloodElf00]{blood elves}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.origins.Item.wowsptNightElf00]{night elves}, or @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.origins.Item.wowsptVoidElf000]{void elves}), so check with your DM before playing a demon hunter of another species.

As a Demon Hunter, you can choose one of three specializations: Devourer, Havoc, or Vengeance.

Devourer Specialization

With the devourer specialization, you harness the power of the Void to crush your enemies and feast on their souls. The following choices will help you focus on this specialization:

Level 1. Choose Handaxes, Scimitars, or Short­swords for your Weapon Mastery feature. Choose the Void Warrior option instead of a Fighting Style feat, and choose @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplChillTouch]{Chill Touch} and @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplMindSliver]{Mind Sliver} as your cantrips.

Spells. Choose the Devourer spells from the Demon Hunter Spells table.

Feats. Consider the following feats at higher levels: @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftDefensiveDu]{Defensive Duelist}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftMageSlayer0]{Mage Slayer}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftShadowTouch]{Shadow Touched}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftSlasher0000]{Slasher}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftSpeedy00000]{Speedy}, and @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftSpellSniper]{Spell Sniper}.

Havoc Specialization

With the havoc specialization, you are a fierce melee combatant who masters the destructive power of fel magic. The following choices will help you focus on this specialization:

Level 1. Choose Handaxes, Scimitars, or Short­swords for your Weapon Mastery feature. Choose @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbfstTwoWeaponF]{Two-Weapon Fighting} for a Fighting Style feat.

Spells. Choose the Havoc spells from the Demon Hunter Spells table.

Feats. Consider the following feats at higher levels: @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftCharger0000]{Charger}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftDualWielder]{Dual Wielder}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftMageSlayer0]{Mage Slayer}, and @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftSlasher0000]{Slasher}.

Vengeance Specialization

With the vengeance specialization, you embrace the demon within to incinerate your enemies and protect your allies. The following choices will help you focus on this specialization:

Level 1. Choose Battleaxes or Longswords for your Weapon Mastery feature. Choose @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbfstIntercepti]{Interception} as your Fighting Style feat.

Spells. Choose the Vengeance spells from the Demon Hunter Spells table.

Feats. Consider the following feats at higher levels: @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftCharger0000]{Charger}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftDurable0000]{Durable}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftSentinel000]{Sentinel}, and @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftSlasher0000]{Slasher}.

Demon Hunter Warglaives

During the War of the Ancients, Illidan defeated a demonic commander and claimed the demon’s weapons—called warglaives—as his own. These later became known as the Twin Blades of Azzinoth (see chapter 3), and they inspired a whole category of weapons that are favored by demon hunters to this day. Warglaives vary widely in appearance and construction, giving different weapons the game statistics of a Battleaxe, a Handaxe, a Longsword, or a Scimitar.

Demon Hunter (Ranger Subclass).name: Demon Hunter (Ranger Subclass)
Demon Hunter (Ranger Subclass).text:
Embrace the Magic of Demons to Fight Fire with Fire

Most Demon Hunters joined Illidan on Outland as he marshaled his forces to battle the Burning Legion. You might have followed a different path, inspired by Illidan rather than directly trained by him, but the result is the same: You have embraced the magic of the Burning Legion with the singular goal of defeating it on Azeroth and every other world.

Overview.name: Overview
Overview.text:
@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.1KNAewIodd6JZJtq caption=false classes="noborder"]

For Level 11–16 Characters • The Burning Legion

Dire Maul is an ancient night elf ruin occupied by vengeful spirits, cruel arcanists, sinister satyrs, and opportunistic ogres. Once known as Eldre’Thalas, it was renamed Dire Maul by the Gordrunni ogres who dwell there now.

Twelve thousand years ago, the city was ruled by a scholarly Highborne prince named Tortheldrin and the Shen’dralar, his secret order of elf mages. They safeguarded the arcane libraries of Queen Azshara, which fell under attack by the Burning Legion during the War of the Ancients.

The war ended with the destruction of the Well of Eternity, the source of the Highborne elves’ immortality. Prince Tortheldrin’s people discovered with horror that they had become addicted to the well’s boundless arcane power, and their cravings soon turned to lethargy and agony. Panicked, the prince summoned a demon called Immol’thar and imprisoned it so his people could nourish themselves by siphoning its endlessly replenishing magic.

The secluded mages kept this secret for millennia. During that time, the fel power Tortheldrin consumed made him cruel. When the mages’ population grew beyond Immol’thar’s ability to sustain, Tortheldrin ordered the culling of his own people, sparing only his Shen’dralar, who retreated into a solipsistic obsession with ancient lore. Now, thieves and squatters have made the ruin their home, reveling just out of sight of the tormented mages within.

Dire Maul Areas.name: Dire Maul Areas
Dire Maul Areas.text:
Dire Maul is a sprawling complex made of three wings accessible via a central ruin.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.fR2OraZZ02Oy4RVg classes="noborder"]

Sample Encounters.text:

You can also roll on the table if characters make enough noise in the dungeon to attract guards from nearby areas to investigate. If the characters leave the dungeon and return after completing a Long Rest, new creatures replace those the characters defeated.

Treasure.text:
When the characters overcome an encounter, roll [[/r 2d6]] on the Dire Maul Treasure table below. When they defeat a boss listed below, roll 4d6 or choose the treasure labeled with the boss’s name.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.tables.RollTable.wowDireMaulTreyT caption=false rangeLabel="4d6" resultLabel="Treasure" rollable nameStyle="h4" no-toc]

Ogre Tribute

Ogre tradition holds that any ogre who slays King Gordok in a one-on-one battle becomes the new King Gordok. If at least one character is disguised as an ogre, killing King Gordok in such a duel makes them the king.

Duel of Honor. A solo fight against King Gordok is a death sentence for most characters. You can make the fight easier by not using his Legendary Actions. However, the goal of a solo fight is to survive until someone realizes that King Gordok cheats by letting Cho’Rush the Observer secretly heal him (see the Adviser’s Aid Bonus Action in his stat block). Revealing this causes the ogre audience to roar for the whole party to join the fight and kill the “cheater king.”

Aftermath. If Cho’Rush survives, he declares the winner the new king. Without his declaration, the ogres all brawl to become the new king. To hail the new king, the surviving ogres bestow tribute or grant Blessings and Charms (see the Dungeon Master’s Guide) with shamanic magic:

Guard Fengus: 3d10 × 10,000 CP

Guard Mol’dar: Charm of Vitality

Guard Slip’kik: Charm of Clairvoyance (functions as a Potion of Clairvoyance)

Stomper Kreeg: Strong rum worth 8d6 × 100 GP

Captain Kromcrush: Blessing of Valhalla that summons Ogres instead of Berserkers

Cho’Rush the Observer: Unread Tome of Leadership and Influence pilfered from the elves

Capital Gardens Characters.name: Capital Gardens Characters
Capital Gardens Characters.text:
@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.HN8CbSEsylI1Zs0N caption=false classes="sepia noborder"]

Dire Maul’s west wing is home to the Shen’dralar and the spirits of their victims. The Shen’dralar are initially Friendly toward the characters but turn Hostile if the characters fight them or steal their tomes. The Shen’dralar are bound to the demon Immol’thar’s power and can’t leave the Capital Gardens for long. The creatures here are listed in the order they’re most likely encountered.

Dire Maul Adventures.name: Dire Maul Adventures
Dire Maul Adventures.text:
The night elves of Darnassus seek to cleanse Eldre’Thalas of corruption. Meanwhile, the Horde’s Stonemaul ogre allies seek to make Dire Maul their new stronghold. Roll on or choose from the Dire Maul Adventure Hooks table to involve the characters with these plots.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.tables.RollTable.wowDireMaulAdvs8 caption=false rangeLabel="1d6" resultLabel="Adventure Hook" rollable nameStyle="h4" no-toc]

Gordok Commons Characters.name: Gordok Commons Characters
Gordok Commons Characters.text: The upper echelons of Gordrunni society have turned Dire Maul’s north wing into their den. The creatures here are listed in the order they’re most likely encountered.

Warpwood Quarter Characters.name: Warpwood Quarter Characters
Warpwood Quarter Characters.text: Dire Maul’s east wing has been taken over by the Wildspawn satyr cult, drawn to its demonic power. The creatures here are listed in the order they’re most likely encountered.

Central Ruin.name: Central Ruin
Central Ruin.text:
The ruins at the center of Dire Maul house ogre commoners and other scoundrels.

Eldreth Row. The front gates of Dire Maul are smashed open. Ogre sentries extort tolls from the scoundrels that congregate in the Broken Commons, and crush them if they refuse to pay. The ogres avoid the side passage into the Warpwood Quarter, because an Ancient of War (see chapter 7) with the Petrified condition blocks the path. It moves if the condition is ended.

Broken Commons. Throngs of scoundrels have set up tents and bonfires amid the ruins, cheering for bloodsport in the Maul. The games are held by the Crimson Ring, a band of thieves and outcasts from the Horde, with King Gordok’s permission. This rough-and-tumble group welcomes outsiders, if only so they have new rubes to fleece.

The Maul. The coliseum was originally a temple built in honor of Queen Azshara at the height of the Kaldorei Empire. A doorway on the west side of the Broken Commons leads to a tunnel into the pit (though showboating gladiators love to jump straight in).

East Wing: Warpwood Quarter.name: East Wing: Warpwood Quarter
East Wing: Warpwood Quarter.text:
The east wing is a grand conservatory corrupted by fel magic, which has attracted a satyr cult.

Warpwood Quarter (Outdoors). A balcony overlooks the canopy of the trees in the Conservatory below. Characters with a Passive Perception score of 15 or higher spot the imp Pusillin (see “Warpwood Quarter Characters”) spying on them behind a statue in the north, clutching a silver key. He flees indoors; a character who takes the Search action and succeeds on a DC 13 Wisdom (Survival) check can track him to the Hidden Reach.

Warpwood Quarter (Indoors). The satyr servants of Alzzin the Wildshaper lair here. A Shivarra (see chapter 7) bound to Alzzin’s service toys with a cult of satyrs who wish to earn her favor.

Hidden Reach. Alzzin and his cult snuck into Dire Maul through this secret back entrance. Pusillin (see “Warpwood Quarter Characters”) hides in the loft in the south of this room. A character can find him by taking the Search action and making a successful DC 18 Wisdom (Perception) check. If they leave here without finding him, he flees through the eastern passage, emerging in the wilds of Feralas.

Conservatory (Indoors). Characters who enter this area from the southern ramp must pass through the pool of Hydrospawn (Marid), a mighty water elemental. Zevrim Thornhoof (see “Warpwood Quarter Characters”) and his bodyguard (Doomguard; see chapter 7) conduct blood rituals from the loft above the pool. They join the fight the round after combat begins with Hydrospawn.

Conservatory (Outdoors). Despite its corruption, this lush garden flourishes beneath a shady canopy. Old Ironbark (see “Warpwood Quarter Characters”) is petrified in the middle of the room. The heavy stone door to the Shrine of Eldretharr is flanked by two Infernals (see chapter 7) and can be opened only by a character who succeeds on a DC 25 Strength check or by Old Ironbark if he is freed.

Shrine of Eldretharr. Huge, thorny vines breach the walls of this shrine. Alzzin the Wildshaper (see “Warpwood Quarter Characters”) has conjured a demonic power called the Felvine, which lets him sense all creatures within the Warpwood Quarter. Two Felhounds (see chapter 7) hide in the undergrowth near the Felvine sapling in the center of the chamber. Alzzin lurks invisibly on the east side of the room until his hounds attack, then he joins in.

About Dire Maul

Dire Maul has been part of World of Warcraft almost since the beginning and includes three connected dungeons intended for a group of five mid-level characters. Its story is rooted in the ancient history of the world and is thus timeless, although current lore suggests that the dungeon has been cleared of its most dangerous inhabi- tants—including the Highborne elves that feed on Immol’thar’s fel magic.

West Wing: Capital Gardens.name: West Wing: Capital Gardens
West Wing: Capital Gardens.text:
The west wing is the last remaining redoubt of the Shen’dralar. Their dependence on Immol’thar’s magic prevents them from leaving. The stone doors within this wing are locked; the locks are simple (1 action to pick) and of superior quality (DC 20). Alternatively, they can be opened with Pusillin’s Crescent Key (see “Pusillin” in “Warpwood Quarter Characters”).

Shield Generators. The dome of force in the Prison of Immolthar is generated by five pylons in this wing. See “Immol’thar” in “Capital Gardens Characters” for more information; they are shown on the map as bright blue crystals.

Capital Gardens. The courtyard of the Capital Gardens is a gnarled field of petrified trees oozing with fel sap. A ramp west of the garden leads down to Tendris Warpwood (see “Capital Gardens Characters”), who guards the gate to the Prison of Immol’thar (marked D on the map) with two Treant allies (they lack the Animate Trees action). Stairs in the northwest part of the hall (marked E on the map) lead up to the Court of the Highborne.

Court of the Highborne. The undead forms of those Prince Tortheldrin slaughtered linger in the Court of the Highborne as Wraiths and Graveyard Revenants, endlessly repeating the motions of life. Illyanna Ravenoak and her giant bear Ferra (see “Capital Gardens Characters”) are cursed to guard this terrace. When she attacks, all remaining Undead in this area join in.

Prison of Immol’thar. Like a crass mimicry of the Well of Eternity, the imprisoned demon Immol’thar’s fel magic is siphoned constantly by 2d6 + 10 Shen’dralar Mages to slake their thirst for magic. A dome of force prevents Immol’thar from escaping (see “Immol’thar” in “Capital Gardens Characters”).

The Athenaeum. A passage from the northeast of Immol’thar’s prison leads up a ramp (marked C on the map) to the Athenaeum—a library holding ten thousand years of lore in its countless precious tomes. Prince Tortheldrin scrawls endless, inane texts here, guarded by two Cultist Hierophants. He is also attended by 2d10 + 10 Cultist Fanatics, who cower in fear if he’s attacked. A narrow passage (marked B) connects the Athenaeum to Gordok Commons in the north wing.

North Wing: Gordok Commons.name: North Wing: Gordok Commons
North Wing: Gordok Commons.text:
The north wing holds a temple to Elune desecrated by the upper echelons of the Gordrunni clan, while the common ogres of the clan live in the Broken Commons or in camps in the wilderness.

Gordok Commons. Ogres use Gordok Commons for raucous parties, brawls, and crude theatre. It is patrolled by Guard Mol’dar, Stomper Kreeg, and Guard Fengus (see “Captain Kromcrush and His Guards” in “Gordok Commons Characters” and “Ogre Tribute” below).

Halls of Destruction. King Gordok’s guards rest in the Halls of Destruction, protecting the only path to and from their king’s chamber. Guard Slip’kik oversees this area. He reports to Captain Kromcrush, who wards the entrance to Gordok’s Seat. A goblin thief named Knot Thimblejack is a prisoner in the northeast corner (see “Gordok Commons Characters”). A ramp in the southwest part of the hall (marked A on the map) leads up to Gordok’s Seat.

Gordok’s Seat. In Gordok’s Seat, dozens of Hyenas sleep in the jungle heat while ogre servants swat flies and use giant palm leaves to fan King Gordok and his vizier, Cho’Rush the Observer (see “Gordok Commons Characters” for both). The ogres scramble to protect their king, but any ogre who challenges the king to a duel of honor can vie for the crown in single combat (see “Ogre Tribute” below). A Shen’dralar named Mordent Evenshade (see “Gordok Commons Characters”) is forced to be King Gordok’s jester.

Zevrim Thornhoof.name: Zevrim Thornhoof
Zevrim Thornhoof.text:
“Your blood shall catch Lord Xavius’s eye! (Please?)”

Zevrim is a Felsworn Satyr (see chapter 7) and the second-in-command of the Wildspawn satyr cult. He has a secret deal with the Crimson Ring to sacrifice gladiators who lose their bouts but survive. His blood rites have whipped the elemental Hydrospawn into a murderous frenzy.

Zevrim hates living in Alzzin’s shadow; he tries to impress the Burning Legion in hopes of a promotion.

Magical Healing. Zevrim has the following additional Bonus Action available:

Gift of the Xavian (1/Day). Zevrim regains 13 (3d8) Hit Points.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowZevrimThornJr statblock caption=false classes="hide-in-embed"]

Pusillin.name: Pusillin
Pusillin.text:
“Eeeheehee, you thinks you has Pusillin cornered? Just looks at what Pusillin has up his sleeve!”

A craven @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowFelImpEEKWKFi]{Fel Imp} (see chapter 7) who knows every inch of Dire Maul, Pusillin has a Crescent Key, which opens any door in the Capital Gardens.

Conjure Scapegoat. Pusillin has learned a ritual from the warlocks of Dire Maul and keeps it on the brink of completion. He has the following Reaction:

Ritual of J’eevee (1/Day). Trigger: Pusillin becomes Bloodied but is conscious. Response: Pusillin summons an Infernal (see chapter 7), which appears in an unoccupied space within 30 feet of him and remains until killed.

The summoned infernal is enraged at being yanked through the fabric of space and indiscriminately battles Pusillin, the characters, and any other creatures in the area. Pusillin attempts to use the distraction to escape the area.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowPusillinAGPYF statblock caption=false classes="hide-in-embed"]

Alzzin the Wildshaper.name: Alzzin the Wildshaper
Alzzin the Wildshaper.text:
“O Felvine, as the Fruit of Fertility you gave this verdant land life. Now, drain it dry, and gift its power unto me!”

Alzzin was once a night elf druid but now leads the Wildspawn cult. Before he was corrupted into a satyr millennia ago, he obsessed over the work of a Highborn named Millicent Serene, who created the Fruit of Fertility, a conduit to the Emerald Dream that turned Feralas into the lush jungle that it is today. Millicent died in the War of the Ancients, and Alzzin’s obsession shifted to her crowning achievement—namely, corrupting it into the Felvine, which drains the life from Feralas and empowers him.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.0iZQFWXO11jXYvpI caption=false classes="noborder"]

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowAlzzintheWiZ5 statblock caption=false classes="double-column hide-in-embed"]

Old Ironbark.name: Old Ironbark
Old Ironbark.text:
“Thank you, mortals. I shall act as your instrument of destruction before I return to the Emerald Dream.”

Old Ironbark is a Friendly @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowAncientofWa1o]{Ancient of War} (see chapter 7) that has the Petrified condition. If freed, he helps the characters defeat Alzzin the Wildshaper. Attempts to end the Petrified condition on him (such as with a Greater Restoration spell) fail unless Zevrim Thornhoof is slain first.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowOldIronbarkFP statblock caption=false classes="hide-in-embed"]

Prince Tortheldrin.name: Prince Tortheldrin
Prince Tortheldrin.text:
“For ten thousand years I have ruled this kingdom. Is it not still glorious? Is it not still a jewel of our empire?”

Prince Tortheldrin presents a genteel facade to his guests. Confident in his near invulnerability, the Highborne fears no threats and dismisses even accusations of mass murder as twaddle. He whiles away his days telling tales to his Shen’dralar sycophants but is eager for new sagas. Thus, he treats adventurers who display even a modicum of sophistication as honored guests.

When Immol’thar is slain, Tortheldrin’s Demonic Invincibility trait ends, and he flies into a rage, murdering anyone in his path. When he dies, his body is reborn as a horned, winged demon. Unlike a true demon, he is permanently destroyed when killed in this form.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowPrinceTorthmG statblock caption=false classes="double-column hide-in-embed"]

Illyanna Ravenoak.name: Illyanna Ravenoak
Illyanna Ravenoak.text:
“Flee … please! My will is not my own! It is the prince!”

Illyanna Ravenoak and her animal companion Ferra were Prince Tortheldrin’s most valued hunters until Illyanna refused the order to massacre her kin. As punishment, the prince executed Illyanna and used fel magic to bind her spirit to her corpse, condemning her to patrol his realm as an undead guard.

Illyanna’s bear @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowFerraqY2oQ5st]{Ferra} uses the Primeval Owlbear stat block but has the Undead creature type.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowIllyannaRavCM statblock caption=false classes="double-column hide-in-embed"]

Tendris Warpwood.name: Tendris Warpwood
Tendris Warpwood.text:
“Ancients, rise up against these intruders!”

Tendris Warpwood (Ancient of War; see chapter 7) was an unquestioning defender of Eldre’Thalas, his heart inexorably entwined with the fate of the city. Just as fel magic corrupted his prince, so too did it infect the ancient’s spirit.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowTendrisWarpc3 statblock caption=false classes="hide-in-embed"]

Immol’thar.name: Immol’thar
Immol’thar.text:
@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.tkIxh2Djb4i52woh caption=false cite=false classes="float-right size-three noborder"]

“Guorrrr … GUORRRR!”

Immol’thar is a void terror conjured from the Twisting Nether. The creature’s fel blood generates vast amounts of magic, which the Shen’dralar siphon hourly.

Immol’thar’s Prison. Immol’thar’s prison is a dome of force sustained by five shield generators (shown as blue crystals on the map). Each generator is powered by four arcane elementals (see below). A generator shuts down if its defenders die or move more than 30 feet from it. When all five generators are offline, the shield falls. The Shen’dralar mages in Immol’thar’s prison try to restrain the demon, but it slays them all with a burst of arcane power and runs rampant through Dire Maul.

Arcane Elementals. The @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowArcaneEleme0B]{arcane elemental} use the Fire Elemental stat block, but they have Immunity to Force damage instead of Fire damage, and their traits and actions that deal Fire damage deal Force damage instead.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowImmoltharCDeG statblock caption=false cite=false classes="double-column hide-in-embed"]

Captain Kromcrush and His Guards.name: Captain Kromcrush and His Guards
Captain Kromcrush and His Guards.text:
“Who you callin’ gnoll lover? You da gnoll lover!”

Kromcrush is the captain of the guard. He got his position by sweet-talking King Gordok, not through any exceptional skill. Kromcrush and his lieutenants use the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-monster-manual.actors.Actor.mmBerserkerComma]{Berserker Commander} stat block, but as ogres, their size is Large and their creature type is Giant.

Kromcrush has four lieutenants:

@UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowFengus4avcrEN]{Guard Fengus}. Ever since Cho’Rush the Observer told Fengus he was destined to meet a mate while on duty, Fengus has spent almost every waking moment patrolling Gordok territory.

@UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowMoldarW05du7O]{Guard Mol’dar}. Mol’dar is a zealously loyal guard. He is convinced King Gordok gifted him with a pair of enchanted gauntlets that have made him the Gordrunni arm wrestling champion for six years running. In truth, King Gordok threw his old armor away—Mol’dar simply found it first.

@UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowSlipkikC9RNnP]{Guard Slip’kik}. Slip’kik is treacherous but lazy. Rather than openly challenge King Gordok, Slip’kik tinkers with traps and magical devices, hoping to eventually deliver a coup de grace without an ounce of risk or a drop of sweat.

@UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowStomperKree34]{Stomper Kreeg}. Though Stomper Kreeg is often passed out drunk on duty, nothing rouses the ogre into a berserker fury faster than the sound of his precious drink splattering on the stone floor.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowCaptainKrombs statblock caption=false classes="double-column hide-in-embed"]

Knot Thimblejack.name: Knot Thimblejack
Knot Thimblejack.text:
“Please tell me that you came to get me out of here!”

Knot Thimblejack (@UUID[Compendium.dnd-monster-manual.actors.Actor.mmGoblinMinion00]{Goblin Minion}) is a tailor who made costumes for gladiators in the Maul, specializing in ogre suits. He was snatched in the night by ogres for his disrespect and thrown in irons. A character can take the Utilize action to try to pick the lock using Thieves’ Tools, doing so with a successful [[/check 25 dex slt format=long]]; alternatively, stealing the key from Guard Slip’kik’s pocket requires a successful [[/check 15 dex slt format=long]]. If the characters save Knot, he gives them a magic cap. It functions as a @UUID[Compendium.dnd-dungeon-masters-guide.equipment.Item.dmgHatOfDisguise]{Hat of Disguise} that allows the wearer to appear as an ogre.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowKnotThimbleOS statblock caption=false classes="hide-in-embed"]

King Gordok.name: King Gordok
King Gordok.text:
“You challenge me, scrubs? I stay da king FOREVER!”

All these King Gordoks … or is it Kings Gordok? Anyway, I think all big ogres would benefit from spending some time small.

—Chromie

To rule the Gordok ogres, one must simply proclaim oneself king, then destroy all who disagree. A devious Gordrunni warlord called Ulrok convinced a dozen of his people’s strongest warriors to challenge the king at the same time. The wild melee left most of the contestants dead or wounded, and Ulrok’s blade easily cut down the survivors and the battle-weary king. To this day, Gordrunni ogres speak in hushed tones about the “Day of Da Blood.”

Gordok is so feared that he rarely faces any challenges, but he keeps his skills sharp as an undefeated champion of the Maul. He never picks a fight he doesn’t think he can win—and cheats by having his vizier Cho’Rush discreetly heal him from afar.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowKingGordokBz5 statblock caption=false classes="double-column hide-in-embed"]

Cho’Rush the Observer.name: Cho’Rush the Observer
Cho’Rush the Observer.text:
“What, we cheat? (Yeah, huh huh, we cheat.) Hush!”

The two-headed ogre mage Cho’Rush doesn’t usually take sides, but when Ulrok was rising to power, it was clear nobody could challenge him. Cho’Rush ingratiated himself to Ulrok by healing him in the bloodbath that made him king. As a reward, the new King Gordok awarded Cho’Rush the position of chief adviser.

If revealed as a cheat (see “Ogre Tribute” above), Cho’Rush abandons all pretense and fights openly.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.ODb0KbpY1OM4bQrj caption=false classes="sepia size-four margin-center noborder"]

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowChoRushtheOB1 statblock caption=false classes="hide-in-embed"]

Mordent Evenshade.name: Mordent Evenshade
Mordent Evenshade.text:
“We Highborne must leave the past behind us.”

Mordent Evenshade is a Shen’dralar @UUID[Compendium.dnd-monster-manual.actors.Actor.mmArchmage000000]{Archmage} who has weaned himself off Immol’thar’s fel magic. He feels the pangs of arcane withdrawals keenly, but he is disciplined enough to endure until he can unite with the night elves and their sustaining moonwells.

Mordent’s Goal. Mordent aimed to flee to Teldrassil and beg Tyrande Whisperwind for aid in freeing the rest of the Shen’dralar from Tortheldrin’s evil, but his escape was cut short by the Gordrunni ogres.

One Last Trick. Mordent put up a desperate struggle to escape but was nonetheless captured. His captors demand that he use his spells to entertain King Gordok as a jester. He plans to cast his Fly spell when adventurers free him and distract the ogres.

Purifying the Felvine. Mordent Evenshade knew Millicent Serene when they were young and gave her the nickname Milli. He thinks that her masterwork, the Fruit of Fertility, could be saved if it were watered with water from the roots of Nordrassil in Mount Hyjal—possibly starting an adventure arc that sends the characters to the ends of Azeroth and pits them against the Burning Legion.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowMordentEvenBL statblock caption=false classes="double-column hide-in-embed"]

Dracthyr.name: Dracthyr
Dracthyr.text:
@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.AAOcGawwFBC5I5uK classes="hide-in-embed noborder"]

In ages long past, Neltharion the Earth-Warder—the former leader of the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowBestiaryOfAze.JournalEntryPage.jnGTp7LiVzQO8DTY]{black dragonflight}—foresaw a world-shaking conflict and set out to create soldiers for that war. Neltharion was inspired by the mortal peoples who had just begun their spread across @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowWorldOfAzerot]{Azeroth}. He blended together the essence of dragons and the adaptability of those peoples, creating the dracthyr. He set them in the Forbidden Reach, the northernmost of the Dragon Isles, which would serve as their training grounds and barracks.

The dracthyr embodied the might of all five dragonflights, and they were bound to Neltharion’s service by the power of a titan relic called the Oathbinder. Then the Oathbinder was destroyed in a battle against the primal dragon Raszageth, and Neltharion feared that the dracthyr would turn against him and the other Dragon Aspects. Rather than allow the dracthyr to choose their own destinies, he and the blue Aspect, Malygos, sealed them away in hidden creches in the Forbidden Reach and put them into a magical stasis, where they remained for nearly twenty millennia.

The return of Raszageth caused the dracthyr to awaken from their stasis. The five weyrns—close-knit fighting groups charged with specific purposes in Neltharion’s original vision—chose new paths in a world very different from the one they were created for:

The Adamant Vigil, intended as scouts and spies for the black dragonflight, were destroyed as they awakened from their stasis by the Primalists who freed Raszageth. Only their leader, Scale­commander Emberthal, survived, and she remains in the Forbidden Reach searching for slumbering dracthyr creches.

The Dark Talons, trained to be an elite force of destruction feared by enemies of the black dragonflight, left the Dragon Isles and warned @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowTheHorde00000]{the Horde} of the danger posed by Raszageth. They later allied with the Horde.

The Ebon Scales, honed as a destructive force, rebelled against the dragons. The weyrn’s leader, Scalecommander Sarkareth, tried to reconstruct the Oathbinder and subjugate all dracthyr once more. After Sarkareth’s death, Scalecommander Emberthal took up the work of reawakening more creches of slumbering dracthyr.

The Healing Wings, trained in the healing arts to give hope to the allies of the dragonflights, remained in the Dragon Isles.

The Obsidian Warders, charged with defending the allies of the black dragonflight and protecting its strongholds, journeyed to Stormwind City to warn the Alliance and subsequently joined forces with that faction.

Dracthyr Renown.name: Dracthyr Renown
Dracthyr Renown.text: Choose one of the following weyrns to align yourself with: the Dark Talons, the Ebon Scales, the Healing Wings, or the Obsidian Warders. If you choose the Dark Talons (Horde) or the Obsidian Warders (Alliance), your Renown Score with the chosen faction begins at 3. If you choose a different weyrn, your Renown Score with the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowValdrakkenAcc]{Valdrakken Accord} begins at 3.

Draenei.name: Draenei
Draenei.text:
@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.PXimkHC7QsxCedEL classes="hide-in-embed noborder"]

Long ago, on the world of Argus, the magically gifted people called eredar drew the attention of Sargeras, the Destroyer of Worlds. @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowTheWorldOfWar.JournalEntryPage.dn81eZPF7h2vuK8O#the-pantheon]{Sargeras} offered untold power to the three leaders of the eredar—Kil’jaeden, Archimonde, and Velen—in exchange for their unquestioning loyalty. A troubling vision soon came to Velen, who saw the eredar transformed into unspeakable demons as members of @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowConflictsOfAz.JournalEntryPage.mOeoKWAu3OOx8LP9]{the Burning Legion}, a force that would grow immense and decimate all life. Despite Velen’s warnings, Kil’jaeden and Archimonde accepted Sargeras’s offer. Velen despaired at his former friends’ decision and prayed for help. To his surprise and relief, he was answered by the benevolent @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowTheWorldOfWar.JournalEntryPage.39WbPfMoJEVvbg15#naaru]{naaru}. These energy beings had, like Velen, foreseen the formation of the Legion.

The naaru offered to shepherd Velen and his followers to safety. Velen quietly gathered eredar who seemed trustworthy. As Sargeras came to Argus and transformed many willing eredar into demons, Velen and his followers narrowly escaped their home world. Furious, Kil’jaeden vowed to track Velen to the ends of creation. Even as the Burning Legion chased Velen across the cosmos, the naaru instructed the exiles, now dubbed draenei (or “exiled ones”), in the way of the Light. Deeply affected, the draenei vowed to honor the Light and uphold the naaru’s ideals. In time the draenei settled on a remote world and met the orcs who inhabited it. The draenei came to call their new home Draenor or “Exiles’ Refuge.”

Kil’jaeden eventually learned of the idyllic world and its unsuspecting inhabitants. Working through the shaman Ner’zhul, the demon lord corrupted the orcs, who began slaughtering the peaceful draenei. When Ner’zhul refused to serve the Legion’s agenda past a certain point, Kil’jaeden turned to Ner’zhul’s apprentice, Gul’dan, who worked the orcs into a frenzy of bloodlust. The orc campaign against the draenei was brutally effective. Over eighty percent of the draenei population was destroyed, though a small group of survivors remained.

Velen and most of the remaining draenei survivors eventually gained control of a dimensional ship called the Exodar and used it to escape to Azeroth. In @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowTheAlliance00]{the Alliance}, they found aid in their battle against the Burning Legion.

If you choose the draenei or Lightforged draenei Eredar Lineage, your Renown Score with the Exodar (Alliance) begins at 3. Otherwise, you have no starting Renown Score.

Krokul.name: Krokul
Krokul.text: The draenei known as Krokul (which means “Broken” in the Draenei language) are remnants of the original eredar who were neither preserved by the naaru, as the draenei were, nor transformed into demons, as the man’ari eredar were, but were corrupted by fel energies. Some of these Krokul never left their original home world of Argus, others remain on the shattered remnants of Draenor (now called Outland), and a few entered Azeroth.

Lightforged Draenei.name: Lightforged Draenei
Lightforged Draenei.text: When Velen and the draenei left their home world of Argus, they traveled from world to world for millennia to avoid Kil’jaeden and the Burning Legion. Eventually, some draenei decided to stop fleeing and take the fight back to the Legion. Led by the naaru Xe’ra, these draenei formed the Grand Army of the Light, which grew over time to include many other foes of the Burning Legion. The draenei most committed to this crusade underwent a ritual to become Lightforged, infusing their bodies with the essence of the Holy Light. Their appearance transformed to reflect this essence: Their eyes turned golden, and their bodies were marked with glowing golden tattoos.

Man’ari Eredar.name: Man’ari Eredar
Man’ari Eredar.text: The man’ari eredar are those who followed Kil’jaeden and Archimonde and joined the Burning Legion, becoming demons. After the imprisonment of Sargeras at the end of the Burning Legion’s third invasion of Azeroth, a group of these eredar, called the Penitents, sought to atone for their vast misdeeds. This group’s leader, Arzaal, appealed to Prophet Velen—not for forgiveness, but for an opportunity to demonstrate the sincerity of the eredar’s repentance. Arzaal proved himself by returning a powerful artifact of the naaru to Velen’s safekeeping. Now some of these Penitents cooperate with their draenei kin in service to the Alliance.

Draenei Renown.name: Draenei Renown
Draenei Renown.text: If you choose the draenei or Lightforged draenei Eredar Lineage, your Renown Score with the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowTheAlliance00.JournalEntryPage.xwHnObtfS8KGOgNp]{Exodar} (Alliance) begins at 3. Otherwise, you have no starting Renown Score.

Speed: 30 feet

Druid.name: Druid
Druid.text:
@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.CccTwPzRbG4HvkHB caption=false cite=false classes="size-three margin-center noborder"]

The first druids learned the secrets of nature magic from the demigod Cenarius, who tutored the yaungol (ancestors of the tauren) and then the night elves in druidic ways.

Druids harness the vast powers of nature to preserve balance and protect life. They unleash nature’s raw energy against their enemies, raining celestial fury on them from a distance, binding them with enchanted vines, or ensnaring them in unrelenting cyclones. Druids are also accomplished shape-shifters, choosing different beast forms to fill a variety of roles in and out of combat.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.XchOMOwpmp21H3mE caption=false classes="noborder"]

Playing a Druid.name: Playing a Druid
Playing a Druid.text:
To play a druid, choose the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.classes.Item.phbdrdDruid00000]{Druid} class from the Player’s Handbook. You can choose one of four specializations to guide your choice of subclass, spells, and feats: balance, feral, guardian, or restoration.

Adopting the Druid class, either at character creation or through multiclassing, increases a character’s Renown Score with the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowCenarionCircl]{Cenarion Circle} by 3 (see chapter 4).

Balance Specialization

By leveraging the sacred powers of the moons, the sun, and the stars, balance druids keep the elemental forces of the cosmos in an equilibrium. To that end, they wield both celestial spells that deal Radiant damage and nature-oriented spells that deal Acid, Lightning, or Poison damage, striving to keep the world and its celestial powers in balance. They use the shape-shifted form of a @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowBestiaryOfAze.JournalEntryPage.FUL6IFSLhMuSEOnm]{moonkin}—an owlbear-like creature favored by the moon goddess Elune (see chapter 7)—to heighten their attunement to these natural forces.

The following choices will help you focus on this specialization:

Level 1. Choose Magician for your Primal Order feature. Choose the following cantrips: @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplDruidcraft]{Druidcraft}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplStarryWisp]{Starry Wisp}, and @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.spells.Item.wowsplWrath00000]{Wrath} (see “Druid Spells”). Prepare the following level 1 spells to start: @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplCureWounds]{Cure Wounds}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplEntangle00]{Entangle}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.spells.Item.wowsplMoonfire00]{Moonfire} (see “Druid Spells”), and @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplThunderwav]{Thunderwave}.

Level 3. Choose the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.classes.Item.phbdrdCirstars00]{Circle of the Stars} subclass. When you use Starry Form, you can take on the appearance of a moonkin, but the other effects are identical.

Feats. Consider the following feats at higher levels: @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftElementalAd]{Elemental Adept} and @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftWarCaster00]{War Caster}.

Feral Specialization

To feral druids, nature is an eternal dance between predator and prey, with death an integral part of the cycle that sustains life. These druids seek deeper understanding of this truth by pursuing a visceral connection to the wild. Their favored shape-shifted form is a deadly feline predator—a ferocious, agile stalker that rips, bites, and bleeds enemies dry.

The following choices will help you fill the feral druid’s role:

Level 1. Choose Warden for your Primal Order feature. Choose the following cantrips: @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplDruidcraft]{Druidcraft} and @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplPoisonSpra]{Poison Spray}. Prepare the following level 1 spells to start: @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplCureWounds]{Cure Wounds}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplEntangle00]{Entangle}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplSpeakwithA]{Speak with Animals}, and @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplThunderwav]{Thunderwave}.

Level 3. Choose the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.classes.Item.phbdrdCirmoon000]{Circle of the Moon} subclass. When you use Wild Shape, you can adopt the Cat Form stat block below.

Feats. Consider the following feats at higher levels: @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftSkulker0000]{Skulker}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftSlasher0000]{Slasher}, and @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftSpeedy00000]{Speedy}.

Guardian Specialization

Guardian druids commune with the wild to better understand how life perseveres through adversity. These druids deeply value steadfastness and meet danger with fierce resistance. They prefer the shape-shifted form of a great bear—a massive wall of fur, claws, teeth, and rage aided by the magic of nature to protect their allies from danger.

The following choices will help you focus on this specialization:

Level 1. Choose Warden for your Primal Order feature. Choose the following cantrips: @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplDruidcraft]{Druidcraft} and @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplThornWhip0]{Thorn Whip}. Prepare the following level 1 spells to start: @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplEntangle00]{Entangle}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplHealingWor]{Healing Word}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplSpeakwithA]{Speak with Animals}, and @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplThunderwav]{Thunderwave}.

Level 3. Choose the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.classes.Item.phbdrdCirmoon000]{Circle of the Moon} subclass. When you use Wild Shape, you can adopt the Bear Form stat block above.

Restoration Specialization

Restoration druids tend to the life-forms of the world, celebrating birth and growth in search of order and harmony. Where there is decay and devastation, these druids bring rejuvenation and regrowth. Life, in their view, needs not only protection, but also nourishment. To that end, they bond with living and growing things, seeking inspiration from the flower’s bloom, the seed’s sprout, the mushroom’s spores, and the tree’s towering growth.

Like nature itself, restoration druids persevere through patience, and they wield their nature-given power to mend wounds and protect their allies.

The following choices will help you focus on this specialization:

Like a dragon’s visage, a druid’s beast form reflects something of their true nature.

—Chromie

Choose the following cantrips: @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplDruidcraft]{Druidcraft}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplProduceFla]{Produce Flame}, and @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplSparetheDy]{Spare the Dying}. Prepare the following level 1 spells to start: @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplCureWounds]{Cure Wounds}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplEntangle00]{Entangle}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplGoodberry0]{Goodberry}, and @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplHealingWor]{Healing Word}.

Level 3. Choose the Circle of the Land subclass.

Classic Druid Beast Forms

The beast forms that every druid in World of Warcraft learns are @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowCatFormP40sJ8]{Cat Form}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowBearForm17Lnh]{Bear Form}, and Travel Form (including Aquatic Form and Flight Form).

Cat Form. If you have the Circle of the Moon subclass, use the Cat Form stat block described above. If not, you can become a @UUID[Compendium.dnd-monster-manual.actors.Actor.mmPanther0000000]{Panther} at level 2 and a @UUID[Compendium.dnd-monster-manual.actors.Actor.mmTiger000000000]{Tiger} at level 8.

Bear Form. If you have the Circle of the Moon subclass, use the Bear Form stat block described above. If not, you can become a @UUID[Compendium.dnd-monster-manual.actors.Actor.mmBlackBear00000]{Black Bear} at level 4 and a @UUID[Compendium.dnd-monster-manual.actors.Actor.mmBrownBear00000]{Brown Bear} at level 8.

Travel Form. You can become an @UUID[Compendium.dnd-monster-manual.actors.Actor.mmElk00000000000]{Elk} starting at level 2. For fast swimming, consider a @UUID[Compendium.dnd-monster-manual.actors.Actor.mmGiantSeahorse0]{Giant Seahorse} starting at level 4 (or level 3 for the Circle of the Moon). When you gain access to flying forms at level 8, you can become an @UUID[Compendium.dnd-monster-manual.actors.Actor.mmEagle000000000]{Eagle}, a @UUID[Compendium.dnd-monster-manual.actors.Actor.mmGiantBat000000]{Giant Bat}, a @UUID[Compendium.dnd-monster-manual.actors.Actor.mmHawk0000000000]{Hawk}, a @UUID[Compendium.dnd-monster-manual.actors.Actor.mmPteranodon0000]{Pteranodon}, or a @UUID[Compendium.dnd-monster-manual.actors.Actor.mmRaven000000000]{Raven}.
