Introduction.name: Introduction
Introduction.text: The rest of this chapter presents six iconic dungeons from World of Warcraft as adventure locations for your Dungeons & Dragons game. Here are a few things to bear in mind about the dungeon experience in D&D.

Encounter Building.name: Encounter Building
Encounter Building.text:
The dungeons presented here are less detailed than you’d find in a dedicated adventure product but more fleshed out than a simple adventure site. Each dungeon is intended for five characters within a certain tier of play. Naturally, characters at the higher end of that tier will have an easier time than characters at the lower end. Use the encounter-building guidelines in the Dungeon Master’s Guide to craft encounters of appropriate difficulty.

These dungeons are populated with a mix of monsters from the Monster Manual and @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowBestiaryOfAze]{chapter 7} of this book alongside dungeon bosses with unique stat blocks. Many of those bosses have traits that cause them to transform or revitalize during a fight, replicating the familiar MMO pattern of a boss battle with distinct phases. In effect, fighting these bosses is like fighting two or even three encounters and gives the characters a commensurate reward.

Along similar lines, use judgment when awarding treasure from the treasure tables in this chapter. Feel free to overrule the dice if they indicate a treasure no character will use, and choose specific armor and weapon types to match the characters’ preferences.

Pace of Play.name: Pace of Play
Pace of Play.text: The pace of play in a tabletop game is different from in an MMO. Exploring a dungeon like the ones described in this chapter is a task that might take several sessions of play for the real people around the game table and days for their characters. While WoW characters can quickly refresh their resources after a fight and enter every boss battle fresh, D&D characters need to take time to rest, regain expended spell slots, restore their Hit Points, and otherwise recuperate from the activities of adventuring. They might be able to rest safely in the dungeon, or they might retreat from the dungeon to make camp outside the entrance.

Pillars of Play.name: Pillars of Play
Pillars of Play.text: A D&D adventure—even one that centers around a dungeon—relies on the three pillars of play described in the Player’s Handbook: @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.content.JournalEntry.phbSocialInterac]{social interaction}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.content.JournalEntry.phbExploration00]{exploration}, and @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.content.JournalEntry.phbCombat0000000]{combat}. Expect players to examine the books on the shelves in the library, talk to neutral or even enemy nonplayer characters, and search for creative ways to bypass obstacles or encounters. Don’t cling too tightly to how you think an adventure is supposed to go, and reward the players for clever ideas even if that means skipping over large parts of the adventure you expected to run.

Renown.name: Renown
Renown.text: Many of the adventure hooks presented for these dungeons include parenthetical notes about the potential for earning renown with the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowFactionsAndRe]{factions} by completing quests in these dungeons. Use characters’ established relationships with these factions to flesh out the adventure hooks and draw characters naturally into their adventures.

Dwarf.name: Dwarf
Dwarf.text:
Eons ago, the titans built the World Forges—the Forge of Wills in Ulduar and the Forge of Origination in Uldum—to strengthen and stabilize the slumbering Worldsoul of Azeroth. In addition, the Forge of Wills drew on the life essence of Azeroth to give shape and sentience to creatures of living stone and metal, including the kindhearted earthen and the clockwork mechagnomes. These titan-forged beings helped the titans shape the world of Azeroth, laying a groundwork of order that would allow the Worldsoul to mature and flourish.

But the Old God Yogg-Saron, imprisoned beneath Ulduar, devised a plan to weaken its jailers and escape imprisonment: It would corrupt the Forge of Wills, tainting its creation matrix with a malady called the curse of flesh, which would make the titan-forged mortal. As this curse slowly spread and infected the earthen, many of them asked to be placed in hibernation until a cure could be found. Keeper Archaedas sealed them within the subterranean realm of Uldaman, promising to rouse them in the future.

Uncounted ages later, most of the mechagnomes tending the slumbering earthen had succumbed to the curse of flesh, becoming gnomes, and either died of old age or ventured out into the world. The last gnome guarding Uldaman awakened the sleepers, and these first dwarves found themselves in a new world. Drawn to a mountain range to the west, these hardy folk settled in the snowy region of Dun Morogh. There, they carved out the proud city of Ironforge, which became the seat of a great and mighty nation that stretched deep under the mountains. For more than two thousand years, Ironforge prospered, bolstered by trade partnerships with the human-built city-states to the north.

Then, about 230 years before the opening of the Dark Portal, long-simmering tensions among the three powerful clans of Ironforge erupted into war as the clans vied for dominion of the mountain in the War of the Three Hammers. In the end, the Bronzebeard clan used its martial expertise to drive the other clans—the Dark Irons and the Wildhammers—from the mountain range.

Bronzebeard Dwarves.name: Bronzebeard Dwarves
Bronzebeard Dwarves.text: The Bronzebeard clan was the largest of Ironforge’s three factions and formed the bulk of its military and mercantile classes. The clan ruled Ironforge for over 250 years after driving the Dark Iron and Wildhammer clans from the city, until King Magni Bronzebeard was transformed into living crystal during the Cataclysm. Now Ironforge is governed by the Council of Three Hammers, with representatives of all three clans.

Dark Iron Dwarves.name: Dark Iron Dwarves
Dark Iron Dwarves.text: The Dark Iron clan inhabited the deepest and darkest corners of Ironforge, and the Dark Irons’ dabbling in sinister magic and their penchant for secrecy and political scheming cost them the other clans’ trust. Sorcerer-Thane Thaurissan controlled Ironforge’s richest gem and mineral deposits and leveraged his wealth to protect his people. After the War of the Three Hammers, Thaurissan led the Dark Iron clan south to the Redridge Mountains and founded a kingdom bearing his name. After an ill-fated attempt to conquer the other clans, Thaurissan brought doom on himself and his people by summoning Ragnaros the Firelord, who enslaved the Dark Iron dwarves for more than two centuries in Blackrock Mountain. Following Ragnaros’s defeat after the Cataclysm, Queen-Regent Moira Thaurissan led her people to rejoin Ironforge. She now sits on the Council of Three Hammers alongside Bronzebeard and Wildhammer representatives. The Dark Iron clan has also become a proud member of the Alliance.

Frostborn.name: Frostborn
Frostborn.text: Though they weren’t among the dwarves who first emerged from Uldaman and thus weren’t part of the original kingdom of Ironforge, the Frostborn dwarves of Northrend consider themselves friendly cousins of the other clans. They descend directly from a different group of @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowEarthen000000]{earthen} in Northrend who succumbed to the curse of flesh.

Wildhammer Dwarves.name: Wildhammer Dwarves
Wildhammer Dwarves.text: Before the War of the Three Hammers, the Wildhammer clan inhabited the craggy hills and icy slopes outside Ironforge and were considered rustic and uncouth by the other clans. After their defeat in the war, the Wildhammers established the fortress of Grim Batol in the highlands east of the Wetlands. When the Dark Iron clan launched a new assault on its kin, Queen Modgud Thaurissan unleashed a terrible curse that left Grim Batol a nightmarish ruin, and the Wildhammers settled in the mountains of Lordaeron, crafting the city of Aerie Peak in the Hinterlands. There they learned to train gryphons for use in war and travel. High Thane Falstad Wildhammer now represents the clan on the Council of Three Hammers in Ironforge.

Dwarf Traits.text: You have the Dwarf species traits from the Player’s Handbook.

Earthen.name: Earthen
Earthen.text:
@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.06gqCX3VsPbB8ivx classes="hide-in-embed noborder"]

The titans created the earthen eons ago in the Forge of Wills, and the earthen helped the titans shape the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowWorldOfAzerot]{world of Azeroth} so its Worldsoul could flourish. The earthen specialized in carving out caverns beneath the surface of the world. Many of them succumbed to Yogg-Saron’s curse of flesh and became dwarves, but sizable populations of earthen remain in Uldaman (beneath the Badlands), Ulduar (in the Storm Peaks in Northrend), and Khaz Algar, as well as in Deepholm in the Elemental Plane.

In Khaz Algar, earthen are stirred from stasis by a device called the Awakening Machine. This device was long shut down and later corrupted, and only recently did the dwarf Magni Bronzebeard channel the power of Azeroth into the machine to restore it to its proper function. In its new configuration, the Awakening Machine allows newly awakened earthen to choose their own fate, rather than being bound to instructions handed down from the titans of old. These awakened earthen often leave Khaz Algar to explore Azeroth, and many of them have allied themselves with @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowTheAlliance00]{the Alliance} or @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowTheHorde00000]{the Horde}.

Earthen resemble dwarves whose bodies are made from living stone and infused with Azerite, the lifeblood of Azeroth itself. Large crystalline structures jut from their bodies, and fine mineral structures resembling hair adorn their heads and faces. They don’t need to eat, but consuming certain minerals can provide benefits—including changes to the growth of the hairlike minerals on their heads.

Speed: 30 feet

Introduction.name: Introduction
Introduction.text:
The Earthen Ring is a gathering of Azeroth’s most powerful shaman, working together to preserve the balance among the elements. The members of the Earthen Ring oppose destructive forces such as the Twilight’s Hammer cult, the rampaging black dragon Deathwing, and the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowConflictsOfAz.JournalEntryPage.mOeoKWAu3OOx8LP9]{Burning Legion}, and they work tirelessly to heal the wounds inflicted on Azeroth by such forces. Insisting on a neutral stance in mortal conflicts (and a generally Neutral alignment), the Earthen Ring welcomes members from both the Alliance and the Horde, though the peoples of the Alliance—particularly @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowDraenei000000]{draenei}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowDwarf00000000.JournalEntryPage.cyFq9ds161YyDy5W]{Wildhammer dwarves}, and humans of @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowHuman00000000.JournalEntryPage.b5Jfulr9rBcvQYN9]{Kul Tiras}—are recent additions to the organization. It also includes murlocs, the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowDraenei000000.JournalEntryPage.NCzAEGbEJZUjmcqZ]{Krokul draenei}, and other druids who haven’t chosen a side in the Alliance–Horde conflict.

The Earthen Ring is governed by the Elder Council, which gathers at a shrine perched at the edge of the Maelstrom called the Heart of Azeroth. The order also maintains a ritual circle just outside Stormwind’s walls (the Eastern Earthshrine) and another above Orgrimmar (the Western Earthshrine). Both circles include portals leading to the Elemental Plane and other areas of Earthen Ring activity, which Earthen Ring shaman allow only those who are at least Honored with the faction to use.

Adopting the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.classes.Item.phbbrbBarbarian0]{Barbarian} class (as a @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowShaman0000000]{shaman}; see chapter 1), either at character creation or through multiclassing, increases a character’s Renown Score with the Earthen Ring by 3.

Earthen Ring Renown Perks.name: Earthen Ring Renown Perks
Earthen Ring Renown Perks.text:
Increasing your Renown Score with the Earthen Ring gives you the following additional benefits.

Earthen Ring: Friendly

Prerequisite: Renown 3+ with the Earthen Ring

You can spend 30 days with a trainer to learn the Kalimag language (see the “Training” sidebar earlier in this chapter). Elementals that haven’t been corrupted by the Old Gods are Friendly to you by default.

Earthen Ring: Honored

Prerequisite: Renown 10+ with the Earthen Ring

You can freely use the portals located in the Eastern and Western Earthshrine.

Additionally, if you spend a Long Rest in an Earthen Ring sanctuary, you gain the Charm of the Earthen Ring, which allows you to cast Summon Elemental. The Charm vanishes from you once used three times, after 7 days, or if your Renown Score with the Earthen Ring falls below 10.

Earthen Ring: Revered

Prerequisite: Renown 25+ with the Earthen Ring

You receive the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.items.Item.wowBlessingEarth]{Blessing of the Earthen Ring}. The Blessing enables you to take a Magic action to summon an @UUID[Compendium.dnd-monster-manual.actors.Actor.mmAirElemental00]{Air Elemental}, an @UUID[Compendium.dnd-monster-manual.actors.Actor.mmEarthElemental]{Earth Elemental}, a @UUID[Compendium.dnd-monster-manual.actors.Actor.mmFireElemental0]{Fire Elemental}, or a @UUID[Compendium.dnd-monster-manual.actors.Actor.mmWaterElemental]{Water Elemental}. The elemental appears in an unoccupied space you choose within 30 feet of yourself, obeys your commands, and takes its turn immediately after you on your Initiative count. The elemental disappears after 1 hour, when it dies, or when you dismiss it as a Bonus Action. You can’t use this Blessing again until the next dawn. You lose the Blessing if your Renown Score with the Earthen Ring falls below 25.

Earthen Ring: Exalted

Prerequisite: Renown 50+ with the Earthen Ring

You receive the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.items.Item.wowBlessingFarse]{Blessing of the Farseer}. The Blessing gives you the benefits of a @UUID[Compendium.dnd-dungeon-masters-guide.equipment.Item.dmgRingOfElement]{Ring of Elemental Command} linked to an Elemental Plane of your choice. When you finish a Long Rest, you can change the plane it’s linked to. You lose the Blessing if your Renown Score with the Earthen Ring falls below 50.

Elf.name: Elf
Elf.text:
@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.SUv2jFVKXCyuTuJS classes="hide-in-embed noborder"]

In ancient ages, night elves founded a vast empire that spanned the world. But as Queen Azshara and the elite Highborne nobles of her court delved into the secrets of arcane magic, using spells to manipulate the cosmic energy of the Well of Eternity, the elves drew the attention of the titan Sargeras, creator of the demonic @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowConflictsOfAz.JournalEntryPage.mOeoKWAu3OOx8LP9]{Burning Legion}. Sargeras convinced Azshara and her loyal high councilor, Xavius, to open a portal that would allow the Legion to enter the world. The resulting conflict, the War of the Ancients, brought all the young peoples of the world together—night elves, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowTauren0000000]{tauren}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowBestiaryOfAze.JournalEntryPage.gpaXzuJeSb0dZxx6]{furbolgs}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowEarthen000000]{earthen}, dragons, and @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowTheWorldOfWar.JournalEntryPage.Jm2kfPalxs8mphjd#wild-gods]{Wild Gods}—to repel the Burning Legion. But the price of closing the portal was the Great Sundering, which shattered the continent into the landmasses of the world today. The Great Sea covered the heart of the ancient continent, and the site of the Well of Eternity is now the swirling Maelstrom.

Just as the continent was shattered in the Great Sundering, the elves were scattered and divided by the cataclysmic event. The Highborne who sided with Azshara were transformed into @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowBestiaryOfAze.JournalEntryPage.Tog74lVhgL5a8Jo6]{naga} and @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowBestiaryOfAze.JournalEntryPage.4yblb5rRbngox4cD]{satyrs}, while those who resisted her continued to pursue arcane magic. The rest of the night elves remained isolated for ten thousand years.

Night Elves (Kaldorei).name: Night Elves (Kaldorei)
Night Elves (Kaldorei).text:
Forswearing the use of arcane magic, the night elves (or kaldorei, which means “children of the stars” in their own language, Darnassian) cultivated a druidic society in the shadowed recesses of Ashenvale Forest. But the return of the Burning Legion shattered the tranquility of their ancient civilization. Though once again victorious against their ancient foes, the night elves were forced to sacrifice their immortality and watch their beloved forests burn.

In the aftermath of the horrific conflict, archdruid Malfurion Stormrage and high priestess Tyrande Whisperwind helped their people rebuild their shattered villages. Although some night elves slowly adjusted to their mortal existence, many couldn’t accept the prospects of aging, disease, and frailty. Seeking to regain their immortality, a number of wayward druids conspired to plant a special tree that would reestablish a link between their spirits and the eternal world. Malfurion warned against it, but his spirit became lost in the depths of the Emerald Dream, and his fellow archdruid Fandral Staghelm planted the great tree Teldrassil off the stormy coasts of northern Kalimdor.

Night elves average between 7 and 8 feet in height. Their skin is generally a shade of purple, from pale lilac to dark violet. Their hair is blue, violet, green, orange, black, or white, and their eyes glow white, blue, or gold. Facial tattoos are a mark of adulthood in night elf culture.

Nightborne (Shal’dorei).name: Nightborne (Shal’dorei)
Nightborne (Shal’dorei).text:
The city of Suramar was one of the jewels of the ancient kaldorei empire, home to Illidan and Malfurion Stormrage, the priestess Tyrande Whisperwind, and other leaders of the empire. During the War of the Ancients, the Highborne of Suramar created the Nightwell to mimic the power of the Well of Eternity, and they used it to create a magical shield that protected the city from the outside world for ten thousand years. The Great Sundering isolated Suramar on the remote Broken Isles, far from potential intruders. During this long period of isolation, the residents of Suramar were transformed by the energy of the Nightwell, becoming the nightborne.

With the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowConflictsOfAz.JournalEntryPage.mOeoKWAu3OOx8LP9]{Burning Legion}’s third attempt to invade Azeroth, the magical barrier protecting Suramar fell, and the leaders of the city allied with the demons. A rebellion among the populace toppled those corrupt leaders, and the nightborne joined the ranks of @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowTheHorde00000]{the Horde}.

Nightborne resemble night elves, though their skin is darker and grayer.

High Elves (Quel’dorei).name: High Elves (Quel’dorei)
High Elves (Quel’dorei).text:
Following the War of the Ancients, the surviving Highborne (outside of Suramar) lived among their kin in northern Kalimdor. However, some of them refused to abandon their practice of arcane magic. To protest the law banning such magic, a group of Highborne, led by a mage named Dath’Remar Sunstrider, called down an arcane storm on Ashenvale. The night elves’ leaders sent the Highborne into exile, and Dath’Remar led them across the sea to the Eastern Kingdoms, where they established the nation of Quel’Thalas (meaning “High Home” in Thalassian) around a font of magic called the Sunwell.

The elves of Quel’Thalas were on reasonable terms with their neighbors and joined the Alliance of Lordaeron (albeit reluctantly) during the Second War. But during the Third War, the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowConflictsOfAz.JournalEntryPage.YRwQ3wrLM22odUUP]{Scourge} decimated the population of Quel’Thalas. Most of the survivors took on the name “blood elves” (see below) and adopted parasitic techniques to sustain themselves without the Sunwell. However, a few survivors refused to use those techniques, and they were exiled from Quel’Thalas as a result. Now known as high elves, they live among the other peoples of the Alliance in the Eastern Kingdoms, with no nation of their own.

High elves are about 6 feet tall with redder skin and hair tones than their night elf kin, reflecting their affinity for the sun. High elves’ eyes glow blue.

Blood Elves (Sin’dorei).name: Blood Elves (Sin’dorei)
Blood Elves (Sin’dorei).text:
With the destruction of the Sunwell during the Third War, most of the survivors of Quel’Thalas took on the name “blood elves” (sin’dorei, or “children of the blood” in Thalassian) to honor their fallen kindred. Since the Sunwell could no longer sustain them, they learned a technique to drain arcane energy from other living creatures.

In the aftermath of the Third War, the blood elves found aid from the unlikeliest of sources: the undead elf Sylvanas Windrunner, the former Ranger-General of Silvermoon who defended Quel’Thalas from the Scourge but was transformed into an undead servant of the Lich King. As the leader of the undead Forsaken, she helped bring the blood elves into the Horde.

Recent years have seen unprecedented changes within Quel’Thalas. The blood elves, following the will of their leader, Kael’thas Sunstrider, channeled dangerous, chaotic magic to transform the Sunwell into a gateway of unspeakable evil. While Kael’thas and his demonic masters were eventually defeated, a fallen naaru sacrificed its life essence to reignite the Sunwell as a font of arcane and holy energy. The blood elf regent, Lor’themar Theron, sees it as a new source of hope for his people.

Blood elves resemble high elves, but their eyes glow green or gold.

Void Elves (Ren’dorei).name: Void Elves (Ren’dorei)
Void Elves (Ren’dorei).text:
Many have sought to harness the corruptive magic of @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowTheWorldOfWar.JournalEntryPage.39WbPfMoJEVvbg15]{the Void}—the force of infinite hunger that stands in opposition to the Light and is embodied in the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowConflictsOfAz.JournalEntryPage.QX2LRHkL98AMmC55]{Old Gods}. Most who tried have lost their grip on the reality of the material world. When a group of blood elves devoted themselves to studying the Void, they were deemed a threat to the newly restored Sunwell and exiled from Silvermoon City.

The high elf Alleria Windrunner was the first elf to defy the whispers of the Void, thanks to the instruction of a powerful being called the Locus-Walker. Determined to use the Void’s power for the good of Azeroth, she sought out the exiles from Silvermoon and trained these elves, now known as void elves, to control the shadows within themselves. Thanks to her leadership, the void elves pledged their support to the Alliance.

Void elves resemble high elves, but their eyes glow violet, and their hair is varying shades of purple and blue. Some void elves have tentacles sprouting from their heads and woven into their hair, reflecting the influence of the Void.

Evoker.name: Evoker
Evoker.text:
@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.lAbP7Vdf3fJMCql0 caption=false cite=false classes="size-three margin-center noborder"]

Evokers wield the magic of the five ordered dragonflights (detailed in chapter 7)—the chaotic flames of the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowBestiaryOfAze.JournalEntryPage.DmsSoir1i1hgTyRj]{red flight}, the focused magic of the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowBestiaryOfAze.JournalEntryPage.g0t7ZVVSG0Vr7TGr]{blue flight}, the might of the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowBestiaryOfAze.JournalEntryPage.jnGTp7LiVzQO8DTY]{black flight}, the life-giving spirit of the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowBestiaryOfAze.JournalEntryPage.wWBP2j6xQk2Tc6AZ]{green flight}, and the time-bending magic of the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowBestiaryOfAze.JournalEntryPage.TzC2d1YrqOCcuCk4]{bronze flight}. Evokers channel this power to devastate their enemies and bolster their allies, using their heightened mobility to dart in and out of the fray.

Evokers can empower, extend, and transmute their spells to suit their needs. They can also charge up their spellcasting, entering a state of heightened magical power.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.ZDfxONwrNEBq8nRD caption=false classes="noborder"]

Playing an Evoker.name: Playing an Evoker
Playing an Evoker.text:
Evoker is a hero class, which means you typically start play at level 3 or higher (see the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowDeathKnight00.JournalEntryPage.gL82O0Vn607HF94R#hero-classes]{Hero Classes} sidebar earlier in this chapter). To play an evoker, choose the Sorcerer class from the Player’s Handbook and the Draconic Sorcery subclass at level 3. Instead of the Draconic Spells subclass feature, you gain the Evoker Spells feature, described below. You can use one of three specializations to guide your choice of class features, spells, Metamagic options, and feats: augmentation, devastation, or preservation.

Creating an Evoker

When you add the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.classes.Item.phbscrSorcerer00]{Sorcerer} class to your character sheet you will be given the option to pick between the Sorcerer and the Evoker.

All evokers in World of Warcraft are @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.origins.Item.wowspDracthyr000]{dracthyr}, so check with your DM before playing an evoker of another species.

Evoker Spells

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.classes.Item.wowsrcEvokerSpel inline]

Augmentation Specialization

Evokers who specialize in augmentation imbue their companions with the might of the black dragonflight, amplifying those allies’ abilities. They can also bend time and fate to their advantage using the magic of the bronze dragonflight.

The following choices will help you focus on this specialization:

Level 3. Choose the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.classes.Item.phbscrDraconicSo]{Draconic Sorcery} subclass, and see “Evoker Spells” above. Choose the following cantrips: @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplElementali]{Elementalism}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplLight00000]{Light}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplSorcerousB]{Sorcerous Burst}, and @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplThundercla]{Thunderclap}. Choose the Augmentation spells from the Evoker Spells table and the following additional prepared spells: @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplArcaneVigo]{Arcane Vigor}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplEnhanceAbi]{Enhance Ability}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplFlamingSph]{Flaming Sphere}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplIceKnife00]{Ice Knife}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.spells.Item.wowsplLivingFlam]{Living Flame} (see “New Evoker Spells”), and @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplShield0000]{Shield}. Choose Empowered Spell and Extended Spell for your Metamagic options.

Level 6. Choose Fire for your Elemental Affinity.

Feats. Consider the following feats at higher levels: @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftElementalAd]{Elemental Adept} (Fire), @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftSpeedy00000]{Speedy}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftSpellSniper]{Spell Sniper}, and @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftWarCaster00]{War Caster}.

Devastation Specialization

The devastation specialization uses the chaotic flames of the red dragonflight and the precise arcane power of the blue dragons to bathe the battlefield in destruction. Devastation evokers can rain fire down from the sky on their foes and maneuver quickly around the battlefield.

The following choices will help you focus on this specialization:

Level 3. Choose the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.classes.Item.phbscrDraconicSo]{Draconic Sorcery} subclass, and see “Evoker Spells” above. Choose the following cantrips: @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplElementali]{Elementalism}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplLight00000]{Light}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplRayofFrost]{Ray of Frost}, and @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplSorcerousB]{Sorcerous Burst}. Choose the Devastation spells from the Evoker Spells table and the following additional prepared spells: @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplArcaneVigo]{Arcane Vigor}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplBurningHan]{Burning Hands}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplCloudofDag]{Cloud of Daggers}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplFlameBlade]{Flame Blade}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplIceKnife00]{Ice Knife}, and @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.spells.Item.wowsplLivingFlam]{Living Flame} (see “New Evoker Spells”). Preservation Specialization

Evokers who specialize in preservation wield the power of the Emerald Dream—the fey realm of verdant life tended by the green dragonflight—to rejuvenate injured allies. They also use bronze dragons’ magic to manipulate the sands of time, preventing harm and rewinding injury.

The following choices will help you focus on this specialization:

Choose the following cantrips: @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplBladeWard0]{Blade Ward}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplElementali]{Elementalism}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplLight00000]{Light}, and @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplSorcerousB]{Sorcerous Burst}. Explorers’ League and Reliquary.name: Explorers’ League and Reliquary
Explorers’ League and Reliquary.text:
Affiliated with @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowTheAlliance00]{the Alliance} and @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowTheHorde00000]{the Horde} respectively, the Explorers’ League and the Reliquary are scholarly organizations dedicated to the practice of archaeology and the study of history, seeking to understand the origins of life and culture on Azeroth.

Magni Bronzebeard, the king of Ironforge, founded the Explorers’ League by decree after dwarf-led expeditions uncovered surprising facts about the dwarves’ connection to the ancient titans. Declaring that learning this history was more important than mining and engineering, Magni directed the Explorers’ League to focus on archaeological work and plumbing the secrets of the ancient world. The league quickly expanded its scope to encompass natural history as well as the history of all Azeroth’s peoples, and it soon accepted citizens of other Alliance nations as members. High Explorer Muninn Magellas is the leader of the Explorers’ League, and the organization’s headquarters remains in Ironforge, in the Hall of Explorers.

The Reliquary, in contrast, began as an effort to harness the power of ancient relics for the benefit of the blood elves and their allies in the Horde. The leader and founder of the Reliquary, Tae’thelan Bloodwatcher, believed such artifacts should be carefully studied, not feared. Tae’thelan’s ultimate goal in founding the Reliquary was to free the blood elves from their magical addiction and reunite them. When the blood elves joined the Horde, the Reliquary opened its membership to all members of the Horde, but its headquarters (also called the Reliquary) remains in Silvermoon City.

Mutually Hostile Factions

World of Warcraft features many opposing factions that are so hostile to each other that any renown gain with one faction automatically results in a loss of renown with the other. The Explorers’ League and the Reliquary were mutually hostile before they were forced to cooperate in exploring the Dragon Isles. Other examples include the Scryers and the Aldor of Shattrath City, as well as the Frenzyheart Tribe of wolvar and the gorlock Oracles of Sholazar Basin. In situations like these, a character’s Renown Score with a faction can drop below 0, which means members of that faction are &Reference[Hostile] to the character by default.

Relic Rivals.name: Relic Rivals
Relic Rivals.text:
Despite their different origins (and different alignments, corresponding to the difference between the Alliance and the Horde), the Explorers’ League and the Reliquary use similar methods and often vie for access to the same sites. For most of recent history, the organizations were bitter rivals, with the tension between them often erupting into violent conflict. During this time, the factions are mutually hostile (see the @UUID[.VEve4LTFSXRVNVFs#mutually-hostile-factions]{Mutually Hostile Factions} sidebar).

However, with the reemergence of the Dragon Isles and the subsequent discovery of Khaz Algar, the two organizations have set aside their old rivalry and formed joint expeditions. During this period, a character’s Renown Score with either faction applies to both factions, so having a Renown Score of 3+ with either one makes members of both factions Friendly by default.

Explorers' League and Reliquary Renown P.name: Explorers' League and Reliquary Renown Perks
Explorers' League and Reliquary Renown P.text:
Increasing your Renown Score with either the Explorers’ League or the Reliquary gives you the following additional benefits. Characters can’t increase their Renown Score with both factions; typically, characters affiliated with the Alliance work with the Explorers’ League and Horde characters work with the Reliquary.

Explorers’ League/Reliquary: Friendly

Prerequisite: Renown 3+ with the Faction

You can spend 30 days with a trainer to learn any language from the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowCharacterOrig.JournalEntryPage.yATa67jopmTEXeiG]{language tables} in chapter 2 or gain proficiency in History (see the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowTheAlliance00.JournalEntryPage.atJHGssGcTvG0dWQ]{Training} sidebar earlier in this chapter).

Explorers’ League/Reliquary: Honored

Prerequisite: Renown 10+ with the Faction

When you gather @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowProfessionsAn.JournalEntryPage.ywSgJFsinrEDfTDk#archaeology]{archaeology fragments} from a dig site, you gain one additional fragment on a successful check, and you have Advantage on Intelligence (History) checks to assemble fragments into a complete relic.

Explorers’ League/Reliquary: Revered

Prerequisite: Renown 25+ with the Faction

If you spend 7 days studying the relics in the Hall of Explorers in Ironforge or the Reliquary in @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowTheHorde00000.JournalEntryPage.2EWR8vxGjhK2Dq6O]{Silvermoon City} (or some other significant Explorers’ League or Reliquary facility, at the DM’s discretion) and then finish a Long Rest there, you gain a Charm that lasts for 7 days or until you use it. You can’t gain another Charm from this feature while you still have one. The effect of the Charm depends on the origin of the relics you study; you can choose one of the following options:

@UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.items.Item.wowCharmofDraehf]{Charm of Draenor}. While you have this Charm, you know Draenei and Orcish. You can expend the Charm to cast @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplConjureMin]{Conjure Minor Elementals}.

@UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.items.Item.wowCharmofPand0R]{Charm of Pandaria}. While you have this Charm, you know the Pandaren language. You can expend the Charm to cast @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplGaseousFor]{Gaseous Form}, targeting yourself. The effect lasts for 1 hour or until you end the effect as a Bonus Action.

@UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.items.Item.wowCharmBurninAE]{Charm of the Burning Legion}. While you have this Charm, you know the Eredun language. You can expend the Charm to cast @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.spells.Item.wowsplRainFire00]{Rain of Fire} (level 4 version).

@UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.items.Item.wowCharmHighbo6e]{Charm of the Highborne}. While you have this Charm, you know Thalassian. You can expend the Charm to cast @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplCharmMonst]{Charm Monster}.

@UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.items.Item.wowCharmOldGodty]{Charm of the Old Gods}. While you have this Charm, you know Shath’Yar. You can expend the Charm to cast @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplSummonAber]{Summon Aberration}.

@UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.items.Item.wowCharmTitanFJ8]{Charm of the Titan-Forged}. While you have this Charm, you know Titan. You can expend the Charm to gain Resistance to all damage for 1 minute as your flesh takes on a mineral appearance.

@UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.items.Item.wowCharmZandalV6]{Charm of the Zandalari}. While you have this Charm, you know Zandali. You can expend the Charm to cast @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplSummonBeas]{Summon Beast} (level 4 version). The summoned Bestial Spirit resembles a loa.

Explorers’ League/Reliquary: Exalted

Prerequisite: Renown 50+ with the Faction

You can request the use of a powerful magic item stored in your organization’s vaults to assist you for a single adventure that is relevant to your organization’s interests and aims. It takes 7 days for top agents in your organization to retrieve the item, which can be any Legendary magic item of your choice (subject to the DM’s discretion). If the item isn’t consumable, you must return it at the conclusion of the adventure, or your Renown Score decreases by [[/r 2d12]]. Once you use this benefit, you can’t do so again until your Renown Score with your organization increases.

Introduction.name: Introduction
Introduction.text:
@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.zuwoUs1ZGHdmY7AZ]

Azeroth is defined by its factions—nations, organizations, cartels, and pacts that claim members from around the world. As characters interact with these factions, they can build a reputation and earn tangible and intangible rewards.

This chapter builds on the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-dungeon-masters-guide.content.JournalEntry.dmgDmsToolbox000.JournalEntryPage.QnYXlS4TpZlmqSt2]{renown rules} found in the Dungeon Master’s Guide to track characters’ standing with the major factions of Azeroth. In addition, characters might gain renown with smaller groups to achieve short-term goals. World of Warcraft offers abundant examples that can be adapted into a tabletop campaign. For example, characters seeking a route from Felwood into Winterspring might work to gain renown with the furbolgs of Timbermaw Hold, who will allow passage through their tunnels once at least one member of the party has achieved a Renown Score of 10+.

The New Faction Actor and Renown

The D&D5E 6.1.0 release introduced the Faction actor, Renown item, and a system for tracking Renown at the individual character level and at the Party level. The Renown system adds a new tab to your Player Character and Group sheets when it is enabled. To enable the Renown system change to the Settings tab, press the Welcome Screen button, and check the Renown Scores option in the window that opens. A new tab will appear in your Player Character and Group sheets where you can find any Renown items that have been granted to them.

Each Renown item allows you to increase or decrease their Renown with one or more Factions. Whenever you create a new Faction they will automatically be visible in the select box. While this module is active you can also align each Faction with the Alliance or the Horde.

Species and classes which grant a bonus to Renown will automatically grant them and the bonuses to renown that are earned from reaching certain thresholds are handled by the module as well. You can control whether or not that occurs with the Subfaction Renown setting in your Game Settings.

Renown items can serve as a great way to track what your players have accomplished, who they've helped, and who may hold a grudge against them.

General Renown Perks.name: General Renown Perks
General Renown Perks.text:
The perks listed here apply to all the factions described in this chapter:

Friendly (Renown 3+). Other members of the faction are Friendly to you by default.

Honored (Renown 10+). You can purchase equipment found in the Player’s Handbook, as well as Common or Uncommon magic items, from merchants of the faction at a 10% discount.

Revered (Renown 25+). Your discount increases to 15% and extends to Rare magic items.

Exalted (Renown 50+). Your discount increases to 25% and extends to Very Rare magic items.

Certain @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowMountsAndVehi]{mounts} and magic items are available only from merchants associated with a particular faction and might require a minimum Renown Score with that faction to purchase.

Starting Renown.name: Starting Renown
Starting Renown.text: Most characters created using the origins in @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowCharacterOrig]{chapter 2} have a starting Renown Score of 3 with one of the subfactions associated with either @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowTheAlliance00]{the Alliance} or @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowTheHorde00000]{the Horde}. A few species and class options give starting Renown Scores with other factions.

Forsaken.name: Forsaken
Forsaken.text:
@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.LDFi6mSCR2UY3O4O classes="hide-in-embed noborder"]

The vast undead armies of the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowConflictsOfAz.JournalEntryPage.YRwQ3wrLM22odUUP]{Scourge} were created by the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowConflictsOfAz.JournalEntryPage.mOeoKWAu3OOx8LP9]{Burning Legion} to prepare @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowWorldOfAzerot]{Azeroth} for its second invasion. Under the command of the dread Lich King, the Scourge spread terror and destruction across the world while conquering Northrend and devastating Lordaeron, the northern portion of the Eastern Kingdoms. But after the Third War, the Lich King’s will faltered, and many of the Scourge broke free from his ironfisted control. Under the leadership of the banshee Sylvanas Windrunner, these renegades took the name of Forsaken and carved out a new existence in a world where no one welcomed them.

With Sylvanas as their Banshee Queen, the Forsaken built a stronghold beneath the ruins of Lordaeron’s former capital city—a hidden Undercity that formed a sprawling labyrinth beneath Tirisfal Glades. From there, they entered an uneasy alliance with the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowOrc0000000000]{orcs} and @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowTauren0000000]{tauren} of @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowTheHorde00000]{the Horde}.

Sylvanas regarded the Horde as nothing more than a useful tool, even when she took up its leadership as warchief. After the Fourth War, she abandoned the Forsaken and the Horde, leaving her people under the leadership of a Desolate Council meant to represent the diverse viewpoints of the Forsaken populace.

Like the armies of the Scourge, the Forsaken are undead, with their souls imperfectly attached to their bodies through magic. They feel only faint sensations of pain or discomfort, but the presence of the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowTheWorldOfWar.JournalEntryPage.39WbPfMoJEVvbg15#church-of-the-holy-light]{Holy Light} is sharply painful to them. Most of them were formerly human, but they consider themselves a singular people regardless of their past existences. Some of them are pale and stiff but with bodies whole enough to pass as living, while others are thoroughly rotted or mummified.

Size: Medium (about 4–7 feet tall) or Small (about 2–4 feet tall), chosen when you select this species
Speed: 30 feet

As a Forsaken, you have these special traits.

Darkvision. You have &Reference[Darkvision] with a range of 60 feet.

Gnome.name: Gnome
Gnome.text:
@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.ea9Y6FpVmKSNbSIw classes="hide-in-embed noborder"]

When the titans built the World Forges to empower the slumbering Worldsoul of Azeroth, they also used the Forge of Wills in Ulduar to draw on the Worldsoul to give shape and sentience to the titan-forged: @UUID[.4OFFV6SmsonDI0kZ]{mechagnomes}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowEarthen000000]{earthen}, vrykul, and others. The titans intended mechagnomes to be servants and caretakers, and the mechagnomes fulfilled this duty as the world took shape.

But Ulduar and its Forge of Wills were also the prison that bound the Old God Yogg-Saron deep beneath the earth, and the Old God schemed to weaken its jailers so it could escape. It corrupted the Forge of Wills, tainting the forge’s creation matrix with the curse of flesh, which would make the titan-forged mortal. Most of the mechagnomes succumbed to this curse, becoming gnomes and abandoning their assigned tasks. Those who had labored in Uldaman spread throughout the snowy mountains to the west, eventually carving out the fortress of Gnomeregan in the mountains of Dun Morogh.

As generations passed, the gnomes dedicated themselves to technological advancement as a means to survive in a harsh world. They became obsessed with developing radical new technologies and constructing marvels of mind-bending engineering. Over the years, the gnomes have contributed ingenious weapons to aid @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowTheAlliance00]{the Alliance} in its fierce battles against @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowTheHorde00000]{the Horde}.

During the Third War, Gnomeregan came under attack from below, as vicious troggs assailed the city. Though the gnome defense forces staged a valiant defense, they couldn’t save their wondrous city. At the command of High Tinker Gelbin Mekkatorque, the gnomes opened the pressure valves of their massive grinding machines and released toxic radiation throughout the city. Not only did the radiation fail to kill the troggs, the gnomes soon discovered that it killed their own people instead. Nearly eighty percent of the population of Gnomeregan died within days. Most of the survivors fled to the protection of their dwarf cousins in Ironforge. In the years since, gnomes have labored to reclaim Gnomeregan from the mutated gnomes that inhabit it and render it fit for habitation once again.

Mechagnome.name: Mechagnome
Mechagnome.text: Many mechagnomes eluded the curse of flesh and remained mechanical. However, a new group of mechagnomes descends from gnomes who settled Mechagon Island in hopes of discovering useful titan technology. These gnomes performed extensive experiments to reverse the curse of flesh and become living machines. After facing the perils of full mechanization, they found the ideal balance between flesh and steel. Now reunited with their gnome cousins, these new mechagnomes bring both tenacity and ingenuity to @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowTheAlliance00]{the Alliance}.

Gnome Traits.name: Gnome Traits
Gnome Traits.text: You have the Gnome species traits from the Player’s Handbook, with the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.origins.Item.phbspRockGnome00]{Rock Gnome} lineage. If you are a Mechagnome, you instead have the traits below.

Goblin.name: Goblin
Goblin.text:
@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.Ij4QLB6yq2q6tcwK caption=false classes="hide-in-embed noborder"]

In distant eons, Keeper Mimiron discovered kaja’mite, a strange ore with magical properties, and the Keeper’s experiments resulted in the creation of goblins from some unknown precursor species. Many centuries later, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowTroll00000000.JournalEntryPage.Ml9ilvzEchsOsCqI]{Zandalari trolls} came to the Isle of Kezan and found both goblins and kaja’mite there. The trolls originally paid the goblins to mine the precious ore for them, but eventually they enslaved the goblins and forced them into this backbreaking labor.

Over the course of centuries, the goblins secretly used engineering and alchemy to craft weapons, traps, and explosives and wielded them to overthrow their troll oppressors. The goblins drove the trolls from Kezan and reclaimed the island.

The goblins of Kezan celebrated their freedom by turning on each other, forming cartels that vied for control of the island. What began as violent conflict soon simmered down into mercantile rivalry as the cartels established lucrative trade across @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowWorldOfAzerot]{Azeroth}, selling their weaponry and other feats of technology to the highest bidder.

Though one cartel sided with the orcs during the Second War, most goblins remained neutral in the Alliance–Horde conflict. Under the leadership of the cartels and their trade princes, the goblins created a paradise for themselves throughout the nearby islands. Their ingenious feats of engineering and vast trade fleets made Kezan one of the great technological wonders of the world.

However, the rise of Deathwing in the great Cataclysm caused the volcano at the heart of Kezan to erupt. Goblins fled the island in droves, and the fate of the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowTheHorde00000.JournalEntryPage.KTz4fgoqdKuVuqzy]{Bilgewater Cartel} in particular was changed forever by a chance encounter. A ship carrying Bilgewater refugees from Kezan sailed into the midst of a one-sided battle between an Alliance fleet and a single Horde warship, and the Alliance destroyed the goblin vessel along with the Horde one. The Bilgewater goblins found themselves washed up on shore with none other than Thrall, former Warchief of the Horde. The goblins helped Thrall and the other Horde survivors repel further Alliance attacks, and ultimately the Bilgewater Cartel settled in Azshara and aligned itself with the Horde.

Goblin Cartels.name: Goblin Cartels
Goblin Cartels.text:
Besides the Bilgewater Cartel, three other cartels remain a significant mercantile force across Azeroth:

Blackwater Cartel. Originally a pirate group affiliated with the Steamwheedle Cartel, the Blackwater Cartel runs the town of Booty Bay in Stranglethorn. Its operations focus on shipping, trade, transport, and tourism, though the cartel still engages in smuggling and piracy on the side.

Steamwheedle Cartel. After allying with the Horde in the Second War, the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowSteamwheedleC]{Steamwheedle Cartel} realized that even greater profits were possible if the cartel remained neutral in future conflicts, making its goods and services available to anyone who can pay. This careful neutrality has led to tremendous financial success. From its capital, Gadgetzan in Tanaris, the cartel oversees operations across Azeroth and even beyond.

Venture Company. The Venture Company is notorious for plundering natural resources across Azeroth without regard to the consequences for the environment. It specializes in gathering raw materials—anything that can be dug up, chopped down, drilled out of the earth, or blown out of a mountainside. The Venture Company also deals in illegal arms and smuggles animals, and cartel members both employ mercenaries to guard their operations and broker mercenary services to others.

Though many believed all of Kezan was destroyed in the Cataclysm, the sprawling subterranean city of Undermine survived the volcanic eruption and still serves as the goblins’ capital. There, the Bilgewater Cartel, Blackwater Cartel, Steamwheedle Cartel, and Venture Company maintain a significant presence and vie for dominance.

Goblin Renown.name: Goblin Renown
Goblin Renown.text: Choose a cartel: @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowTheHorde00000.JournalEntryPage.KTz4fgoqdKuVuqzy]{Bilgewater Cartel}, Blackwater Cartel, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowSteamwheedleC]{Steamwheedle Cartel}, or Venture Company. If you are associated with the Bilgewater Cartel (Horde) or the Steamwheedle Cartel, your Renown Score with that faction begins at 3. Otherwise, you have no starting Renown Score.

Haranir.name: Haranir
Haranir.text:
@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.VybwM0d4qReL0BVw classes="hide-in-embed noborder"]

Haranir are reclusive people who dwell in the magical forests of Harandar, a subterranean realm where the roots of the World Trees grow together. Their ancient druidic traditions connect them to the earth and teach them to protect the roots that reach into the deep places where they dwell.

Haranir have little contact with the surface world and its peoples, and they are reluctant to share the details of their traditions with strangers. They have long avoided even allowing other peoples to know of their existence, striving to stay out of sight and conceal traces of their presence.

Haranir bear a passing resemblance to both night elves and trolls. They have tusks (smaller than trolls’), bat-like ears, and grayish-purple skin with patches of fur or sharp quills. They tend to favor clothing made from leaves and thorns.

Haranir Traits.name: Haranir Traits
Haranir Traits.text:
Creature Type: Humanoid
Size: Medium (about 7–8 feet tall)
Speed: 30 feet

As a Haranir, you have these special traits.

Darkvision. You have &Reference[Darkvision] with a range of 120 feet.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.origins.Item.wowsptGiftWorldT caption=false cite=false nameStyle=inline]

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.origins.Item.wowsptHaranirMag caption=false cite=false nameStyle=inline]

Human.name: Human
Human.text:
@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.TgIJPj89OSlwDQIv classes="hide-in-embed noborder"]

Humans are descended from the vrykul of North­rend, who are in turn the result of the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowConflictsOfAz.JournalEntryPage.QX2LRHkL98AMmC55]{Old Gods}’ curse of flesh taking hold of the titan-forged iron vrykul. Born small and weak as a result of the curse, humans were often killed by their vrykul parents, but some parents took the children to Lordaeron, where the humans formed scattered tribes and, under pressure from the expanding @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowTroll00000000.JournalEntryPage.AdBTf7AxlTOG09N7]{Amani empire of trolls}, eventually united into the Empire of Arathor.

After several centuries, the prosperous city-states of Arathor split into the Seven Kingdoms: Alterac, Dalaran, Gilneas, @UUID[.b5Jfulr9rBcvQYN9]{Kul Tiras}, Lordaeron, @UUID[.O9p7hdJXavAFDVD8]{Stromgarde}, and @UUID[.592An0ENopmrf0AR]{Stormwind} far to the south. After orcs from Draenor opened the Dark Portal and invaded Azeroth, Stormwind was destroyed, and the survivors fled north. The leaders of the Seven Kingdoms united as the Alliance of Lordaeron to battle the orcs, alongside the dwarves and gnomes of Khaz Modan and the high elves of Quel’Thalas. After the Second War, humans rebuilt Stormwind City—a testament to perseverance in the face of disaster.

The kingdom of Lordaeron suffered a near-fatal blow with the coming of the plague of undeath, which killed countless people and transformed them into mindless undead servants of the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowConflictsOfAz.JournalEntryPage.YRwQ3wrLM22odUUP]{Scourge}. The lands once claimed by Lordaeron are now the Plaguelands, and few remnants of the human empire’s glories remain.

With Lordaeron and Alterac fallen, the magocracy of Dalaran removed from the Eastern Kingdoms and then destroyed, and Gilneas afflicted with the curse of the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowWorgen0000000]{worgen}, Stormwind stands now as the strongest bastion of humanity on Azeroth and the most powerful force in the Alliance. Kul Tiras has rejoined the Alliance, and Stromgarde struggles to rebuild its strength after years of conflict against the Horde, the Scourge, and a group of ruffians called the Syndicate.

Stormwind.name: Stormwind
Stormwind.text: Law-abiding humans of the kingdom of Stormwind (whose holdings extend across Elwynn Forest, Westfall, Duskwood, and the Redridge Mountains) hold fast to the principles of honor and justice as they defend their settlements and the Alliance against aggressors. But countless other humans engage in banditry, plot rebellion, or scheme with sinister forces such as the Cult of the Damned to bring about the end of the world.

Kul Tiras.name: Kul Tiras
Kul Tiras.text: The Admiralty of Kul Tiras is known for its strong seafaring tradition, its legendary naval fleet, and its far-reaching merchant ships. After the Third War, Lord Admiral Daelin Proudmoore led the Kul Tiran fleet in an invasion of Durotar, which led to his death. Following that tragedy, Kul Tiras withdrew from all involvement in the outside world. In its isolation, a civil war brewed as two of the four ruling houses conspired against a third, House Proudmoore. At the same time, the powerful tide­sages of the isles were corrupted by the influence of the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowConflictsOfAz.JournalEntryPage.QX2LRHkL98AMmC55]{Old Gods}. As @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowTheAlliance00]{the Alliance} entered the Fourth War against @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowTheHorde00000]{the Horde}, it sent emissaries in an effort to bring Kul Tiras back into the Alliance. Only after its internal conflicts were resolved did Kul Tiras, now under the leadership of Lord Admiral Jaina Proudmoore, support the Alliance.

Dalaran.name: Dalaran
Dalaran.text: Dalaran was founded during the height of the Empire of Arathor and eventually became a haven for mages and a center of magical learning. Governed by the mages of the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowKirinTor00000]{Kirin Tor}, Dalaran attracted scholars and spellcasters from across the Eastern Kingdoms. During the Third War, the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowConflictsOfAz.JournalEntryPage.YRwQ3wrLM22odUUP]{Scourge} razed Dalaran, but in the war’s aftermath, the survivors rebuilt the city. During the war against the Lich King, the Kirin Tor used mighty magic to levitate the city high in the air where no ground assault could ever reach it again and positioned it in the skies over Crystalsong Forest in Northrend. Since then, it was relocated multiple times—first above Karazhan in Deadwind Pass, then to the Broken Isles, then above the Isle of Dorn in Khaz Algar, where it was destroyed. The survivors of that final attack are now settled in Dornogal, and the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowKirinTor00000]{Kirin Tor} remains a powerful force in the defense of Azeroth from all threats.

Stromgarde.name: Stromgarde
Stromgarde.text: During the Fourth War, descendants of the fallen kingdom of Stromgarde rebuilt their old capital in the Arathi Highlands, Stromgarde Keep, and their long-exiled king reclaimed his throne. Though the Horde fought bitterly to prevent it, the Alliance ultimately claimed victory and regained this important foothold in Lordaeron.

Arathi Empire.name: Arathi Empire
Arathi Empire.text: Centuries ago, a group of humans from the city-states of Arathor and a group of high elves from Quel’Thalas launched an exploratory expedition across the Storming Sea. In an unknown land far to the east, they founded a new Arathi Empire. The modern inhabitants of this empire all share mixed human and elf descent, calling themselves simply Arathi rather than human or elf. Most of them look predominantly human except for their slightly pointed ears. The official religion of the Arathi Empire is the church of the Sacred Flame, a fiery expression of the Holy Light, and the divine emperor rules with the aid of prophetic visions. After years of isolationg from the nations of Azeroth, a group of Arathi recently came to Khaz Algar in service to one of the emperor’s visions, and they have made contact with their long-sundered kin there.

Hunter.name: Hunter
Hunter.text:
@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.C6GtI8L4RP2434Fg caption=false cite=false classes="size-three margin-center noborder"]

From an early age, some adventurers hear the call of the wild drawing them from the comfort of their homes into the unforgiving outdoors. Those who endure become hunters. These masters of their environment slip like ghosts through the trees and lay traps in their enemies’ paths.

Many hunters have pets that attack while the hunters nock their arrows, fire their guns, or ready their polearms. Hunters are highly mobile, evading or restraining foes to control the arena of battle.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.UCOczkbGCQsw2YoR caption=false classes="noborder"]

Playing a Hunter.name: Playing a Hunter
Playing a Hunter.text:
To play a hunter, choose the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.classes.Item.phbrgrRanger0000]{Ranger} class from the Player’s Handbook. You can choose one of three specializations to guide your choice of subclass, spells, and feats: beast mastery, marksmanship, or survival.

Beast Mastery Specialization

From childhood, many hunters have formed profound bonds with the beasts of the wild. These hunters specialize in beast mastery. They are drawn to the primal world and invigorated by the dangerous wilds. Wilderness landscapes become their homes, and ferocious predators become their kin. To aid them in hunting and in battling foes, these hunters summon and command a wide array of vicious animals to fight at their side.

The following choices will help you focus on this specialization:

Level 1. Choose the following prepared spells: @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplEnsnaringS]{Ensnaring Strike} and @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplSpeakwithA]{Speak with Animals}. Choose any two of Heavy Crossbows, Longbows, or Muskets for your Weapon Mastery feature.

Level 2. Choose @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbfstArchery000]{Archery} for a Fighting Style feat.

Level 3. Choose the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.classes.Item.phbrgrBeastMaste]{Beast Master} subclass. See @UUID[.jtLGmq7XRMpXSgLI]{Hunter Pets} below.

Level 6. Instead of the Roving class feature, you gain the Pet Specialization feature (see below).

Feats. Consider the following feats at higher levels: @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftCrossbowExp]{Crossbow Expert}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftMediumArmor]{Medium Armor Master}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftPiercer0000]{Piercer}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftSharpshoote]{Sharpshooter}, and @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftWeaponMaste]{Weapon Master}.

Marksmanship Specialization

Some hunters forgo the companionship of a wild beast, preferring to blend into the natural environment as they wield ranged weapons with deadly skill. Specializing in marksmanship, these hunters learn techniques for stalking and ambushing their prey by observing the deadliest predators of the wilds. They prefer to remain in hiding as they unleash their shots with deadly precision.

The following choices will help you focus on this specialization:

Level 1. Choose the following prepared spells: @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplCureWounds]{Cure Wounds} and @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplEnsnaringS]{Ensnaring Strike}. Level 2. Choose @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbfstArchery000]{Archery} for a Fighting Style feat.

Survival Specialization

Some hunters are drawn to the most brutal aspects of nature: the unrelenting ferocity of predatory animals and the merciless bloodshed that means survival for the strongest. These hunters prefer close-quarters combat, wielding spears and polearms to bring down their prey. They call on the aid of beast companions, coat their weapons with venom, and lay deceptive traps.

Hunter Pets.text:
As a Beast Master (whether you choose the beast mastery or survival specialization), when you use your Primal Companion feature to summon a primal beast, you choose the form it takes from among the pet families shown on the table below. Each family has three characteristics:

Stat Block. Your primal beast’s family determines which one of the stat blocks in the Player’s Handbook it uses: Beast of the Land, Beast of the Sea, or Beast of the Sky.

Specialization (Spec.). Each pet family has a specialization—Cunning (C), Ferocity (F), or Tenacity (T)—that comes into play only if you have the Pet Specialization feature.

Mastery Property (Mastery). When you gain the Primal Companion feature and whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can choose your pet’s family as one of the weapons for your Weapon Mastery feature. Then its mastery property applies to your primal companion’s Beast’s Strike attack.
