Chromie's Letter.name: Chromie's Letter
Chromie's Letter.text:
@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.wZ551gBNhys0P9Ey classes="float-right size-three noborder"]

Welcome, adventurer! You’ve come just in the nick of time. I am known as Chronormu, but you can call me Chromie. I am comfortable with such familiarity. But perhaps you already knew that. Have we met before, or am I simply remembering that we shall meet again?

You see, I am one of the bronze dragonflight, forever attuned to the ebb and flow of time. My job is to keep tabs on certain timelines——the really important ones——to make sure things unfold the right way. Which is to say, the way they already unfolded. Or is it the way they will unfold?

Anyway, can you keep a secret? The truth is, messing with time is actually super fun. What if two fierce rivals never met? What if they teamed up and became a heroic duo? What if they fell in love but their romance was forbidden by their families? So many possibilities.

So this codex is something I whipped up as a fun way to explore all those what-if questions without risking any actual damage to the timelines. With this book, we can delve into the secrets of Azeroth like never before! Together, we can jump into these pages to view different versions of Azeroth’s past, present, and future as if we were really there!

Oh, and don’t worry! I’m almost entirely sure that this codex is absolutely, nearly one hundred percent stable! There’s practically no chance of your adventures causing any significant snarls in any important timestreams.

So what do you say? Adventure awaits!

——Chromie

Worlds Collide.name: Worlds Collide
Worlds Collide.text:
This book is a union of two worlds in more than one sense: D&D: World of Warcraft is the meeting of the multiverse of D&D with the world of Azeroth (and connected realms), as well as the meeting of the world of tabletop roleplaying games with the world of massively multiplayer online roleplaying games. This fruitful collaboration brings new dimensions to your exploration of the world of Azeroth and new ideas to your D&D gaming table.

To make best use of this book, you need the Dungeons & Dragons Player’s Handbook, Dungeon Master’s Guide, and Monster Manual. But you can also get started with the resources available on DnDBeyond.com, including ready-made characters and free basic rules.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.GaGujiyThO26REPy caption=false classes="noborder"]

What Is World of Warcraft?.name: What Is World of Warcraft?
What Is World of Warcraft?.text:
World of Warcraft (WoW) is a massively multiplayer online roleplaying game (MMORPG, usually shortened to MMO)—an online video game where many, many people enter into a fantasy world, through the avatars of their characters, and explore that world in groups or independently. From the perspective of a D&D player, WoW is a treasure trove of lore and inspiration—a world that feels both familiar and uniquely new. Adventurers of familiar species such as elves and dwarves travel alongside less familiar folk such as pandaren and tauren. And the history of WoW’s night elves, blood elves, and three main dwarf clans—and the dwarves’ ties to the ancient titans—sets them apart from their counterparts
in D&D.

With over twenty years of the World of Warcraft MMO (plus multiple real-time strategy games in the Warcraft line before that), the story of the world of Azeroth is long and deep. This book only scratches the surface of that rich lore. The official World of Warcraft website (worldofwarcraft.blizzard.com) offers a starting point where you can learn more about the world and the MMO, while fan-made wikis—readily discoverable in any online search engine—carefully chronicle the details of these decades of stories. The “Where to Learn More” sidebar includes a list of resources to help you learn more about the world of Azeroth.

Inside This Book.name: Inside This Book
Inside This Book.text:
D&D: World of Warcraft is a guide to creating characters and adventures in the world of Azeroth.

@UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowCharacterClas]{Chapter 1} focuses on the thirteen character classes in the World of Warcraft MMO. Each is presented in alphabetical order, with an explanation of how to build and play that class as a D&D character. That explanation points you to one of the twelve classes in the D&D Player’s Handbook, but it includes alterations, new options, and guidance to reflect WoW classes and their specializations. So whether you want to re-create the fury warrior you play in the MMO or make a new character, this chapter is your starting point for playing WoW classes in D&D.

@UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowCharacterOrig]{Chapter 2} focuses on character origins, particularly species. Each playable species in the MMO is described here. Some species use rules described in the D&D Player’s Handbook, while other species have new rules. Whether you’re playing a human or a vulpera, this chapter has the information you need.

@UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowProfessionsAn]{Chapter 3} covers rules and options related to character professions—both gathering and crafting—as well as @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowMountsAndVehi]{mounts}, pets, and new @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowMagicItems000]{magic items}.

@UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowFactionsAndRe]{Chapter 4} details important factions of Azeroth, starting with the Alliance and the Horde and their subfactions. The chapter expands on the renown rules in the D&D Dungeon Master’s Guide to map out the rewards you can gain as you build your reputation with these factions.

@UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowTheWorldOfWar]{Chapter 5} is a brief overview of the world of Azeroth. It includes a summary of each region of the world, suggestions for the kinds of adventure to be found in those locations, and a glimpse at the worlds and planes beyond Azeroth.

@UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowAdventuresInA]{Chapter 6}, intended solely for the Dungeon Master, focuses on crafting adventures in the world of Azeroth. It outlines the world’s major conflicts and encourages the DM to mix and match those conflicts to create unique adventures and campaigns. It then presents several familiar dungeons from the World of Warcraft MMO for characters to explore.

@UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowBestiaryOfAze]{Chapter 7}, also intended for the Dungeon Master, includes descriptions and stat blocks for new monsters and important nonplayer characters (NPCs) from the World of Warcraft MMO. From dragons of the five ordered dragonflights and demons of the Burning Legion to lowly murlocs and furbolgs, this bestiary supplements the D&D Monster Manual to provide new adversaries and potential allies for characters in a World of Warcraft D&D campaign. And if characters want to join forces with Thrall or Jaina and test their mettle against Illidan or Arthas, this chapter provides stat blocks for those legendary characters, among others.

As Chromie suggests at the start of this introduction, this book helps you make Azeroth your own. Just as you would when you start any D&D campaign, you can adapt elements in this book to fit the way you want to play. Chromie has given you a separate timeline as your playground, so make of it whatever you will!

Where to Learn More

The books listed here are a great place to dive more deeply into the lore of Azeroth:

World of Warcraft: Chronicle. The four volumes in this series offer a comprehensive look at the history of Azeroth and Draenor, covering the stories of every game in the Warcraft franchise and each World of Warcraft expansion.

World of Warcraft: Exploring Azeroth. This five-book series—Eastern Kingdoms, Kalimdor, North­rend, Pandaria, and Islands & Isles—surveys the world of Azeroth, providing more detail on the regions mentioned in chapter 5 of this book.

World of Warcraft: Grimoire of the Shadowlands and Beyond. This book provides a tour of the Shadowlands—Warcraft’s mysterious afterlife.

World of Warcraft: The Dragonflight Codex. This book offers a comprehensive guide to the dragons of Azeroth, as well as to the Dragon Isles.

In addition to these reference books, dozens of novels, short stories, audio dramas, animations, and comics in both the Warcraft and the World of Warcraft lines tell the stories of Azeroth in narrative form.

Creating a Character.name: Creating a Character
Creating a Character.text:
Take care of yourself out there.

—Chromie

Making a D&D character to explore the world of Azeroth follows the same steps outlined in the Player’s Handbook, but this book provides additional options you can select throughout the process:

1: Choose a Class. Use the descriptions of World of Warcraft classes in chapter 1 to guide your class selection.

2: Determine Origin. Choose a background from the Player’s Handbook and a species from chapter 2. These two elements can combine in interesting ways to make unique origins. Also note your starting Renown Score, if any, from your species.

3: Determine Ability Scores. Use the Player’s Handbook to guide you in this step.

4: Choose an Alignment. The peoples of the Alliance tend toward Lawful Good alignments, while those of the Horde tend toward Chaotic Good. See chapter 4 for more information.

5: Fill in Details. Use the Player’s Handbook to guide you in this step.

Creating a World of Warcraft character

When you add a class to your character sheet you will be given the option to pick between the World of Warcraft version of the class and the default Player's Handbook/SRD version of the class.

Note: There is a Customize Classes setting in your Game Settings which controls whether or not the World of Warcraft version of the class icon is used or the default icon from the Player's Handbook/SRD.

What is D&D?.name: What is D&D?
What is D&D?.text:
@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.3fUA6bp6DTgvzeSA caption=false classes="banner-bottom noborder"]

This book is a setting supplement for Dungeons & Dragons, the original and still the greatest tabletop roleplaying game (TRPG). If you’re familiar with the World of Warcraft online game, you already know the basic idea of D&D: Players create characters and explore a fantasy world, using magic and weapons to overcome obstacles and defeat enemies. But the action in D&D takes place primarily in the players’ imaginations at a physical or virtual game table. One player takes on the role of Dungeon Master (DM), providing narration that sets the scene and determining the outcomes of the player characters’ actions.

If you’re a WoW fan, this book invites you to take your exploration of the world of Azeroth to a new level. As you travel across Kalimdor or the Eastern Kingdoms, sail to Northrend or the Dragon Isles, and venture into the dungeons detailed in this book (or dungeons of your DM’s creation), you can interact with anything you can see, talk to anyone you meet, and try anything you can imagine. And because the game unfolds in the players’ imaginations, anything can happen.

If you play as the DM, this book gives you tools to create your own adventures in Azeroth. Those stories might echo the themes and characters from WoW, or they might draw on existing elements to create entirely new adventures to make Azeroth your own.

Here’s a glimpse of what a D&D game looks like:

Jared (as Dungeon Master): Seated at the table, apparently waiting for you, is a hulking tauren with enormous moose-like antlers. He stands as you enter and says, “Greetings, adventurers. I am Spiritwalker Ebonhorn. Mayla has told me much about you.”

Phillip (as Delenus): Does his name mean anything to me?

Maeve (as Maiatsumi): Can I get a read on this guy? What’s his deal?

Jared: All right, one at a time. Phillip, Delenus is searching his memory for any knowledge of Ebonhorn?

Phillip: Yeah. And what’s a spiritwalker?

Jared: Make an Intelligence check.

Phillip: Does my Religion skill apply?

Jared: Sure, at least as far as what “spiritwalker” means.

Phillip (rolling a d20): Ugh. Seven.

Jared: It must be a Highmountain tauren thing. Means nothing to you. And Maeve, you’re trying to get a read on him?

Maeve: Yeah. Maybe using Insight?

Jared: Sure, make a Wisdom (Insight) check.

Maeve (rolling a d20): Nineteen! Plus … well, plus zero is still nineteen!

The adventure continues from there, relying on the DM’s descriptions to set the scenes and on the players’ decisions to determine how the action unfolds. You can learn more about D&D—including more examples of play, free rules, and ready-to-play characters you can use to start your adventures in Azeroth—by visiting DnDBeyond.com.

Introduction.name: Introduction
Introduction.text:
@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.Ic2S2HgMKUVE74YV caption=false classes="noborder"]

The Kirin Tor began as a secretive mages’ guild within the Empire of Arathor, the first great human civilization of the Eastern Kingdoms. Viewed with suspicion by much of the populace, the mages of Arathor secluded themselves in their own city, Dalaran, which became a beacon to mages from across Azeroth. With the fall of Arathor, Dalaran became a nation in its own right, one of Arathor’s seven successor kingdoms, and the Council of Six who led the Kirin Tor became the rulers of this city-state. Razed during the Third War, Dalaran was rebuilt behind powerful warding spells and later transformed into a flying island that could be relocated to safety when needed. From its original site in the Hillsbrad Foothills, Dalaran moved first to Northrend’s Crystalsong Forest, then above Karazhan in Deadwind Pass, then to the Broken Isles, then above the Isle of Dorn in Khaz Algar. There it met its doom at the hands of Xal’atath’s forces of the Void, but the survivors of the Kirin Tor remain in Dornogal, coordinating the magical defense of Azeroth.

The Council of Six, the leadership of the Kirin Tor, is made up of the most senior members of the Kirin Tor. Its leaders have included Archmage Rhonin, who oversaw the rebuilding of Dalaran after the Third War, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowJainaProudmiL]{Lady Jaina Proudmoore} (see chapter 7), and Archmage Khadgar, who was imprisoned by Xal’atath just before Dalaran’s destruction. The Kirin Tor is generally Lawful Neutral in alignment.

Adopting the Wizard class, either at character creation or through multiclassing, increases a character’s Renown Score with the Kirin Tor by 3.

Kirin Tor Renown Perks.name: Kirin Tor Renown Perks
Kirin Tor Renown Perks.text:
Establishing your Bastion in Dalaran increases your Renown Score with the Kirin Tor by 1.

Increasing your Renown Score with the Kirin Tor gives you the following additional benefits.

Kirin Tor: Friendly

Prerequisite: Renown 3+ with the Kirin Tor

You can enjoy a Modest lifestyle in Dalaran at no cost. You can also request a favor from the archmages of the Kirin Tor, which can take one of the following forms:

  • An archmage casts for you a spell of level 3 or lower at half the usual cost.

  • An archmage provides you with a @UUID[Compendium.dnd-dungeon-masters-guide.tables.RollTable.dmgArcanaCommon0]{Common} or @UUID[Compendium.dnd-dungeon-masters-guide.tables.RollTable.dmgArcanaUncommo]{Uncommon} magic item from the Arcana tables in the Dungeon Master’s Guide at half the usual cost.

  • An archmage spends 30 days teaching you, so you learn a language from the tables in chapter 2 or gain proficiency with a tool (see the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowTheAlliance00.JournalEntryPage.atJHGssGcTvG0dWQ]{Training} sidebar earlier in this chapter).

You can request such a favor a number of times equal to your Renown Score with the Kirin Tor. If your Renown Score falls below the number of favors you have requested, a higher-ranking member of the Kirin Tor might call in a favor from you, sending you on a mission for the organization.

Kirin Tor: Honored

Prerequisite: Renown 10+ with the Kirin Tor

You can enjoy a Comfortable lifestyle in Dalaran at no cost.

If your Bastion is in Dalaran, when you issue the Maintain order to your Bastion, the DM rolls twice on the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-dungeon-masters-guide.tables.RollTable.dmgBastionEvents]{Bastion Events} table and you can pick which event occurs.

In addition, when you request a favor from the Kirin Tor (see “Kirin Tor: Friendly”), it can take one of the following additional forms:

  • An archmage casts for you a spell of level 4 or lower at half the usual cost.

  • An archmage provides you with a @UUID[Compendium.dnd-dungeon-masters-guide.tables.RollTable.dmgArcanaRare000]{Rare} magic item from the Arcana tables in the Dungeon Master’s Guide at half the usual cost.

  • Whenever you take a Bastion turn, you can issue the Research order to the Kirin Tor as if it were a Library facility in your Bastion.

Kirin Tor: Revered

Prerequisite: Renown 25+ with the Kirin Tor

You can enjoy a Wealthy lifestyle in Dalaran at no cost.

In addition, when you request a favor from the Kirin Tor (see “Kirin Tor: Friendly”), it can take one of the following additional forms:

  • An archmage casts for you a spell of level 6 or lower at half the usual cost.

  • An archmage provides you with a @UUID[Compendium.dnd-dungeon-masters-guide.tables.RollTable.dmgArcanaVeryRar]{Very Rare} magic item from the Arcana tables in the Dungeon Master’s Guide at half the usual cost.

  • Whenever you take a Bastion turn, you can issue the Craft order to the Kirin Tor as if it were a @UUID[Compendium.dnd-dungeon-masters-guide.bastions.Item.dmgScriptorium00]{Scriptorium} facility in your Bastion.

Kirin Tor: Exalted

Prerequisite: Renown 50+ with the Kirin Tor

You can enjoy an Aristocratic lifestyle in Dalaran at no cost.

In addition, when you request a favor from the Kirin Tor (see “Kirin Tor: Friendly”), it can take one of the following additional forms:

  • An archmage casts for you a spell of level 8 or lower at half the usual cost.

  • An archmage provides you with a @UUID[Compendium.dnd-dungeon-masters-guide.tables.RollTable.dmgArcanaLegenda]{Legendary} magic item from the Arcana tables in the Dungeon Master’s Guide at half the usual cost.

  • When you craft a magic item, two Kirin Tor apprentices assist you, reducing the time required to craft the item accordingly.

Mage.name: Mage
Mage.text:
@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.gnQ3C3zWhb7wxE3J classes="size-three margin-center noborder" caption=false cite=false]

Students with a keen intellect and unwavering discipline may walk the path of the mage. The arcane magic available to mages is both great and dangerous, and it is revealed only to the most devoted practitioners. To avoid interference with their spellcasting, mages wear no armor, instead protecting themselves with arcane shields and enchantments. To keep enemies at bay, mages can summon bursts of fire to incinerate distant targets and cause entire areas to erupt, setting groups of foes ablaze.

Mages are found among many peoples and cultures of Azeroth, and they’re regarded with varying degrees of suspicion. Thousands of years ago, Highborne night elf mages collaborated with their queen, Azshara, to turn the Well of Eternity into a portal through which the Burning Legion could enter Azeroth. The resulting conflict—the War of the Ancients—shattered the continent, leaving many night elves and others wary of mages and their hunger for power. The Highborne subsequently settled in the Eastern Kingdoms, where they eventually shared their magic with a select group of humans. These human mages, faced with suspicion from their own people, founded the city-state of Dalaran, which was ruled by a senate of mages called the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowKirinTor00000]{Kirin Tor}.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.9uxCKudRATFIEtyV caption=false classes="noborder"]

Playing a Mage.name: Playing a Mage
Playing a Mage.text:
To play a mage, choose the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.classes.Item.phbwzdWizard0000]{Wizard} class from the Player’s Handbook. You can choose one of three specializations to guide your choice of spells and feats: arcane, fire, or frost.

Adopting the Wizard class, either at character creation or through multiclassing, increases a character’s Renown Score with the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowKirinTor00000]{Kirin Tor} by 3 (see chapter 4).

Magic Items.name: Magic Items
Magic Items.text:
Many magic items are available to characters in a World of Warcraft campaign. The items described here cover the gamut from renowned weapons to simple Potions that characters skilled in alchemy can craft. They follow the rules for magic items in the Dungeon Master’s Guide.

Ashbringer

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.MXQ9u3MBotBNxePA caption=false classes="float-right size-three noborder"]

Weapon (Greatsword), Artifact (Requires Attunement by a Paladin)

Infused with the Holy Light and forged by King Magni Bronzebeard on the Great Anvil of Ironforge, Ashbringer was once the pride and joy of the knightly Mograine family. But when the traitorous Renault Mograine used the sword to kill his father, it became corrupted. The sword was claimed by the Scourge until Renault’s brother, Darion Mograine, betrayed the Lich King and delivered the weapon to Tirion Fordring—an act of heroism that cleansed Ashbringer of its corruption and restored the sword to its rightful form.

Magic Weapon. You gain a +3 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. It deals an extra 1d10 Fire damage on a hit, or an extra 3d10 Fire damage if the target is Undead.

Changing States. When first encountered, Ashbringer is in either its True State or its Corrupted State. At the DM’s discretion, Ashbringer changes into its Corrupted State if its wielder uses it to commit an act of legendary wickedness; it changes into its True State if its wielder uses it to commit an act of legendary heroism. Ashbringer’s current state grants you one of the following benefits:

Steal Life (Corrupted State Only). Whenever you use Ashbringer to reduce a creature to 0 Hit Points, you gain 20 Temporary Hit Points.

Wake of Ashes (True State Only). Whenever you use Ashbringer to reduce a creature to 0 Hit Points, you can make its corpse explode into a cloud of smoldering ash. Each creature of your choice in a 10-foot Emanation originating from the target must succeed on a DC 18 Constitution saving throw or have the Blinded condition until the end of its next turn.

Sentience. Ashbringer is a sentient weapon with an Intelligence of 14, a Wisdom of 17, and a Charisma of 17. It is Lawful Good in its True State or Lawful Evil in its Corrupted State. It has hearing and Darkvision with a range of 120 feet.

The weapon communicates telepathically with its wielder and speaks Common and Dwarven.

Personality. Ashbringer’s voice sounds like faint, intermittent whispers. In its True State, Ashbringer seeks to serve the forces of the Light and reduce the unholy to ash. In its Corrupted State, Ashbringer wants to undermine faith in the Light and destroy the righteous. Conflict arises if the wielder doesn’t share the goals of Ashbringer’s current state.

Random Properties. Ashbringer has the following random properties:

  • 1 minor beneficial property

  • 1 major beneficial property

  • 1 minor detrimental property

Destroying Ashbringer. Ashbringer can be destroyed only by its creator, Magni Bronzebeard. The weapon will shatter when he strikes it against the Great Anvil of Ironforge.

Aviana’s Feather

Wondrous Item, Legendary (Requires Attunement)

While attuned to this golden feather, you can take a Magic action to sprout a pair of glowing, golden wings from your back. The wings give you a Fly Speed of 80 feet, and any creature that makes an Opportunity Attack against you when you fly out of its reach has Disadvantage on the attack roll. If you fall while you have the wings, you descend at a rate of 60 feet per round until you land.

The wings last until you end the effect early as a Magic action or until your Attunement ends. If you are aloft when the wings disappear, you fall.

Crown of the Ogre King

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.Dyhf87rCLwSUd0HK caption=false classes="float-right size-two noborder"]

Wondrous Item, Very Rare (Requires Attunement)

While wearing this crown, you can take a Magic action to release a powerful belch that can be heard up to 300 feet away. Each creature in a 20-foot Cone originating from you makes a DC 17 Strength saving throw. On a failed save, a creature is pushed up to 20 feet away from you and has the Prone condition.

Cursed. This item is cursed. Attuning to it curses you until you are targeted by a Remove Curse spell or similar magic. Removing the crown fails to end the curse on you. While cursed, you are far hungrier than normal. You lose all your table manners, and your daily food requirement triples.

Defias Leather

Armor (Leather), Rare

Elite members of the Defias Brotherhood wear this armor to honor the faction’s stonemason founders. While wearing the armor, you gain the following benefits.

Mason’s Camouflage. You have Advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks made to hide behind stone objects and structures.

Meld into Stone. You can cast Meld into Stone from the armor. Once the armor has been used to cast this spell, it can’t be used to cast it again until the next dawn.

Doomhammer

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.qkSfwscFtflAacPc caption=false classes="float-right size-three noborder"]

Weapon (Warhammer), Artifact (Requires Attunement by a Barbarian)

Long ago on the world of Draenor, an orc named Gelnar set out to fashion a weapon that would empower his people against their ogre foes. He forged a fearsome hammer in the heat of an elemental pool of lava. Dubbed Doomhammer, this weapon was passed down through generations of Blackrock orcs. An ancient prophecy foretold that possession of the hammer would someday leave the Blackrock lineage; this prophecy came true when Thrall, an orc shaman, proved himself the weapon’s worthy wielder.

Magic Weapon. You gain a +3 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. It deals an extra 1d8 Lightning damage on a hit.

Gelnar’s Gifts. While holding Doomhammer, you gain the following benefits:

Doom Winds. Your fury carries the unbridled momentum of a windstorm. While your Rage is active, your Speed is doubled, and you can take an extra Attack action (one attack only) on each of your turns.

Lava Stride. You take no damage from molten lava and can walk across it as if it were solid ground.

Lightning Rod. When a creature you can see within 60 feet of you would take Lightning damage, you can take a Reaction to reduce the damage to 0.

Storm’s Passage. You can cast Wind Walk from this weapon. Once the weapon has been used to cast this spell, it can’t be used to cast it again until the next dawn.

Random Properties. Doomhammer has the following random properties:

  • 2 minor beneficial properties

  • 1 major beneficial property

  • 1 minor detrimental property

Destroying Doomhammer. To destroy Doomhammer, a descendant of Gelnar must hurl the weapon into the eye of a storm in Outland, the remnants of the destroyed world of Draenor.

Experimental Goblin Jetpack

Wondrous Item, Rare (Requires Attunement)

While wearing this pack, you can take a Magic action to fire up its jets. The jets remain active for 1 hour or until you end the effect early as a Magic action. The jets give you a Fly Speed of 60 feet. If you are aloft when the jets become inactive, you fall. When the jets stop, you can’t use them again for 1d12 hours.

Figurine of Wondrous Power (Jeweled Panther)

Wondrous Item, Rare

This statuette of a panther—made from jade, onyx, ruby, sapphire, or sunstone—follows the rules for Figurines of Wondrous Power in the Dungeon Master’s Guide. It can become a Large Panther with a Fly Speed of 30 feet for up to 12 hours and can be ridden as a mount. Once it has been used, it can’t be used again until 2 days have passed.

Flask of the Titans

Potion, Very Rare

When you drink this potion, your Hit Point maximum and current Hit Points increase by 30 for 1 hour.

The golden liquid in this flask tastes like honey and gleams with the light of dawn.

Monk.name: Monk
Monk.text:
@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.W1lrjcAcufuUMe96 caption=false cite=false classes="size-three margin-center noborder"]

When @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowPandaren00000]{pandaren} were subjugated by mogu millennia ago, the monks among them nurtured hope. While the mogu rulers banned weapons among their subjects, pandaren monks cultivated techniques of unarmed combat based on harnessing and focusing their innate spiritual energy. Finally, the monks and their disciples revolted against their masters and threw off the yoke of oppression.

Monks are masters of bare-handed combat, most widely known for their fearsome jabs and flying kicks, though monks don’t limit themselves to a single method of combat. Some monks revel in the intoxicating effect of absorbing blow after blow while their companions press the attack. Other monks call on the restorative power of Pandaria’s magical mists to return the sick and wounded to health.

Monks seek spiritual balance in life and in combat, and they rarely pick a fight without just cause. They find power through serenity and inner peace—then express their power through artful combat techniques and powers that mend life. Perhaps most surprisingly, some monks are also adept at producing powerful brews they consume in battle.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.z15IxL2GR9c8j0SM caption=false classes="noborder"]

Playing a Monk.name: Playing a Monk
Playing a Monk.text:
To play a monk, choose the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.classes.Item.phbmnkMonk000000]{Monk} class from the Player’s Handbook. You can choose one of three specializations to guide your choice of subclass and feats: brewmaster, mistweaver, or windwalker.

Brewmaster Specialization

Brewmaster monks inhabit the murky space between intoxication and the appearance of intoxication. They use a combination of powerful concoctions and unpredictable, staggering movements to enhance their own attacks and defenses and keep enemies off guard. Deceived by a brewmaster’s apparent intoxication, enemies barely have time to process the monk’s unpredictable behavior before being laid low by careful fist strikes.

The following choices will help you focus on this specialization:

Level 3. Choose the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.classes.Item.wowmnkBrewWarrio]{Warrior of Mystic Brews} subclass (see below).

Feats. Consider the following feats at higher levels: @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftChef0000000]{Chef}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftCrusher0000]{Crusher}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.feats.Item.wowftElusiveBraw]{Elusive Brawler} (see @UUID[.ebbMlLdJ6qAZ0bdq]{Monk Feats}), @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftGrappler000]{Grappler}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftSentinel000]{Sentinel}, and @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.feats.Item.wowftStaggerSway]{Stagger and Sway} (see @UUID[.ebbMlLdJ6qAZ0bdq]{Monk Feats}).

Mistweaver Specialization

Monks originated in Pandaria, where some of them learned from a Wild God called Yu’lon the Jade Serpent how to draw power from the magical mists that shrouded the continent for millennia. By weaving the mists, these monks wield the power of life’s essence to heal wounds and sap their foes’ life energy.

The following choices will help you focus on this specialization:

Level 3. Choose the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.classes.Item.phbmnkMercyWarri]{Warrior of Mercy} subclass.

Feats. Consider the following feats at higher levels: @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.feats.Item.wowftEnvelopiMis]{Enveloping Mist} (see @UUID[.ebbMlLdJ6qAZ0bdq]{Monk Feats}), @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftObservant00]{Observant}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftPoisoner000]{Poisoner}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftShadowTouch]{Shadow Touched}, and @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftSkulker0000]{Skulker}.

Windwalker Specialization

Windwalker monks are the quintessential martial artists, fighting with mastery and grace. Through a combination of intense physical training and mystical discipline, they can unleash a dizzying flurry of punches and kicks to devastate their enemies.

The following choices will help you focus on this specialization:

Level 3. Choose the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.classes.Item.phbmnkOpenHandWa]{Warrior of the Open Hand} subclass.

Feats. Consider the following feats at higher levels: @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftCharger0000]{Charger}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftCrusher0000]{Crusher}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.feats.Item.wowftFistsFury00]{Fists of Fury} (see @UUID[.ebbMlLdJ6qAZ0bdq]{Monk Feats}), and @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftSpeedy00000]{Speedy}.

Monk Feats.text:
Elusive Brawler, Enveloping Mist, Fists of Fury, and Stagger and Sway are new General feats intended primarily for monks.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.feats.Item.wowftElusiveBraw caption=false nameStyle=h4]

Monastic Orders of Pandaria

Monks undergo rigorous physical and spiritual training within monasteries. Even those who learn a martial art from traveling masters can trace their art’s origin back to a monastic order. The most notable monastic orders are the following.

Crane Wing Order. Under the guidance of the August Celestial Chi-Ji (one of the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowTheWorldOfWar.JournalEntryPage.Jm2kfPalxs8mphjd#wild-gods]{Wild Gods} who watch over Pandaria), monks practice their art in the Temple of the Red Crane in Pandaria’s Krasarang Wilds. Chi-Ji’s teachings emphasize physical and emotional adaptability.

Niuzao Sentinels. A martial order serving the August Celestial Niuzao maintains a temple in Pandaria’s Townlong Steppes. The stern sentinels of this order undergo rigorous emotional and physical training to ward against fear as they keep vigil over the Sha of Fear imprisoned in the catacombs beneath the temple.

Order of the Broken Temple. When the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowConflictsOfAz.JournalEntryPage.mOeoKWAu3OOx8LP9]{Burning Legion} destroyed the Peak of Serenity in Pandaria, the survivors formed the Order of the Broken Temple on the mysterious Wandering Isle. They welcome monks of all kinds in an effort to hold strong against the Burning Legion.

Order of the Cloud Serpent. Some monks bond with Pandaria’s flying cloud serpents to defend the Jade Forest. By cultivating hatchling cloud serpents and shepherding their growth to adulthood, these monks learn patience to temper their ambitions. The windwalker specialization represents these monks’ bond with the skies.

Shado-Pan. The Watchers on the Wall are elite monks who protect Pandaria’s peaceful way of life from internal and external threats. They operate across their realm from the Shado-Pan Monastery in Kun-Lai Summit and move through the shadows to strike suddenly against any foe.

Mounts and Vehicles.name: Mounts and Vehicles
Mounts and Vehicles.text:
Mounts are an important tool for every adventurer, not only carrying people and goods across Azeroth but also helping adventurers express their personalities and accomplishments.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.lC9O6JnVh4wiUEnS classes="noborder"]

Mounts for Purchase

The @UUID[.yAEK4SpiZaVON0YB]{Mounts for Purchase} table shows mounts that characters can purchase. Many of the mounts listed there can’t be purchased unless a character has achieved a certain level of renown with a particular @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowFactionsAndRe]{faction}. These mounts follow the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.content.JournalEntry.phbMountsAndVehi]{mount rules} in the Player’s Handbook.

Crafted Mounts

Characters can use the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowProfessionsAn]{professions} described earlier in this chapter to craft magic items that serve as mounts. Among the best-known such mounts are the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-dungeon-masters-guide.equipment.Item.dmgCarpetOfFlyin]{Carpet of Flying} (crafted with artisan tailoring), the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.items.Item.wowJeweledPanthe]{jade panther} Figurine of Wondrous Power (crafted with expert @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowProfessionsAn.JournalEntryPage.7ekbPmuT21XfF3GN#jewelcrafting]{jewelcrafting} and described later in this chapter), and vehicles made with engineering.

Powered Vehicles

Powered vehicles are similar to the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.content.JournalEntry.phbMountsAndVehi.JournalEntryPage.oXm4zg000veQxNUk]{large airborne and waterborne vehicles} described in the Player’s Handbook. They include the following:

@UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowFlyingMachiui]{Flying Machine}: A small gyrocopter with a rotor on top, two side-mounted engines, and skis as landing gear.

@UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowGoblinTrikerV]{Goblin Trike}: A three-wheeled motor vehicle with luxurious wood paneling.

@UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowMechanoHogvRn]{Mechano-Hog} and @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowMekgineersCvQ]{Mekgineer’s Chopper}: Two powerful motorcycles with optional sidecars, one made by @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowTheHorde00000]{the Horde}, the other by @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowTheAlliance00]{the Alliance}.

Characters traveling in these vehicles use the vehicle’s speed in miles per hour (as shown on the @UUID[.MTOBE50pEFAHI2sn#powered-vehicles]{Powered Vehicles} table) to determine their rate of travel, and they don’t choose a travel pace. These vehicles require Fuel, which weighs 10 pounds and costs 1 GP for each 8 hours of travel. (Characters can use the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowProfessionsAn.JournalEntryPage.7ekbPmuT21XfF3GN#alchemy]{alchemy profession} to craft Fuel.)

Special Mounts

Other mounts can be acquired by characters as adventure rewards, treasure, or renown perks. These include magical mounts that can be summoned and dismissed by means of a command word, as well as more unusual creatures beyond those described above. Here are two examples:

  • A character with a Renown Score of 25+ with the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowValdrakkenAcc]{Valdrakken Accord} gains a Blessing allowing them to summon a draconic steed.

  • A character who uses archaeology to collect six magic fragments from Highmountain tauren dig sites and who is an artisan @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowProfessionsAn.JournalEntryPage.ywSgJFsinrEDfTDk#archaeology]{archaeologist} can assemble the fragments into a Very Rare @UUID[Compendium.dnd-dungeon-masters-guide.equipment.Item.dmgEnspelledStaf]{Enspelled Staff} with the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplFindSteed0]{Find Steed} spell (level 4 version). The staff summons the spirit of Eche’ro, the famed moose mount of Huln Highmountain.

Overview.name: Overview
Overview.text:
For Level 17–20 Characters • Dragonflights

A jagged stone edifice looms in the southern wilds of Dustwallow Marsh. Near enough to threaten Theramore and spy on Orgrimmar, Onyxia, daughter of Deathwing, spins her schemes from the seething depths of her volcanic lair. The regent of Stormwind and the Warchief of the Horde will both pay handsomely for Onyxia’s head.

About Onyxia's Lair

Onyxia’s Lair was one of the forty-character raids that appeared in World of Warcraft when the game first launched. It is a classic adventure to slay a powerful, cunning dragon.

Treasure.name: Treasure
Treasure.text:
Onyxia’s treasure hoard contains 50,000 GP in coins; also, roll three times on the Onyxia’s Lair Art Objects table and three times on the Onyxia’s Lair Magic Items table, rerolling duplicate magic items.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.tables.RollTable.wowOnyxiasLair8b caption=false rangeLabel="2d6" resultLabel="Art Object" rollable nameStyle="h4" no-toc]

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.tables.RollTable.wowOnyxiasLairWP caption=false rangeLabel="1d8" resultLabel="Magic Item" rollable nameStyle="h4" no-toc]

Onyxia’s Lair Characters.name: Onyxia’s Lair Characters
Onyxia’s Lair Characters.text: Onyxia is the only character of note here. She might have guests, such as naga, Dark Iron supplicants, or her brother Nefarian.

Onyxia’s Lair Areas.name: Onyxia’s Lair Areas
Onyxia’s Lair Areas.text:
@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.HLWhjoJ5CYC26umS caption=false classes="noborder"]

Cavern Mouth. The pitch-black mouth of the cave slopes downward and contains a magical trap. When a Humanoid walks down the path as it loops under itself, the path above detonates, collapsing in a shower of boulders in a 20-foot-­radius, 40-foot-high Cylinder centered on the triggering creature. This seals the exit, and creatures in the Cylinder make a [[/save dex 19 format=long]], taking [[/damage 18d10 average]] damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one.

Path of the Warders. Two dragonspawn warders (use the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowBlackDragonzH]{Black Dragonflight Drake} stat block from chapter 7, but remove their Fly Speed) defend this cavern. They are Onyxia’s loyal guards. Each has a quadrupedal lower body and a scaled, humanlike torso with vestigial wings and a draconic head. Two more warders appear here if characters try to fight Onyxia from this area.

Whelp Caves. Onyxia’s eggs incubate in the whelp caves. Each 10-foot square contains one whelp egg. If a Humanoid comes within 10 feet of an egg, the egg hatches into a @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowBlackDragonpP]{Black Dragonflight Whelp} (see chapter 7) and begins combat. A creature can avoid causing eggs to hatch until the end of its turn by taking the Hide action and making a successful [[/check stealth 15 format=long]].

Onyxia’s Hoard. Onyxia (@UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowBlackDragonf7]{Black Dragonflight Dragon}; see chapter 7) lairs here. In her lair, she can use Legendary Resistance five times per day, and she can use four Legendary Actions per round. Defeating her in her lair earns a party [[/award 50000xp]]. She starts the fight on the ground, starts flying when she is Bloodied, then lands to flee through the secret exit. When Onyxia is Bloodied, one @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowBlackDragonpP]{Black Dragonflight Whelp} hatches on Initiative count 20 of each round. Replace Onyxia’s Pounce Legendary Action with Tail Swipe:

Tail Swipe. Melee Attack Roll: [[/attack 16]] to hit, reach 20 ft. Hit: [[/damage 6d8 + 9 average]] damage, and the target is pushed 60 feet straight away from Onyxia.

Secret Exit. An illusory wall in the northwest of Onyxia’s hoard hides a secret exit that leads to the surface. A similar illusion conceals the tunnel, which opens into the rocky, southern hills of Dustwallow Marsh. Physical interaction with either image reveals it to be illusory. A creature that takes the Study action to examine an image can determine that it is an illusion with a successful [[/check investigation 22 format=long]].

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.z5mkrw0ILlE6H4oW caption=false classes="noborder"]

Onyxia.name: Onyxia
Onyxia.text:
“How fortuitous. Usually, I must leave my lair to feed.”

Onyxia is manipulating Azeroth’s factions. She has her father’s arrogance and enough cunning to deserve it. Unlike her brother, Nefarian, she has little desire to monologue or stroke her ego. She flees fights she doesn’t think she can win—such as if her human visage is revealed deep in enemy territory—and swiftly and confidently attacks when confronted in her lair.

In Stormwind, she uses her visage to masquerade as Lady Katrana Prestor, adviser to King Varian Wrynn. In his addled state, the king hangs on her every word. There, she is protected by dragonspawn disguised with illusions as Stormwind guards. She has made fewer inroads within the Horde, but from her lair in Dustwallow Marsh, she secretly stokes tensions between Theramore and Orgrimmar, preventing the Horde and the Alliance from uniting against the black dragonflight forces mustering in Blackrock Mountain.

Orc.name: Orc
Orc.text:
@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.NPWb1t6pLONfLyF1 classes="hide-in-embed noborder"]

Orcs originate from the planet of Draenor, and as such their primordial history is separate from the efforts of the titan Pantheon to preserve Azeroth’s Worldsoul from corruption. Orcs descend from Grond, a living mountain shaped by the titan Aggramar to battle the massive botanical hivemind of the Evergrowth, which dominated ancient Draenor. Infused with life, the broken pieces that fell from Grond’s body became creatures in their own right—first the mighty earth giants called colossi, then the magma giants called magnaron, then the fearsome gronn, then ogron, and finally, from the ogron came ogres and orcs. Though the orcs are the smallest and weakest of Grond’s descendants, they possess a fierce intellect and strong sense of community.

Some early orcs were drawn to the site of Grond’s demise, and there they learned about the elemental spirits of air, earth, fire, and water. Cultivating harmony among the four elements, these orcs became the first shaman, who rose to become the spiritual leaders of their people.

In the decades before the opening of the Dark Portal, the demon lord Kil’jaeden manipulated Ner’zhul, one of the spiritual leaders of the orcs of Draenor, and through him the rest of the orc clans. Kil’jaeden convinced Ner’zhul that the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowDraenei000000]{draenei} were conspiring against the orcs and goaded him into attacking the draenei. When Ner’zhul balked at an all-out assault on Shattrath City, Kil’jaeden discarded him and turned to Ner’zhul’s apprentice, Gul’dan, who was all too eager to wreak destruction across the world in exchange for the power offered by the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowConflictsOfAz.JournalEntryPage.mOeoKWAu3OOx8LP9]{Burning Legion}. Gul’dan gave the leaders of the orc tribes demon blood to drink, transforming them and their followers into a merciless, destructive force bound to the Legion’s service.

After defeating the draenei and sating their bloodlust with internecine warfare, the orcs were lured to the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowWorldOfAzerot]{world of Azeroth} and enticed to make war on the human kingdoms of Stormwind and Lordaeron in what became known as the First and Second Wars. Though @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowTheHorde00000]{the Horde} nearly succeeded in annihilating humanity, the Horde ultimately devoured itself from within and collapsed. The defeated orcs spent many years in internment camps, listless and lethargic without access to the fel magic that had empowered them. After many years, a visionary young warchief named Thrall rose to lead his people in their darkest hour. Under his rule, the orcs freed themselves from the chains of demonic corruption and embraced their ancient heritage.

Thrall led his people away from human lands to the continent of Kalimdor. There, Thrall and the Horde came face to face with their old oppressor, the Burning Legion. With the aid of humans and night elves, the orcs repelled the Legion and set out to find their own path in their adopted world. The orcs claimed the harsh wastelands of Durotar as their kingdom in Kalimdor.

Now based in the city of Orgrimmar, the orcs look forward to a shining new future. With the death of the pit lord Mannoroth, whose blood brought the demonic curse on the orcs of Draenor, the curse is now lifted, and the orcs are free of demonic influence. Though they are no longer driven by dreams of conquest, they stand ready to destroy all who would challenge their sovereignty or their supremacy. It is every orc’s duty to crush the enemies of Durotar, both seen and unseen, for the nefarious agents of the Burning Legion still wander the land.

Exposure to the fel magic of the Burning Legion transformed the orcs of Draenor, turning their skin green. Though the orcs of Azeroth are now free of fel corruption, they retain this green skin.

Mag'har Orcs.name: Mag'har Orcs
Mag'har Orcs.text: A few orcs were never tainted by fel magic, remaining uncorrupted—in Orcish, “mag’har.” Retaining their original brown or gray skin, they also preserve the shamanistic traditions the orcs cherished before the Burning Legion’s intervention.

Orc Traits.name: Orc Traits
Orc Traits.text: You have the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.origins.Item.phbspOrc00000000]{Orc }species traits from the Player’s Handbook.

Paladin.name: Paladin
Paladin.text:
@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.xf01mvGaODKGDH0p caption=false cite=false classes="size-three margin-center noborder"]

The call of the paladin is to protect the weak, mete out justice to the unjust, and vanquish evil from the darkest corners of the world. These holy warriors are heavily armored and favor powerful weapons as they confront the toughest of foes, and the blessing of the Light allows them to heal wounds and smite their enemies.

Paladins’ magical power comes from the Holy Light, one of @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowTheWorldOfWar.JournalEntryPage.Pe0syoLav7rLgFLa]{The Cosmic Forces} of the universe. The first paladins on Azeroth were humans who belonged to the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowTheWorldOfWar.JournalEntryPage.39WbPfMoJEVvbg15#church-of-the-holy-light]{Church of the Holy Light}. Due to their virtue and piety, they were inducted into the Order of the Silver Hand during the Second War. Dwarves soon joined the ranks of the knights, and the order played a key role in battling both the Horde in the Second War and the Scourge in the Third War.

@UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowDraenei000000]{Draenei} access the power of the Light through their connection to the naaru, living embodiments of Light, while blood elves channel the Light’s power through their Sunwell. Tauren servants of An’she, their sun god, wield holy power in similar ways, as do Zandalari troll devotees of Rezan. Earthen warriors called Ordinants channel the power of Order with effects that are indistinguishable from paladins’ use of the Light.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.2mRQijMrRFwTcz2D caption=false classes="noborder"]

Playing a Paladin.name: Playing a Paladin
Playing a Paladin.text:
To play a paladin, choose the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.classes.Item.phbpdnPaladin000]{Paladin} class from the Player’s Handbook. You can choose one of three specializations to guide your choice of subclass, spells, and feats: holy, protection, or retribution.

Holy Specialization

Holy paladins spend much of their lives in hallowed halls studying divine doctrine, learning to stand as beacons of the Light for their allies. They believe that evil must be eradicated from the world so that the Light can prevail, and they serve all who are engaged in this holy struggle. The Light, in turn, imbues holy paladins with the power to heal and revitalize their comrades.

The following choices will help you focus on this specialization:

Level 1. Pandaren.name: Pandaren
Pandaren.text:
@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.1P52rDI5YLujTkrI classes="hide-in-embed noborder"]

The origins of the pandaren are a mystery, but pandaren settled around the Vale of Eternal Blossoms millennia before the Great Sundering. Wise and peaceful, they forged a strong bond with four @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowTheWorldOfWar.JournalEntryPage.Jm2kfPalxs8mphjd#wild-gods]{Wild Gods} called the August Celestials: Chi-Ji the Red Crane, Niuzao the Black Ox, Xuen the White Tiger, and Yu’lon the Jade Serpent. Under the tutelage of these ancient beings, the pandaren developed a rich tradition of philosophy, art, agriculture, and medicine.

That tradition was nearly extinguished when the mogu—a titan-forged people whose infection with the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowConflictsOfAz.JournalEntryPage.QX2LRHkL98AMmC55]{Old Gods}’ curse of flesh left them valuing only power and control—conquered and enslaved the pandaren. For millennia, the pandaren were trapped in subservience, not allowed to carry weapons or to read or write. But pandaren monks passed down the traditions of their people and kept the pandaren unified despite their bitter oppression.

As the mogu empire began to falter, the pandaren launched a rebellion. Trained by the monks to fight without weapons, the pandaren overthrew the mogu and formed an empire. This empire persisted in relative peace and prosperity for millennia, until the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowConflictsOfAz.JournalEntryPage.mOeoKWAu3OOx8LP9]{Burning Legion} first invaded @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowWorldOfAzerot]{Azeroth} and caused the Great Sundering.

As the demons of the Burning Legion spread, the pandaren emperor sacrificed himself to shroud his land in mist, protecting it from the devastation of the Legion and the Great Sundering that followed. The mists persisted for ten thousand years, and the pandaren flourished in isolation, almost entirely forgotten by the outside world.

Some eight hundred years before the opening of the Dark Portal, an adventurous pandaren named Liu Lang set out to discover what was beyond the mists. He set sail on the back of a giant sea turtle named Shen-zin Su. As the young turtle grew, so did the number of adventurous pandaren making their home on this “Wandering Isle.” Among the most notable of these adventurous pandaren is Chen Stormstout, a brewmaster who helped Thrall and his allies found the new orc homeland of Durotar. Although the turtle hasn’t made landfall in many years, the pandaren who live on it are driven by a spirit of adventure that is alien to most of their kind.

Pandaren Philosophies.name: Pandaren Philosophies
Pandaren Philosophies.text:
Shortly after the Cataclysm set into motion by Deathwing’s emergence into the world, the mists that shrouded Pandaria suddenly vanished. The wide-ranging battle fleets of both @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowTheAlliance00]{the Alliance} and @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowTheHorde00000]{the Horde} quickly discovered this land where their charts showed only empty sea, and Pandaria became a new battleground in the never-ending conflict between these factions. Though the pandaren as a whole remained neutral, the two philosophical sects that dominate the teaching of the Wandering Isle each aligned with one of the two global factions.

The philosophical path of @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowTheHorde00000.JournalEntryPage.zHGqWgoJEhzGtiGL]{Huojin} teaches direct action. Followers of this path believe that injustice must be met with a swift and decisive response. They teach that it is honorable to defend one’s homes and families at any cost, and that inaction is often worse than wrong action. Led by Ji Firepaw, the adherents of the Huojin philosophy were drawn to the practical nature of the Horde.

The path of Tushui, by contrast, emphasizes meditation and careful discernment in the context of constant training, meditation, and moral conviction. They enjoy the contemplation of moral ideals and concepts of justice and believe that living a principled life is the greatest good. This philosophy naturally attracted the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowTheAlliance00.JournalEntryPage.ilOLdiGjFqiEtSlG]{Tushui}—and their leader, Aysa Cloudsinger—to the cause of the Alliance.

Pandaren Renown.name: Pandaren Renown
Pandaren Renown.text: Choose whether to align with the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowTheHorde00000.JournalEntryPage.zHGqWgoJEhzGtiGL]{Huojin} (Horde) or the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowTheAlliance00.JournalEntryPage.ilOLdiGjFqiEtSlG]{Tushui} (Alliance) philosophy. Your Renown Score with the chosen faction begins at 3.

Priest.name: Priest
Priest.text:
@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.gIUuejjF1fTYkO0k caption=false cite=false classes="noborder margin-center size-three"]

Priests are devoted to the spiritual realm, drawing power from the opposing forces of @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowTheWorldOfWar.JournalEntryPage.39WbPfMoJEVvbg15]{Light and Void}. From the Light—which priests might conceptualize or revere as the Holy Light, Elune, or some other force or entity—priests draw holy power for healing and protection. From Shadow, priests call on power to break the will and sap the vitality of their foes. Priests wield both forces to support their allies and devastate their enemies.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.j0mytf51jop4DiFw caption=false classes="noborder"]

Playing a Priest.name: Playing a Priest
Playing a Priest.text:
To play a priest, choose the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.classes.Item.phbclcCleric0000]{Cleric} class from the Player’s Handbook. You can choose one of three specializations to guide your choice of subclass, spells, and other features: discipline, holy, or shadow. These specializations reflect varying degrees of devotion to the cosmic forces of @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowTheWorldOfWar.JournalEntryPage.39WbPfMoJEVvbg15]{Light and Shadow}, with holy priests focusing on the Light, shadow priests drawing primarily on Shadow, and discipline priests balancing the two.

Discipline Specialization

Some priests pride themselves on pragmatism. They understand that light casts a shadow, that darkness is defined by light, and that true discipline stems from one’s ability to balance these opposing powers in service of a greater cause. While these priests possess many holy virtues to aid their allies, they also dabble in the dark arts to debilitate their enemies—exercising immense discipline to prevent themselves from delving too far into the shadows. Many discipline priests believe the ends justify the means; they maximize their effectiveness by studying scriptures both virtuous and vile.

The following choices will help you focus on this specialization:

Level 1. Choose Thaumaturge for your Divine Order. Choose the following cantrips: @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplGuidance00]{Guidance}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplResistance]{Resistance}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplThaumaturg]{Thaumaturgy}, and @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplWordofRadi]{Word of Radiance}. Prepare the following spells to start: @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplCureWounds]{Cure Wounds}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplGuidingBol]{Guiding Bolt}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbSanctuary0000]{Sanctuary}, and @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplShieldofFa]{Shield of Faith}.

Level 3. Choose the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.classes.Item.wowclcDiscipDoma]{Discipline Domain} subclass (see below).

Feats. Holy Specialization

After spending much of their lives in temples studying ancient doctrine, preaching the tenets of their faith, and pledging their devotion to the divine powers they follow, the most adept priests leave their houses of worship to serve on the battlefield. There, they use their holy powers to bless allies and mend wounds. And while most stay behind the front lines to aid their comrades, these holy champions can also smite foes and carry out sacred justice. Holy priests are morally opposed to shadow magic. They are exemplars of the incredible grace and power of the divine and the Light.

The following choices will help you focus on this specialization:

Level 1. Choose Thaumaturge for your Divine Order. Choose the following cantrips: @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplGuidance00]{Guidance}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplLight00000]{Light}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplSacredFlam]{Sacred Flame}, and @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplSparetheDy]{Spare the Dying}. Shadow Specialization

The Light in which many priests bathe is brilliant and effervescent, granting them immense divine power. But the brightest light casts the darkest shadow—and within this shadow, a rival power dwells. Shadow priests fully embrace this polarity, their resolute faith focused on shadowy magics and mental manipulation. They derive their power from the Void, straying dangerously close to the domain of the Old Gods and its ancient, corruptive influence. This is the state in which these dark priests thrive, feeding off of the minds of their opponents to reach terrifying new limits.

The following choices will help you focus on this specialization:

Level 1. Choose Thaumaturge for your Divine Order. Choose the following cantrips: @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplMending000]{Mending}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplResistance]{Resistance}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplThaumaturg]{Thaumaturgy}, and @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplTolltheDea]{Toll the Dead}. Prepare the following spells to start: @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplBane000000]{Bane}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplCommand000]{Command}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplHealingWor]{Healing Word}, and @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.spells.Item.wowsplShadowWord]{Shadow Word: Pain} (see “Priest Spells”).

Level 3. Choose the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.classes.Item.wowclcShadowDoma]{Shadow Domain} subclass (see below).

Feats. Consider the following feats at higher levels: @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftActor000000]{Actor}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftMageSlayer0]{Mage Slayer}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftShadowTouch]{Shadow Touched}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftSkulker0000]{Skulker}, and @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftTelepathic0]{Telepathic}.

Faiths of the Light and Shadow

Priests in Azeroth belong to several notable faiths related to the Light and Shadow.

Holy Light. Many peoples across Azeroth revere the Holy Light as an abstract force or as a personified being. The @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowTheWorldOfWar.JournalEntryPage.39WbPfMoJEVvbg15#church-of-the-holy-light]{Church of the Holy Light} is the most prominent religious body in the world, devoted to the pure ideals of the Light as revealed in visions sent by the naaru. This faith is predominant among humans, dwarves, gnomes, high and blood elves, and draenei. A similar faith, the Church of the Sacred Flame, was brought east across the sea by the humans and high elves who founded the Empire of Arathor.

Sun and Moon. Tauren revere the sun deity An’she as the right eye of the Earth Mother, with the moon (a being of Life), Mu’she, being her left eye. Night elves also revere a moon deity, Elune, who is associated with both the power of nature and the Holy Light.

Old Gods. Most priests view Shadow as a dark mirror of the Light, but some revere it in the form of Old Gods or void lords. The Twilight’s Hammer is the most widespread cult of the Old Gods, but less destructive faiths also draw on Shadow power. Most notable among these is the Cult of the Forgotten Shadow, founded by Forsaken priests who believed themselves abandoned or betrayed by the Light. Followers of the Forgotten Shadow wield Void power but believe it’s important to understand the Light as well, balancing these opposed forces.

Lok’osh. Many orc priests practice Lok’osh, a path of healing and renewal that draws on “songs of life and shadow” found within each practitioner’s heart and spirit. Priests within this tradition focus on Light and Void powers to varying degrees, but the path of the Lok’osh prevents priests from straying too far into the corruption of the Void.

Introduction.name: Introduction
Introduction.text:
@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.MnPDnLANLA9t8D41 classes="noborder"]

Beyond choosing class and origin, you can customize your character in a World of Warcraft campaign through their professions and equipment—especially @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowMountsAndVehi]{mounts}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowCompanionCrea]{pets}, and @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowMagicItems000]{magic items}. This chapter covers those options.

Professions and Crafting.name: Professions and Crafting
Professions and Crafting.text:
Characters in Azeroth can use their tool proficiencies to practice professions, allowing them to gather resources and craft them into equipment and magic items. A character can practice any profession as long as the character has the prerequisite proficiency.

The rules in this chapter build on the crafting rules in the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.content.JournalEntry.phbCraftingEquip]{Player’s Handbook} and @UUID[Compendium.dnd-dungeon-masters-guide.content.JournalEntry.dmgMagicItems000.JournalEntryPage.CmKJpbyrDuVrAkIs]{Dungeon Master’s Guide}. With these rules, characters can use @UUID[.ywSgJFsinrEDfTDk]{gathering professions} (such as fishing, mining, and skinning) to collect abstract resources that are measured in GP value. For example, a character might use the herbalism profession to collect 50 GP worth of herbalism resources. The character can then use any combination of those resources and the character’s own money to craft items using their @UUID[.7ekbPmuT21XfF3GN]{production professions }(such as blacksmithing, cooking, and leatherworking). Having gathered 50 GP worth of herbalism resources, a character might spend those resources, along with 50 GP of coins or other monetary resources, to craft a @UUID[Compendium.dnd-dungeon-masters-guide.equipment.Item.dmgPotionOfWater]{Potion of Water Breathing}.

Optionally, a DM can make the resources less abstract, but this approach requires the DM to invent or research recipes for magic items characters wish to create and name the resources characters gather. A character who wants to craft a Potion of Water Breathing might need to gather 50 GP worth of stranglekelp, not just abstract herbalism resources, and also acquire 50 GP worth of blackmouth oil (or use fishing to catch oily blackmouth fish). Listing specific resources and recipes is beyond the scope of this book.

How to Craft Items in Foundry VTT

We have built a simple Crafting application into the World of Warcraft module to make crafting items easier. When the World of Warcraft module is active you can change to the Inventory tab of any Player Character's sheet and a new icon ( ) will be at the bottom of the window which will open the crafting window. If you have any active crafts it will appear in a new group as seen here:

  1. This is where any in-progress crafts will appear. The bar represents your progress through the number of days necessary to create the item.

  2. This button will advance progress by a day. It will not automatically progress as time passes because the system does not know if you have spent the necessary time working on it that day. As a result, whenever you work on crafting the item you will need to track it manually with this button.

  3. This button will open the Crafting dialog shown below.

This is the crafting dialog:

  1. When the window opens you can drag and drop the item you want to craft into the Recipe section.

  2. This dropdown lets you select which tool will be used to create the item. If the Crafter doesn't have proficiency with the tool, a warning icon will be displayed.

  3. The Crafter section accepts an Actor who will make the item.

  4. This field will show what the Crafter's Proficiency Level is with the given tools. If they are not a high enough Profiency Level a warning icon will be displayed.

  5. Drag and drop the ingredients that are being contributed to make the item in the Ingredients section. The quantities can be increased up to the maximum quantity of the item you have. In this example our Crafter has 10 Gromsblood and is contributing 5 of them for a total value of 5,000 gold.

  6. The Summary section explains the gold contribution from your Ingredients, the remaining Gold cost, and the total Cost in gold for the item as well as the Time it will take to make it.

  7. The   Begin Crafting button will add the Crafting group to the bottom of the inventory as shown above. You can track your progress going forward from there.

Gathering Professions.name: Gathering Professions
Gathering Professions.text:
Gathering professions allow characters to collect resources, which can be sold or used for crafting.

Most gathering professions work like @UUID[Compendium.dnd-dungeon-masters-guide.content.JournalEntry.dmgRunningExplor.JournalEntryPage.HtzmbDmbBmFB2gDq#journey-stage-challenges]{foraging during travel}, as described in the Dungeon Master’s Guide. You can make a [[/skill sur]] check using a gathering profession once per journey stage (or once per day if a stage is shorter than a day). The DC is set by the DM based on the general @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowWorldOfAzerot.JournalEntryPage.jG5jNO0PgPvRlpMB]{level range of the region} where you’re traveling. (@UUID[.#archaeology]{Archaeology} and @UUID[.#skinning]{skinning} work differently, as described below.)

You find nothing on a failed check. On a successful check, you find one resource per day of the journey stage. If you beat the DC by 5 or more, one of the resources you find on that journey stage is a rare (more valuable) resource. The DM decides what resources you find.

Archaeology

Requires Proficiency in History

You can use the archaeology profession to gather archaeology fragments from the sites of ancient ruins. Unlike the resources gathered with other gathering professions, these resources aren’t used in crafting. Rather, you can piece these archaeology fragments together into items of historical interest.

Gathering Fragments. To gather archaeology fragments, you must visit a dig site. The DM determines whether an area is a dig site and where the relics originate from. The Dig Sites table shows the regions where relics of different origins can be found.

After spending 1 hour exploring a dig site (which can be concurrent with a Short Rest), you make an [[/skill his]] check. The DC of the check depends on the region level, as shown on the Gathering Professions table. On a successful check, you unearth [[/r 1d6]] archaeology fragments. If you beat the DC by 5 or more, you unearth a complete relic with the value of a rare resource for that region, as shown on the Gathering Professions table. On a natural 20, you instead find one magic fragment.

Assembling a Relic. You can assemble six archaeology fragments with the same origin into a completed relic by succeeding on a [[/check history 15 format=long]]. The value of the assembled relic equals the value of a common resource for your level (rather than the region level), as shown on the Gathering Professions table. On a failed check, you can’t try again until you’ve collected at least one additional archaeology fragment with the same origin.

Assembling a Magic Item. You can assemble six magic fragments with the same origin into an item of the DM’s choice whose rarity corresponds with your Proficiency Bonus, as shown on the Profession Levels table. For example, if you collect six magic fragments from dwarf dig sites, and you are a master archaeologist (Proficiency Bonus +6), you can assemble the pieces into a @UUID[Compendium.dnd-dungeon-masters-guide.equipment.Item.dmgStaffOfTheMag]{Staff of the Magi} that was wielded by Sorcerer-Thane Thaurissan.

Fishing

Requires No Proficiency

The primary use for fishing is foraging for food, which uses @UUID[Compendium.dnd-dungeon-masters-guide.content.JournalEntry.dmgRunningExplor.JournalEntryPage.HtzmbDmbBmFB2gDq#journey-stage-challenges]{the rules} in the Dungeon Master’s Guide. If you roll a natural 20 on a [[/skill sur]] check to forage for food using fishing, you might pull up a chest, crate, or lockbox containing other resources—such as ores, fabrics, or leather—at the DM’s discretion. The value of such a find equals the value of a rare resource for the region’s level.

If you are searching for particular fish to use in a recipe, you can make a [[/skill sur]] check once per journey stage to see whether you can catch the desired fish, using a DC chosen from the Gathering Professions table.

Herbalism

Requires Proficiency with @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.equipment.Item.phbtulHerbalismK]{Herbalism Kit}

You can use the herbalism profession to gather herbs, flowers, and mushrooms. These resources are primarily useful in crafting items with the alchemy and inscription professions.

Using herbalism follows the general rules described in “Gathering Professions.” In unusual circumstances, you can use herbalism to gather rare resources from Plant creatures. Use the rules for @UUID[.#skinning]{skinning} as a guideline to determine the DC for gathering such resources and their value.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.da0g9IMxW5WAveof classes="float-right size-three noborder"]

Mining

Requires Proficiency with @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.equipment.Item.phbtulMasonsTool]{Mason’s Tools}

You can use the mining profession to gather metal ores, stones, and gems. These resources are primarily useful in crafting items with the @UUID[.7ekbPmuT21XfF3GN#blacksmithing]{blacksmithing}, @UUID[.7ekbPmuT21XfF3GN#engineering]{engineering}, and @UUID[.7ekbPmuT21XfF3GN#jewelcrafting]{jewelcrafting} professions.

Smelting. If you are gathering specific resources to use in detailed recipes, metal mining resources might need to be smelted into bars before they can be used in crafting. You need access to a smith’s forge or a refinery to smelt ore, and the time required is 1 hour for every 10 GP of the metal resource’s value. So copper and tin (10 GP mining resources) can be refined into bars in 1 hour, while creating an empyrium bar (a 500 GP resource) takes 50 hours.

You can use the same rules to combine metal resources to create alloys, which can be important in blacksmithing.

Skinning

Requires Proficiency with @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.equipment.Item.phbtulLeatherwor]{Leatherworker’s Tools}

You can use the skinning profession to gather leather or hide. These resources are primarily useful in crafting items with the @UUID[.7ekbPmuT21XfF3GN#leatherworking]{leatherworking} profession.

You use skinning on dead creatures rather than as part of travel, and the quality of leather or hide gathered depends on the Challenge Rating of the creature rather than the level of the region.

Skinning a Beast or an animallike Monstrosity yields leather or hide. You must be in the same space as the corpse and spend 10 minutes skinning the creature, and then you make a [[/skill sur]] check using @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.equipment.Item.phbtulLeatherwor]{Leatherworker’s Tools}. The check DC depends on the Challenge Rating of the creature, using the Region Level column of the Gathering Professions table and treating a CR above 20 as Endgame. If you make a successful check, the effort yields a leather resource worth the value of a common resource. If you beat the DC by 5 or more, the effort yields hide instead, which has the value of a rare resource.

You can also skin certain Fiends and Dragons. Skinning an animallike Fiend, such as a @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowBestiaryOfAze.JournalEntryPage.Xkd9lZp4CbeapZ09]{felhound}, requires journeyman-level skinning (a Proficiency Bonus of +3 or higher). Skinning a Dragon requires artisan-level skinning (a Proficiency Bonus of +5 or higher). A successful check in either case yields hide with the value of a rare resource.

Proficiency Levels.name: Proficiency Levels
Proficiency Levels.text:
A character’s Proficiency Bonus is the measure of how skilled the character is at a profession. A character with a +2 Proficiency Bonus is an apprentice in a profession, a +3 bonus makes the character a journeyman, and so on, as shown on the Profession Levels table below. Each recipe used in a crafting profession requires a minimum Proficiency Bonus, which is determined by the rarity of the magic item the recipe creates. (Most nonmagical equipment requires apprentice recipes.)
