This chapter assumes characters work with trainers to improve their professions between adventures. If your campaign uses the variant rule in the Dungeon Master’s Guide that characters must spend time and money @UUID[Compendium.dnd-dungeon-masters-guide.content.JournalEntry.dmgCharacterAdva.JournalEntryPage.6yN0D49j6MDWpovd#variant:-training-to-gain-levels]{training to gain levels}, characters must also spend time and money training with profession trainers to improve their skill in the profession. This training requires a number of days equal to the character’s new Proficiency Bonus and costs 2 GP per day. So when a character reaches level 5 and a Proficiency Bonus of +3, the character must spend 3 days and 6 GP training to achieve a journeyman proficiency level in each profession they practice.

Production Professions.name: Production Professions
Production Professions.text:
Production professions allow characters to use resources—whether gathered using gathering professions, found as treasure, or purchased from merchants—to craft nonmagical and magical items.

Production professions use the rules for @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.content.JournalEntry.phbCraftingEquip]{crafting equipment} in the Player’s Handbook and the rules for @UUID[Compendium.dnd-dungeon-masters-guide.content.JournalEntry.dmgMagicItems000.JournalEntryPage.CmKJpbyrDuVrAkIs]{crafting magic items} in the Dungeon Master’s Guide, with one key change: Ingredients provide the magic. Characters can craft magic items even if they lack proficiency in the Arcana skill. They also don’t need to have spells prepared in order to craft magic items that produce spells. Instead, they need to know specific recipes and use ingredients—many of which are infused with magic—to create items. Characters learn recipes as described below and in the profession descriptions that follow.

Crafting Recipes

“Recipe” is a general term that encompasses recipes for alchemy and cooking, plans for blacksmithing, formulas for enchanting, schematics for engineering, techniques for inscription, designs for jewelcrafting, and patterns for leatherworking and tailoring. As characters advance their crafting skills, they learn basic recipes automatically. Basic recipes let a character create mundane items and Common, Uncommon, and Rare magic Armor, Potions, Scrolls, Wands, and Weapons. Other recipes can be purchased from specialist trainers, found as treasure, or granted as @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowFactionsAndRe]{renown rewards}. Artisan and master recipes can be acquired only by extraordinary means, as described below.

The specific recipes mentioned here are examples only, inspired by crafting recipes in the World of Warcraft game. The DM is free to create unique recipes or to ignore the specifics and require only some combination of abstract resources and money.

Apprentice Recipes. Apprentice recipes require some combination of two or three different resources. For example, using alchemy to craft a Common potion costs 25 GP. The DM might look up alchemy recipes from World of Warcraft and decide that this requires 20 GP of herbalism resources plus 5 GP of miscellaneous ingredients. Crafting a @UUID[Compendium.dnd-dungeon-masters-guide.equipment.Item.dmgPotionOfHeali]{Potion of Healing} might require one peacebloom and one silverleaf, while a @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.items.Item.wowPotionofManzG]{Potion of Mana} might require a mage­royal and a silverleaf. All these are common resources found in level 1–4 regions (worth 10 GP each). Similarly, using blacksmithing to craft a suit of Plate Armor in World of Warcraft requires iron bars and heavy stones, so the DM might decide that the 750 GP cost to craft the armor consists of twelve iron bars and three heavy stones, which are all common resources found in level 5–10 regions (50 GP each).

Journeyman Recipes. Journeyman recipes sometimes involve more complex steps than simply combining two or three resources of the same type. For example, crafting an elixir of water breathing in World of Warcraft requires the combination of stranglekelp (gathered with herbalism) and blackmouth oil (made with alchemy from oily blackmouth fish). So the DM might create a recipe for a @UUID[Compendium.dnd-dungeon-masters-guide.equipment.Item.dmgPotionOfWater]{Potion of Water Breathing} (an Uncommon potion that costs 100 GP to make) that involves catching two rare fish resources in a level 1–4 region (25 GP each), then combining the oil from them with stranglekelp, a common herb resource from a level 5–10 region (50 GP). Similarly, using blacksmithing to craft a @UUID[Compendium.dnd-dungeon-masters-guide.equipment.Item.dmgWeapon12or300]{+1 Greatsword} (which costs 225 GP) might involve both mining and skinning resources: ten copper bars (10 GP each), two malachite stones (10 GP each), and two medium leather (50 GP each), plus 5 GP extra.

Expert Recipes. In addition to requiring more expensive resources, expert recipes are often quite complex and sometimes require unusual ingredients—which often give them minor properties or quirks (see @UUID[Compendium.dnd-dungeon-masters-guide.content.JournalEntry.dmgMagicItems000.JournalEntryPage.0WfMqxMjsTpUyRDM]{Magic Item Special Features} in the Dungeon Master’s Guide). For example, characters in World of Warcraft can use blacksmithing to create barbaric iron plate using iron bars, heavy stones, and fangs and claws from predatory animals. The DM might decide that this armor is +1 Plate Armor with the Guardian minor property, granting the wearer a +2 bonus to Initiative rolls. Such an item costs 2,750 GP to craft, so the recipe might require forty-eight iron bars (50 GP each), five heavy stones (50 GP each), and 100 GP of fangs and claws.

Artisan Recipes. Befitting their high price, artisan recipes require rare and expensive ingredients. Learning the recipes required for these items often requires completing special quests or earning a Renown Score of 10+ with a @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowFactionsAndRe]{faction} that guards the secrets of creating them. For example, an alchemy recipe called “elixir of giants”—which teaches a character to make a @UUID[Compendium.dnd-dungeon-masters-guide.equipment.Item.dmgCloudPotionOf]{Potion of Giant Strength} (cloud)—isn’t commonly known in modern times but can be found in lockboxes and other treasure hoards across Azeroth. (It might require five Gromsblood and five sungrass, both 1,000 GP herbalism resources.)

Artisan recipes sometimes require numerous resources that must first be processed with other professions. For example, making a @UUID[Compendium.dnd-dungeon-masters-guide.equipment.Item.dmgFrostBrand000]{Frost Brand} (Longsword) with blacksmithing could require eighteen arcanite bars, which are thorium bars (250 GP mining resources) that have been combined via alchemy with arcane crystals (100 GP gems). The hilt requires four enchanted leather, which are thick leather (250 GP leather resources) enhanced via enchanting using 1,200 GP of magical residue from disenchanting items. The cold magic in the blade comes from four water elemental essences (available for 100 GP each from specialized vendors). Then these items are combined with four blue sapphires (1,000 GP gems), four Azerothian diamonds (1,000 GP gems), and a dense grinding stone (125 GP mining resource).

Master Recipes. Master recipes can be acquired only as treasure or renown rewards. They often require rare resources or resources found on other worlds or planes of existence. For example, crafting a @UUID[Compendium.dnd-dungeon-masters-guide.equipment.Item.dmgStormPotionOf]{Potion of Giant Strength} (storm) with alchemy might require twenty rising glory—a 5,000 GP herbalism resource that grows only in the Shadowlands realm of Bastion. Similarly, crafting @UUID[Compendium.dnd-dungeon-masters-guide.equipment.Item.dmgPlateArmorOfE]{Plate Armor of Etherealness} with blacksmithing requires a combination of six different minerals found only in the Shadowlands: five laestrite ore (5,000 GP mining resource) and two each of elethium, solenium, phaedrum, sinvyr, and oxxein ore (7,500 GP mining resources), along with 750 GP worth of luminous flux (purchased from a vendor) to aid the mixture of metals.

Disenchanting. When you reach journeyman enchanting skill, you learn to disenchant magic items. If you spend 1 hour (which can be concurrent with a Short Rest) with a permanent magic item that isn’t attuned to someone else, you can remove its magic and store it in the residue, which takes the form of a magical dust or shard. Cloth Resources. Cloth resources have the same range of values as resources collected with gathering professions, from 10 GP linen and 25 GP wool to 7,500 GP dawnweave or duskweave, found only in Khaz Algar. Cloth is sometimes found as treasure in the hands of Humanoids who recognize its value as a trade good.

Rogue.name: Rogue
Rogue.text:
@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.GNYAkpHaiEOPt0a4 caption=false cite=false classes="size-three margin-center noborder"]

Rogues are lethal assassins and masters of stealth, whose preferred tactics include ambushes from the shadows, lethally precise strikes, and combinations of attacks that soften the enemy up for a killing blow. For many rogues, their only code of conduct is their employment contract, and their honor is purchased in gold. Others are loyal to organizations such as Stormwind’s shadowy SI:7, the rebellious Defias Brotherhood, or the Deathstalkers among the Forsaken.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.CzK3sYYg78HdG6b5 caption=false classes="noborder"]

Playing a Rogue.name: Playing a Rogue
Playing a Rogue.text:
To play a rogue, choose the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.classes.Item.phbrgeRogue00000]{Rogue} class from the Player’s Handbook. You can choose one of three specializations to guide your choice of subclass and feats: assassination, outlaw, or subtlety.

Assassination Specialization

Rogues who specialize in assassination use poison extensively, often wielding a pair of daggers coated with deadly toxins.

The following choices will help you focus on this specialization:

Level 1. Choose Daggers and Shortbows for your Weapon Mastery feature.

Level 3. Choose the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.classes.Item.phbrgeAssassin00]{Assassin} subclass.

Level 5. Frequently use the Poison option for your Cunning Strike.

Feats. Consider the following feats at higher levels: @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftActor000000]{Actor}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftAlert000000]{Alert}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftDefensiveDu]{Defensive Duelist}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftPiercer0000]{Piercer}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftPoisoner000]{Poisoner}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftSkulker0000]{Skulker}, and @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftSpeedy00000]{Speedy}.

Outlaw Specialization

Rogues with the outlaw specialization are ruthless swashbucklers who use agility and guile to dominate in combat while standing toe-to-toe with their enemies. Many of these rogues are affiliated with outlaw bands like the Defias Brotherhood and the pirates of Booty Bay.

The following choices will help you focus on this specialization:

Level 1. Choose Daggers and Rapiers for your Weapon Mastery feature.

Level 3. Choose the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.classes.Item.wowrgeSwashbuckl]{Swashbuckler} subclass (see below).

Feats. Consider the following feats at higher levels: @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftAthlete0000]{Athlete}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftDefensiveDu]{Defensive Duelist}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftMartialWeap]{Martial Weapon Training}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftPiercer0000]{Piercer}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftSpeedy00000]{Speedy}, and @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftTough000000]{Tough}.

Subtlety Specialization

Rogues who specialize in subtlety draw on the supernatural magic of the shadows to cloak themselves in darkness and form deadly blades. They strike from hiding, incapacitate their enemies with an overwhelming assault of rapid attacks, and disappear just as quickly back into the shadows.

The following choices will help you focus on this specialization:

Level 1. Choose Daggers and Maces for your Weapon Mastery.

Level 3. Choose the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.classes.Item.phbrgeSoulknife0]{Soulknife} subclass.

Feats. Consider the following feats at higher levels: @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftDualWielder]{Dual Wielder}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftMageSlayer0]{Mage Slayer}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftShadowTouch]{Shadow Touched}, and @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftSkulker0000]{Skulker}.

Overview.name: Overview
Overview.text:
@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.6QAGMUd4PnD7Wo0U caption=false classes="noborder"]

For Level 5–10 and 11-16 Characters • The Scourge

The warriors of the Light have sacrificed much in the campaign to purge the ravening Scourge from the despoiled kingdom of Lordaeron. But pride and loss have warped zeal into fanaticism. The extremists of the Scarlet Crusade believe all who don’t wear their scarlet tabard are plagued. The Crusade has abandoned the Alliance to purge Lordaeron not just of the Scourge, but of all non-humans.

The Scarlet Monastery is the Crusade’s headquarters and looms on the edge of Tirisfal Glades. Scarlet Commander Renault Mograine has transformed this sprawling temple into a fortress.

About Scarlet Monastery

The Scarlet Monastery has been in World of Warcraft from the beginning, first appearing as four linked dungeons. They were designed for five characters, and each was more challenging than the one before it. The graveyard was suitable for characters not yet at the middle of the level range, while the cathedral was a challenge for high-level characters. The four dungeons were simplified into two in the Mists of Pandaria expansion, with many dungeon bosses remaining in place as the Scarlet Crusade resisted all efforts to oust them from their stronghold. During the Burning Legion’s third invasion, however, the Knights of the Ebon Blade wiped out the crusaders and raised High Inquisitor Whitemane as a death knight.

Treasure.name: Treasure
Treasure.text:
When the characters overcome an encounter, roll [[/r 2d6]] on the Scarlet Monastery Treasure table. When they defeat a boss listed below, roll 4d6 or choose the treasure labeled with the boss’s name.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.tables.RollTable.wowScarletMonazC caption=false rangeLabel="4d6" resultLabel="Treasure" rollable nameStyle="h4" no-toc]

Sample Encounters.text:
Use the encounters tables here to help craft planned encounters for key locations within each area of the dungeon. You can also roll on the table if characters make enough noise in the dungeon to attract guards from nearby areas to investigate. If the characters leave the dungeon and return after finishing a Long Rest, new crusaders have mustered in the area. Unless otherwise specified, Humanoid NPCs found in the monastery are Medium and Lawful Evil.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.tables.RollTable.wowGraveyardEnTt caption=false rangeLabel="1d6" resultLabel="Encounter" rollable nameStyle="h4" no-toc]

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.tables.RollTable.wowLibraryEncoak caption=false rangeLabel="1d6" resultLabel="Encounter" rollable nameStyle="h4" no-toc]

†Can cast @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplCureWounds]{Cure Wounds} (level 4 version) once

Scarlet Monastery Areas.name: Scarlet Monastery Areas
Scarlet Monastery Areas.text:
The Scarlet Monastery is a sprawling complex consisting of a graveyard, library, armory, and cathedral. Its exterior is covered with gleaming stained glass windows, which have AC 15 and 30 HP and have Immunity to all damage from sources outside the monastery’s walls. Secret doors within the monastery are standard (DC 15 to detect). The monastery includes these featured areas.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.uKbpUCpy3Ei6V4Im caption=false classes="noborder"]

Scarlet Monastery Adventures.name: Scarlet Monastery Adventures
Scarlet Monastery Adventures.text:
Use the suggestions in the Scarlet Monastery Adventure Hooks table to draw adventurers there. An adventure could take place in one part of the monastery or take the characters from wing to wing.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.tables.RollTable.wowScarletMonahz caption=false rangeLabel="1d6" resultLabel="Adventure Hook" rollable nameStyle="h4" no-toc]

Scarlet Monastery Characters.name: Scarlet Monastery Characters
Scarlet Monastery Characters.text:
These zealots of the Scarlet Crusade train crusaders for future battlefields. Characters are ordered by wing, matching the order in “Scarlet Monastery Areas”: Graveyard, Library, Armory, and Cathedral.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.vAhjF0ozrXGfcWtz caption=false classes="sepia noborder"]

Graveyard.name: Graveyard
Graveyard.text:
Despite the Scarlet Crusade’s unending war against the Scourge, the curse of undeath has taken root within the monastery grounds. The graveyard is suitable for levels 5–10.

Chamber of Atonement. The Chamber of Atonement is a morgue that Interrogator James Vishas (Medium, Lawful Evil @UUID[Compendium.dnd-monster-manual.actors.Actor.mmAssassin000000]{Assassin}) and his torturers ([[/r 1d4 + 1]] @UUID[Compendium.dnd-monster-manual.actors.Actor.mmCultistFanatic]{Cultist Fanatics}) use as a torture chamber, teaching foes and new recruits to fear the Light.

Forlorn Cloister. @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowBloodmageThtE]{Bloodmage Thalnos} (see “Scarlet Monastery Characters”), who haunts the western mausoleum, unwittingly carried the plague of undeath to this graveyard. The lawn smolders with burning corpses. The northern double door leading into the Cathedral is sealed with an Arcane Lock, but the Scarlet Key opens it (see “Athenaeum” below). The secret door leading from the grand vestibule is plainly visible and easy to open from this side.

Library.name: Library
Library.text:
The library wing of the monastery contains plundered treasures. It is suitable for characters of levels 5–10.

Huntsman’s Cloister. Scarlet beastmasters (Medium, Lawful Evil @UUID[Compendium.dnd-monster-manual.actors.Actor.mmScoutCaptain00]{Scout Captains}) train their tracking hounds (@UUID[Compendium.dnd-monster-manual.actors.Actor.mmDireWolf000000]{Dire Wolves}) in the Huntsman’s Cloister. Passing them without being noticed requires a successful [[/check stealth 13 format=long]]. On a failed check, the hounds begin combat, which also draws @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowHoundmasterAY]{Houndmaster Loksey} (see “Scarlet Monastery Characters”) and his three tracking hounds (Dire Wolves) from the south cloister.

Gallery of Treasures. The gallery overflows with gilded and marble art plundered from the few survivors of Lordaeron, ostensibly so the Crusade can protect them. A tapestry on the west wall hides a secret door to the Training Grounds in the Armory.

Athenaeum. The Athenaeum is a series of halls filled with tomes of lore and even heretical works hidden by Arcanist Doan (see “Scarlet Monastery Characters”), who studies in the northernmost chamber. Doan holds the Scarlet Key, which opens the magically locked doors in the grand vestibule and the Forlorn Cloister. A ten-foot-tall portrait of High Inquisitor Sally Whitemane on the west wall hides a secret passage to the Crusader’s Armory.

Armory.name: Armory
Armory.text:
The monastery’s armory is the focal point of its military efforts—training soldiers, housing and equipping soldiers, and commemorating its victories. The armory is suitable for levels 11–16.

Training Grounds. The courtyard has been turned into a target range, and the covered halls on either side are blocked off with iron portcullises. A tapestry on the east wall hides a secret door to the Gallery of Treasures.

Footman’s Armory. The rank-and-file soldiers of the Crusade eat, sleep, and train in the filthy, cavernous cells of the Footman’s Armory. Levers here control portcullises between each cell.

Crusader’s Armory. Elite crusaders instruct their disciples in the Crusader’s Armory. Artillery, battering rams, and explosives line the walls. A ten-foot-tall portrait of Commander Renault Mograine on the west wall hides a secret door to the Athenaeum.

Hall of Champions. Marble statues of the Crusade’s founders, heroes from Stromgarde to Kul Tiras and even to Quel’Thalas (before elves were banished from the Crusade) watch over the Hall of Champions. which is Scarlet Champion Herod’s sparring arena. The westernmost statue (of high elf mage Arellas Fireleaf) has crumbled. Beneath its plinth is a secret passage to a tool room in the Chapel Gardens.

Cathedral.name: Cathedral
Cathedral.text:
The cathedral is the ritual center of the monastery, where its corrupted priests continue to pray to the Holy Light even as they serve the forces of darkness. The cathedral is suitable for levels 11–16.

Chapel Gardens. Statues of crusaders overlook the two-tiered Chapel Gardens. The soil is wet with blood, and the grass is flaked with ashes of “heretics” burned at the stake before the cathedral. Roll for encounters in both the lower and upper gardens.

A tool room to the east of the gardens contains a statue of an ancient crusader-gardener surrounded by hoes, rakes, and shovels. The statue pivots easily to reveal a trap door; a ladder leads down to a tunnel connecting the gardens to the Hall of Champions.

Crusader’s Chapel. @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowScarletCommJv]{Scarlet Commander Mograine} preaches in the Crusader’s Chapel; @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowHighInquisibi]{High Inquisitor Whitemane} prays in the secret crypt behind him and emerges only when Mograine dies (see “Scarlet Monastery Characters” for both). Former High Inquisitor Fairbanks (@UUID[Compendium.dnd-monster-manual.actors.Actor.mmRevenant000000]{Revenant}) is interred in the secret crypt. The door can be opened from within or by pulling a candelabra on the chapel’s altar.

Grand Vestibule.name: Grand Vestibule
Grand Vestibule.text: At any given time, [[/r 2d6]] @UUID[Compendium.dnd-monster-manual.actors.Actor.mmWarriorVeteran]{Warrior Veterans} and [[/r 2d6]] @UUID[Compendium.dnd-monster-manual.actors.Actor.mmMageApprentice]{Mage Apprentices} loiter in the grand vestibule, drinking, brawling, and studying scripture. Two double doors to the north are sealed with Arcane Lock spells, but the Scarlet Key opens them (see “Athenaeum” in “Library”). Pulling a torch sconce in the statueless southwest alcove opens a secret door to the Forlorn Cloister. The grand vestibule is suitable for levels 5–10.

Arcanist Doan.name: Arcanist Doan
Arcanist Doan.text:
“You will not defile this archive’s mysteries!”

Doan was a renowned scholar of purifying magic, particularly cleansing flame. These days, he stews in the monastery’s library, mistrusted by the Crusade’s leaders and longing to prove himself.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.FnbrRbG7jiB7nUx6 caption=false classes="noborder size-four margin-center"]

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowArcanistDoa7u statblock caption=false classes="double-column hide-in-embed"]

Scarlet Champion Herod.name: Scarlet Champion Herod
Scarlet Champion Herod.text:
“Ah, I’ve been waiting for a real challenge.”

Herod is a charming bully who became a dazzling gladiator. The Scarlet Commander keeps him in the monastery to inspire the troops, since his tendency to cleave indiscriminately can make him a liability to his allies in combat.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowScarletChames statblock caption=false classes="double-column hide-in-embed"]

Scarlet Commander Mograine.name: Scarlet Commander Mograine
Scarlet Commander Mograine.text:
“I am the son of the Ashbringer, and we are all children of the Light! It is the one true path to victory!”

Renault Mograine murdered his father in cold blood on the battlefield. He was manipulated into doing so by the dreadlord Balnazzar, but that doesn’t dilute his sin. Renault is haunted but zealous, and he’s oblivious that his Crusade is a sham puppeted by a demon.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.TeTeIN9SPazXeD65 caption=false classes="size-four margin-center noborder"]

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowScarletCommJv statblock caption=false classes="double-column hide-in-embed"]

Bloodmage Thalnos.name: Bloodmage Thalnos
Bloodmage Thalnos.text:
“We hunger for vengeance.”

Thalnos earned repute in the Scarlet Crusade for the brutal, lustrating tortures he inflicted on new recruits. The sadistic mage contracted the plague of undeath but kept his mind. Now he is tormented by his fellow crusaders, who wish to wipe him out even though he craves their blessings.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowBloodmageThtE statblock caption=false classes="double-column hide-in-embed"]

High Inquisitor Sally Whitemane.name: High Inquisitor Sally Whitemane
High Inquisitor Sally Whitemane.text:
“The Light has spoken, for it has found you wanting.”

Sally Whitemane was young when the plague of undeath swept through Lordaeron, and she was forced to raise a blade against her family—mother, father, brothers, sisters—as they turned into the Lich King’s mindless pawns. She doesn’t hold the ideals of the Crusade, but she swore to support her childhood friend Renault Mograine’s quest to destroy undead at any cost.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowHighInquisibi statblock caption=false classes="double-column hide-in-embed"]

Houndmaster Loksey.name: Houndmaster Loksey
Houndmaster Loksey.text:
“Release the hounds!”

Loksey has loved dogs since he was a child, but the fanatical crusade convinced him it was right to send them into war to die. He thinks only purging the unclean can wash the canine blood from his hands.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowHoundmasterAY statblock caption=false classes="double-column hide-in-embed"]

Overview.name: Overview
Overview.text:
For Level 1–4 Characters • Alliance Versus Horde

For generations, Shadowfang Keep has stood on the boundary between Silverpine Forest and the walled kingdom of Gilneas. The keep has been conquered countless times over the years, filling its halls with restless spirits.

Today, this accursed fortress is held by Lord Vincent Godfrey, a treacherous undead who’s a fugitive from both the Alliance and the Horde. Both Packleader Ivar Bloodfang (Medium, Lawful Good Warrior Veteran), a worgen leader who supports the Alliance, and Deathstalker Commander Belmont (Medium Warrior Veteran), a Forsaken leader of the Horde, lead attacks on the fortress, seeking to gain revenge on Lord Godfrey and to claim this crucial redoubt in the war for Silverpine.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.mUcPhx0U7zWXS222 caption=false classes="noborder"]

Shadowfang Keep Areas.name: Shadowfang Keep Areas
Shadowfang Keep Areas.text:
Shadowfang Keep has the following featured areas:

Entry Gate. An iron portcullis blocks access from the keep’s entry to the courtyard. Baron Ashbury (see “Shadowfang Keep Characters”) leads the keep’s defenses from the jail and gatehouse, which leads to the courtyard, and can raise the gate. Skeletons arisen from the keep’s countless defeated assailants prowl here.

Courtyard. This courtyard provides access to the dining hall and the keep’s battlements and rooftops. It is patrolled by Pustulant Monstrosities (see “Shadowfang Keep Characters”) and restless Specters of the keep’s staff.

Silverlaine Manor. The one area of the keep Lord Godfrey couldn’t reclaim is Silverlaine Manor. It is prowled by feral worgen (use the Werewolf stat block without its Bite attack) summoned by the keep’s previous master. The worgen of Gilneas have been unable to negotiate with them.

Dining Hall. A banquet was set here to celebrate Lord Godfrey’s liberation of Pyrewood Village, but the feast now rots untouched. Baron Silverlaine (see “Shadowfang Keep Characters”) haunts the hall, guarded by four Specters of his staff.

Battlements and Rooftops. The ghostly Commander Springvale patrols here with two Springvale’s Specters (see “Shadowfang Keep Characters” for both), watched by leering Gargoyles. Loot from ancient battles is strewn across the battlements.

The Keep. Wooden stairways and catwalks wind up a tower teeming with Undead. Above it is an abandoned magical laboratory that Lord Walden (see “Shadowfang Keep Characters”) is ransacking.

Godfrey’s Chamber. At the keep tower’s apex is the two-story chamber of Lord Godfrey and his two Pustulant Monstrosity bodygards (see “Shadowfang Keep Characters” for both). Its upper floor has collapsed into the first, and he shoots intruders from the top of the stairs while the intruders are busy with the bodyguards below.

About Shadowfang Keep

Shadowfang Keep was a five-player dungeon in the original World of Warcraft, designed for low-level characters to confront the archmage Arugal and the worgen he liberated from the Emerald Dream and set loose on the Eastern Kingdoms. In this first iteration, best suited for level 5–10 characters, the dungeon bosses are the living Arugal (Archmage), the already ghostly forms of Baron Silverlaine and Commander Springvale, and several worgen (Werewolves), some of whose spirits Baron Silverlaine later calls on: Rethilgore, Razorclaw the Butcher, Odo the Blindwatcher, Fenrus the Devourer, and Wolf Master Nandos. Other tormented spirits and ferocious worgs also populate the dungeon.

The version presented in this chapter represents a later stage in the keep’s history, after a group of Forsaken converted the keep into a stronghold to protect themselves from enemies during the Cataclysm.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.RxqUQODavXk67WoU caption=false classes="noborder"]

Shadowfang Keep Characters.name: Shadowfang Keep Characters
Shadowfang Keep Characters.text:
The following characters occupy Shadowfang Keep. They are listed in the order they’re most likely encountered.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.a8wxfis1LG4E6HaT caption=false classes="noborder"]

Shadowfang Keep Adventures.name: Shadowfang Keep Adventures
Shadowfang Keep Adventures.text:
Use the suggestions in the Shadowfang Keep Adventure Hooks table to draw adventurers there.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.tables.RollTable.wowShadowfangKFW caption=false rangeLabel="1d6" resultLabel="Adventure Hook" rollable nameStyle="h4" no-toc]

Treasure.name: Treasure
Treasure.text:
When the characters overcome an encounter, roll [[/r 2d6]] on the Shadowfang Keep Treasure table. When they defeat a boss listed below, roll 4d6 or choose the treasure labeled with its name.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.tables.RollTable.wowShadowfangKZp caption=false rangeLabel="4d6" resultLabel="Treasure" rollable nameStyle="h4" no-toc]

Sample Encounters.name: Sample Encounters
Sample Encounters.text:
Use the Shadowfang Keep Encounters table to help craft planned encounters for key locations within each area of the dungeon. You can also roll on the table if characters make enough noise in the dungeon to attract guards from nearby areas to investigate. If the characters leave the dungeon and return after completing a Long Rest, Lord Godfrey has mustered new undead troops.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.tables.RollTable.wowShadowfangKLh caption=false rangeLabel="1d6" resultLabel="Encounter" rollable nameStyle="h4" no-toc]

Commander Springvale and Specters.name: Commander Springvale and Specters
Commander Springvale and Specters.text:
“Intruders in the keep! To arms!”

Commander Springvale unquestioningly served Baron Silverlaine in the old days. Springvale died on the walls defending his liege lord and patrols them still, unaware that his castle is overrun and his allies are now rotten, shambling corpses.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowCommanderSpHY statblock caption=false classes="double-column hide-in-embed"]

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowSpringvalesID statblock caption=false classes="double-column hide-in-embed"]

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.u3yveXAr0bYQAYQC caption=false classes="sepia noborder"]

Lord Walden.name: Lord Walden
Lord Walden.text:
“Missing pages, broken equipment, tainted samples! How does someone work in these conditions?”

The arrogant Lord Walden, Godfrey’s right-hand man, vowed to pay any price, including death, to serve his compatriot and keep his power. He has adopted the vile alchemy of the Forsaken with aplomb.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowLordWaldenpZL statblock caption=false classes="double-column hide-in-embed"]

Lord Godfrey and Pustulent Monstrosities.name: Lord Godfrey and Pustulent Monstrosities
Lord Godfrey and Pustulent Monstrosities.text:
@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.mUcPhx0U7zWXS222 caption=false classes="float-right size-three noborder"]

“Reduced to ashes … Soon nothing will be left of Gilneas or the worgen taint.”

Lord Vincent Godfrey of Gilneas saw the worgen curse ravage his kingdom. All his life, he had positioned himself to be the true power behind the Gilnean throne, but he broke when he learned that King Genn Greymane had become a worgen. Godfrey threw his life’s work away to spite Greymane. Godfrey and his toady, Baron Ashbury, tried to trade Greymane to the Forsaken in exchange for peace. His attempt failed, and he took his own life on the rocks of the Gilnean coast rather than live in a kingdom of wolves.

The Val’kyr found his shattered corpse and raised him as a Forsaken, though he didn’t swear allegiance to Sylvanas and managed to temporarily incapacitate her when he ransacked Pyrewood Village and conquered the keep overlooking it. Now, hated by both the Alliance and the Horde, he lurks within Shadowfang Keep, hatching a scheme that will allow him to emerge the one true victor in the war for Gilneas.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowLordGodfreyj7 statblock caption=false classes="double-column hide-in-embed"]

Pustulant Monstrosities. Pustulent monstrosities are powerful zombies found throughout Shadowfang Keep, and in particular alongside Lord Godfrey in his chamber. They are shambling hulks covered with oozing pustules filled with deadly toxin.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowPustulantMo4p statblock caption=false classes="hide-in-embed"]

Baron Silverlaine.name: Baron Silverlaine
Baron Silverlaine.text:
@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.LeZXPQd8dIaE74PE caption=false classes="sepia noborder"]

“Leave this accursed place at once!”

I tend to believe that restless spirits and all other beings deserve a nice, long rest.

—Chromie

Baron Silverlaine was master of Shadowfang Keep before it fell to Arugal’s feral worgen. His cursed spirit calls on the beasts that slaughtered him to punish trespassers. He is bound to the stones of the keep and has no loyalty to Godfrey or any of the keep’s masters.

Baron Ashbury.name: Baron Ashbury
Baron Ashbury.text:
“Tally ho! The hunt begins!”

A noble of Gilneas and a patriot who betrayed his king, Baron Ashbury was raised as an undead Forsaken when Sylvanas Windrunner’s army attacked his homeland. Now an enemy of both the worgen of Gilneas and the Forsaken, he serves the only master left to him: Lord Godfrey.

Shaman.name: Shaman
Shaman.text:
@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.OGW32USNcQ0MFGq6 caption=false cite=false classes="size-three margin-center noborder"]

Shaman are spiritual adepts who commune with the elemental forces of the world and channel their power. These elemental forces are chaotic and, left to their own devices, would rage against each other in unending primal fury. A shaman’s call is to bring balance to this chaos, acting as a moderator among air, earth, fire, and water. A shaman’s magic focuses the elements to support the shaman’s allies or punish those who threaten them.

Shaman are fierce warriors who wield their elemental magic as totems placed on the ground or auras that surround the shaman, rather than traditional spellcasting.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.LswMh8ON4EvDSEIs classes="noborder"]

Playing a Shaman.name: Playing a Shaman
Playing a Shaman.text:
To play a shaman, choose the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.classes.Item.phbbrbBarbarian0]{Barbarian} class from the Player’s Handbook. At level 3, you gain the Totems feature described below instead of the Primal Knowledge feature. You can choose one of three specializations to guide your choice of subclass, feats, and weapons: elemental, enhancement, or restoration.

Creating a Shaman

When you add the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.classes.Item.phbbrbBarbarian0]{Barbarian} class to your character sheet you will be given the option to pick between the Barbarian and the Shaman.

Adopting the Barbarian class as a shaman, either at character creation or through multiclassing, increases a character’s Renown Score with the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowEarthenRing00]{Earthen Ring} by 3 (see chapter 4).

Level 3: Totems

This feature replaces the Barbarian’s Primal Knowledge feature.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.classes.Item.wowbrbTotem00000 inline]

Elemental Specialization

Shaman with the elemental specialization dedicate themselves to forging deep bonds with the elements. Inspired by visions of an ancient past where manifestations of volatile energy once raged unimpeded across primordial Azeroth, these shaman devote themselves to channeling such power into destructive magical surges. The raw elemental energy of storms—lightning, fire, and cold—flow through their bodies as they summon spirits to their aid.

The following choices will help you focus on this specialization:

Level 1. Choose any two of Battleaxes, Longswords, or Maces for your Weapon Mastery feature.

Level 3. Choose the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.classes.Item.wowbrbPathElemen]{Path of the Elements} subclass (see below). You also gain the Totems feature in place of the Barbarian’s Primal Knowledge feature, as described above.

Feats. Consider the following feats at higher levels: @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftAthlete0000]{Athlete}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftCrusher0000]{Crusher}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftDurable0000]{Durable}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftMediumArmor]{Medium Armor Master}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftRitualCaste]{Ritual Caster}, and @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftSlasher0000]{Slasher}.

Enhancement Specialization

Shaman who specialize in enhancement empower their physical attacks with elemental energy as they wade into the thick of combat. They supplement their augmented weapon attacks with potent elemental strikes and totems.

The following choices will help you focus on this specialization:

Level 1. Choose any two of Handaxes, Light Hammers, Scimitars, or Shortswords for your Weapon Mastery feature.

Level 3. Choose the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.classes.Item.wowbrbPathSpirit]{Path of the Spiritual Guardian} subclass (see below). You also gain the Totems feature in place of the Barbarian’s Primal Knowledge feature, as described above.

Feats. Consider the following feats at higher levels: @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftAthlete0000]{Athlete}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftCharger0000]{Charger}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftCrusher0000]{Crusher}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftDualWielder]{Dual Wielder}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftDurable0000]{Durable}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftMediumArmor]{Medium Armor Master}, and @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftSlasher0000]{Slasher}.

Restoration Specialization

Shaman who specialize in restoration find a serene affinity for the restorative properties of water. They feel a profound spiritual connection with the source from which all mortal life takes root, and they wield that power to restore vitality to their allies. These shaman balance this healing focus with a command of the other elements, finding harmony in nature and purifying their allies as a tidal surge washes across a sandy shore.

The following choices will help you focus on this specialization:

Level 1. Choose any two of Flails, Maces, or Warhammers for your Weapon Mastery feature.

Level 3. Choose the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.classes.Item.phbbrbWorldTree0]{Path of the World Tree} subclass. You also gain the Totems feature in place of the Barbarian’s Primal Knowledge feature, as described above.

Feats. Consider the following feats at higher levels: @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftChef0000000]{Chef}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftCrusher0000]{Crusher}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftDurable0000]{Durable}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftInspiringLe]{Inspiring Leader}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftMediumArmor]{Medium Armor Master}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftSentinel000]{Sentinel}, and @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftShieldMaste]{Shield Master}.

Path of the Spiritual Guardian (Barbaria.name: Path of the Spiritual Guardian (Barbarian Subclass)

Introduction.name: Introduction
Introduction.text: The Steamwheedle Cartel is one of the largest and richest goblin cartels, having maintained a careful neutrality in the conflict between @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowTheAlliance00]{the Alliance} and @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowTheHorde00000]{the Horde} since the Second War (and a generally Neutral alignment). From its headquarters in Gadgetzan (in Tanaris), the cartel oversees operations across Azeroth and even Outland. It also runs Booty Bay (in Stranglethorn), Ratchet (in the Northern Barrens), and Everlook (in Winterspring), as well as smaller outposts. The cartel’s hands are in virtually every line of work, with a specialty in premium-grade alchemy (at least since the alchemist Marin Noggenfogger assumed the position of trade prince). Besides potions, the cartel also deals in fuels, poisons, and industrial chemicals—what some goblins describe as “liquid assets.”

Steamwheedle Cartel Renown Perks.name: Steamwheedle Cartel Renown Perks
Steamwheedle Cartel Renown Perks.text:
Establishing your Bastion in Gadgetzan or another Steamwheedle Cartel territory increases your Renown Score with the Steamwheedle Cartel by 1.

Increasing your Renown Score with the Steamwheedle Cartel gives you the following additional benefits. (Steamwheedle Cartel merchants appear in many locations across the world, making their discounts particularly notable.)

Steamwheedle Cartel: Friendly

Prerequisite: Renown 3+ with the Steamwheedle Cartel

You can spend 30 days with a trainer to learn the Goblin language or gain proficiency with @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.equipment.Item.phbtulAlchemists]{Alchemist’s Supplies} or @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.equipment.Item.phbtulTinkersToo]{Tinker’s Tools} (see the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowTheAlliance00.JournalEntryPage.atJHGssGcTvG0dWQ]{Training} sidebar earlier in this chapter).

Steamwheedle Cartel: Honored

Prerequisite: Renown 10+ with the Steamwheedle Cartel

You can request a supply of [[/r 1d4]] flasks of @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.items.Item.wowNoggenfoggeLg]{Noggenfogger Elixir} from the leaders of the cartel before you undertake a quest on their behalf. Once you request these elixirs, you can’t do so again until your Renown Score with the cartel increases.

Steamwheedle Cartel: Revered

Prerequisite: Renown 25+ with the Steamwheedle Cartel

You can purchase an @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.items.Item.wowExperimentalG]{Experimental Goblin Jetpack} from the Steamwheedle Cartel for 2,000 GP (with no further discount).

Steamwheedle Cartel: Exalted

Prerequisite: Renown 50+ with the Steamwheedle Cartel

You can purchase a Steamwheedle Apparatus (which functions as an @UUID[Compendium.dnd-dungeon-masters-guide.equipment.Item.dmgApparatusOfKw]{Apparatus of Kwalish}) from the Steamwheedle Cartel for 100,000 GP (with no further discount).

Tauren.name: Tauren
Tauren.text:
@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.nQ8rWLHbSmivoNsA classes="hide-in-embed noborder"]

The tauren are descended from the yak-like yaungol, who roamed the great plains at the heart of the unbroken continent of Kalimdor millennia before the Great Sundering. The yaungol were enslaved and magically altered by the titan-forged mogu, whose infection with the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowConflictsOfAz.JournalEntryPage.QX2LRHkL98AMmC55]{Old Gods}’ curse of flesh made them fierce and tyrannical. After winning their freedom from the mogu alongside the pandaren and other peoples of that region, many of the yaungol fled north. Some settled in the area surrounding the Well of Eternity, where they reunited with the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowTheWorldOfWar.JournalEntryPage.Jm2kfPalxs8mphjd#wild-gods]{Wild God} Cenarius and relearned their ancient traditions of druidic magic. The magic of the Well of Eternity reshaped these yaungol into the tauren.

After the Great Sundering, the tauren roamed the plains of the Barrens for countless generations, hunting the mighty kodos and seeking the wisdom of their eternal goddess, the Earth Mother. Scattered across the land, the wandering tribes were united only by a common hatred for their sworn enemy, marauding centaur bands. Seeking aid against these foes, the chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof befriended Warchief Thrall and the other orcs who had journeyed with Thrall to Kalimdor.

With the orcs’ help, Cairne and his Bloodhoof tribe drove back the centaur bands and claimed the grasslands of Mulgore for their own. For the first time in centuries, the tauren had their own land. On the windswept mesa of Thunder Bluff, Cairne built a refuge where tauren of every tribe are welcome. Over time, the tauren tribes united under Cairne’s rule. Since Cairne’s death, his son, Baine, has led Thunder Bluff with calm wisdom and moderation.

Despite their allegiance to @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowTheHorde00000]{the Horde}, the tauren—and particularly those among them who follow druidic ways—respect the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowElf0000000000.JournalEntryPage.C4fRQxnWgEHPPK1W]{night elves} of Kalimdor. The archdruids of Thunder Bluff have long cooperated with night elf druids in the Cenarion Circle, working together to preserve Azeroth, though their partnership has been strained since it began during the War of the Ancients, ten thousand years ago.

Highmountain Tauren.name: Highmountain Tauren
Highmountain Tauren.text: The tauren of the Broken Isles are direct descendants of the tauren (led by Huln Highmountain) who fought alongside the night elves in the War of the Ancients. During the war, Cenarius blessed Huln and his followers with a perpetual sign of his favor: the Horns of Eche’ro, which manifest as antlers like those of a moose. To this day, Highmountain tauren decorate and inscribe their antlers with signs of tribe affiliation and status.

Taunka.name: Taunka
Taunka.text: Taunka are the direct descendants of the ancient yaungol. Before the Great Sundering, they settled in the Storm Peaks (in what would become Northrend) and adapted to the harsh environment. In contrast to the peaceful shamanism of the Mulgore tauren, taunka shaman wrest power from the hostile elemental forces of Northrend.

Tauren Renown.name: Tauren Renown
Tauren Renown.text: Your Renown Score with @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowTheHorde00000.JournalEntryPage.dy8Z8Gtvbu98gfQc]{Thunder Bluff} (Horde) begins at 3.

Tauren Traits.name: Tauren Traits
Tauren Traits.text:
Creature Type: Humanoid
Size: Medium (about 8–9 feet tall)
Speed: 30 feet

As a Tauren, you have these special traits.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.origins.Item.wowsptHorns00000 caption=false cite=false nameStyle=inline]
