Warlock.name: Warlock
Warlock.text:
@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.rHVwZK9JDD5zqvRa caption=false cite=false classes="size-three margin-center noborder"]

Throughout the ages, many mortals have bargained with the demonic forces of the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowConflictsOfAz.JournalEntryPage.mOeoKWAu3OOx8LP9]{Burning Legion} and the entities of the Void to gain power. To these warlocks, the destructive might of demons isn’t something to be feared, but an opportunity to be coveted. The worst of them seek domination over others. The best of them wield demonic power as a weapon against the demons it comes from, turning the might of the Burning Legion against itself.

Warlocks summon demon minions to fight alongside them—wretched imps, loyal @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.actors.Actor.wowVoidwalkerBzr]{voidwalkers}, manipulative sayaad (succubi and incubi), relentless felhunters, and more. While their minions harry their enemies, warlocks scour their foes with searing flames, demonic corruption, and ravaging curses.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.Lxd1vkKRRGMzor4o caption=false classes="noborder"]

Playing a Warlock.name: Playing a Warlock
Playing a Warlock.text:
To play a warlock, choose the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.actors.Actor.phbprgWarlock000]{Warlock} class from the Player’s Handbook. You can choose one of three specializations to guide your choice of subclass, spells, and Eldritch Invocations: affliction, demonology, or destruction.

Affliction Specialization

Affliction warlocks draw primarily on the power of @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowTheWorldOfWar.JournalEntryPage.39WbPfMoJEVvbg15]{the Void}, a power often called shadow magic. Their spells cause intense pain, corrupting minds and agonizing souls, leaving their enemies in a state of ongoing torment.

Warlock Patrons

The @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.classes.Item.phbwlkFiendPatro]{Fiend Patron} subclass draws on the powers of the fel forces of the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowConflictsOfAz.JournalEntryPage.mOeoKWAu3OOx8LP9]{Burning Legion}. The @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.classes.Item.phbwlkGreatOldOn]{Great Old One Patron} subclass gains its magic from the powers of the Void, including the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowConflictsOfAz.JournalEntryPage.QX2LRHkL98AMmC55]{Old Gods}. Any given Warlock might have a multitude of both fel and Void patrons, but a Warlock’s subclass shapes their spells and other abilities.

The following choices will help you focus on this specialization (Eldritch Invocations marked with an asterisk are described in @UUID[.zzpm5eftIkMnFXZ9]{Eldritch Invocations} in this section):

Level 1. Choose the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.classes.Item.wowinvPactLegion]{Pact of the Legion*} Eldritch Invocation. Choose the following cantrips: @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplEldritchBl]{Eldritch Blast} and @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplPoisonSpra]{Poison Spray}. Prepare the following spells to start: @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplHex0000000]{Hex} and @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplWitchBolt0]{Witch Bolt}.

Level 2. Choose these Eldritch Invocations: @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.classes.Item.phbinvAgonizingB]{Agonizing Blast} and @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.classes.Item.wowinvCurseCorru]{Curse of Corruption*}.

Level 3. Choose the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.classes.Item.phbwlkGreatOldOn]{Great Old One Patron} subclass.

Eldritch Invocations. Consider the following Eldritch Invocations as you reach level 5 and higher: @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.classes.Item.wowinvCallVoid00]{Call of the Void*}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.classes.Item.phbinvEldritchMi]{Eldritch Mind}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.classes.Item.phbinvGiftoftheD]{Gift of the Depths}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.classes.Item.wowinvLegionSumm]{Legion Summoning*}, and Visions of Distant Realms.

Demonology Specialization

Demonology warlocks harness the power of demons on the field of battle. They harvest soul energy from their foes and use it to pull abominations from the chaos of the Twisting Nether, maintaining absolute control over the summoned creatures.

The following choices will help you focus on this specialization (Eldritch Invocations marked with an asterisk are described in @UUID[.zzpm5eftIkMnFXZ9]{Eldritch Invocations} in this section):

Level 1. Choose the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.classes.Item.wowinvPactLegion]{Pact of the Legion*} Eldritch Invocation. Choose the following cantrips: @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplEldritchBl]{Eldritch Blast} and @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplTolltheDea]{Toll the Dead}. Prepare the following spells to start: @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplArmsofHada]{Arms of Hadar} and @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplHex0000000]{Hex}.

Level 2. Choose these Eldritch Invocations: @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.classes.Item.wowinvHealthFunn]{Health Funnel*} and @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.classes.Item.phbinvRepellingB]{Repelling Blast}.

Level 3. Choose the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.classes.Item.phbwlkFiendPatro]{Fiend Patron} subclass.

Eldritch Invocations: Consider the following Eldritch Invocations as you reach level 5 and higher: @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.classes.Item.wowinvCallVoid00]{Call of the Void*}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.classes.Item.wowinvExpendMini]{Expendable Minions*}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.classes.Item.phbinvGiftoftheD]{Gift of the Depths}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.classes.Item.wowinvLegionSumm]{Legion Summoning*}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.classes.Item.wowinvMasterDemo]{Master Demonologist*}, and @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.classes.Item.phbinvVisionsOfD]{Visions of Distant Realms}.

Destruction Specialization

Destruction warlocks favor magic of pure chaos and aggression in battle. They wield shadow, fire, fel, and raw chaos magic with equal ease, rattling the souls and immolating the flesh of their foes. They revel in the sheer destruction they cause, thrilling at the opportunity to watch the world burn.

The following choices will help you focus on this specialization (Eldritch Invocations marked with an asterisk are described in @UUID[.zzpm5eftIkMnFXZ9]{Eldritch Invocations} in this section):

Summon Fiend

When you cast @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplSummonFien]{Summon Fiend} as a Warlock, the fiendish spirit resembles a demon of the Burning Legion: an infernal (choose the Devil option), a demonic tyrant (choose the Yugoloth option), or a vilefiend (choose the Demon option).

Level 1. Choose the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.classes.Item.wowinvPactLegion]{Pact of the Legion*} Eldritch Invocation. Choose the following cantrips: @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplEldritchBl]{Eldritch Blast} and @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplThundercla]{Thunderclap}. Prepare the following spells to start: @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplHellishReb]{Hellish Rebuke} and @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplHex0000000]{Hex}.

Level 2. Choose these Eldritch Invocations: @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.classes.Item.phbinvAgonizingB]{Agonizing Blast} and @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.classes.Item.phbinvRepellingB]{Repelling Blast}.

Level 3. Choose the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.classes.Item.phbwlkFiendPatro]{Fiend Patron} subclass.

Warrior.name: Warrior
Warrior.text:
@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.6EwICmYWPyR8U5fl caption=false cite=false classes="size-three margin-center noborder"]

For as long as war has raged, heroes of every people have aimed to master the art of battle. Warriors combine strength, leadership, and a vast knowledge of arms and armor to wreak havoc in glorious combat. Across cultures and kingdoms, those who demonstrate great physical aptitude undergo tests and training to build their strength, endurance, and fighting capability, forging them into the greatest warriors.

Some warriors protect others from the front lines with shields, locking down enemies while allies support the warrior from behind with spell and bow. Others forgo the shield and unleash their rage at the closest threat with a variety of deadly weapons.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.W2MgbAET6K07HD21 caption=false classes="noborder"]

Playing a Warrior.name: Playing a Warrior
Playing a Warrior.text:
To play a warrior, choose the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.classes.Item.phbftrFighter000]{Fighter} class from the Player’s Handbook. You can choose one of three specializations to guide your choice of subclass, spells, and feats: arms, fury, or protection.

Creating a Warrior

When you add the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.classes.Item.phbftrFighter000]{Fighter} class to your character sheet you will be given the option to pick between the Fighter and the Warrior.

Arms Specialization

Warriors’ choices of weapons and fighting style determine their role on the battlefield. Arms warriors favor two-handed weapons that allow them to deliver devastating blows. These warriors combine these overpowering attacks with heightened mobility to strike where their foes are least defended.

The following choices will help you focus on this specialization:

Level 1. Choose @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbfstGreatWeapo]{Great Weapon Fighting} for a Fighting Style feat. Choose at least one of Greataxes, Greatswords, or Mauls for your Weapon Mastery feature.

Level 3. Choose the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.classes.Item.phbftrBattleMast]{Battle Master} subclass. Consider the following maneuvers: @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.classes.Item.wowmnvBattleShou]{Battle Shout*}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.classes.Item.phbmnvDisarmingA]{Disarming Attack}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.classes.Item.phbmnvDistractin]{Distracting Strike}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.classes.Item.wowmnvMortalStri]{Mortal Strike*}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.classes.Item.phbmnvPushingAtt]{Pushing Attack}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.classes.Item.phbmnvSweepingAt]{Sweeping Attack}, and @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.classes.Item.phbmnvTripAttack]{Trip Attack}. Maneuvers marked with an asterisk are described below.

Feats. Consider the following feats at higher levels: @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftCharger0000]{Charger}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftCrusher0000]{Crusher}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftGreatWeapon]{Great Weapon Master}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftPiercer0000]{Piercer}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftSpeedy00000]{Speedy}, and @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftSlasher0000]{Slasher}.

Fury Specialization

Through a lifetime of training and sparring, fury warriors become masters of carnage, wielding a weapon in each hand to maximize the destruction they cause. Though they forgo the protection of a shield, they surround themselves with whirling blades that leave little opportunity for their opponents to strike without suffering grievous wounds in return. Fury warriors dive into the fray in a breathtaking display of brute force, savoring the frenzy of battle.

The following choices will help you focus on this specialization:

Level 1. Choose @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbfstTwoWeaponF]{Two-Weapon Fighting} for a Fighting Style feat. Choose Scimitars among your other weapons for your Weapon Mastery feature.

Level 3. Choose the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.classes.Item.phbftrChampion00]{Champion} subclass.

Feats. Consider the following feats at higher levels: @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftCharger0000]{Charger}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftCrusher0000]{Crusher}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftDualWielder]{Dual Wielder}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftPiercer0000]{Piercer}, and @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftSlasher0000]{Slasher}.

Protection Specialization

Protection warriors favor a more measured approach to battle than other warriors, countering incoming attacks and using their shields to protect their allies as well as themselves. For the protection warrior, being the toughest soldier on the battlefield means nothing if allies are left vulnerable. These warriors stand as an unbreakable wall protecting their friends from their foes.

Berserker Barbarians

Although D&D’s Fighter class is the best match for a warrior in World of Warcraft, you could also play a @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.classes.Item.phbbrbBarbarian0]{Barbarian}. Choose the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.classes.Item.phbbrbBerserker0]{Path of the Berserker} subclass, and otherwise follow the guidance for building a fury warrior as a Fighter.

The following choices will help you focus on this specialization:

Level 1. Choose @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbfstIntercepti]{Interception} or @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbfstProtection]{Protection} for a Fighting Style feat. Choose at least one of Battleaxes, Longswords, or Morningstars for your Weapon Mastery feature.

Level 3. Choose the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.classes.Item.phbftrBattleMast]{Battle Master} subclass. Consider the following maneuvers: @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.classes.Item.phbmnvBaitandSwi]{Bait and Switch}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.classes.Item.wowmnvBattleShou]{Battle Shout*}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.classes.Item.wowmnvDemoraShou]{Demoralizing Shout*}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.classes.Item.phbmnvGoadingAtt]{Goading Attack}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.classes.Item.phbmnvManeuverin]{Maneuvering Attack}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.classes.Item.phbmnvParry00000]{Parry}, and @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.classes.Item.wowmnvWardinMane]{Warding Maneuver*}, Maneuvers marked with an asterisk are described below.

Feats. Consider the following feats at higher levels: @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftCrusher0000]{Crusher}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftDurable0000]{Durable}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftHeavyArmorM]{Heavy Armor Master}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftPiercer0000]{Piercer}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftSentinel000]{Sentinel}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftShieldMaste]{Shield Master,} and @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.feats.Item.phbftSlasher0000]{Slasher}.

Worgen.name: Worgen
Worgen.text:
@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.34jWFQ8VLIwj6VPF classes="hide-in-embed noborder"]

The worgen curse originated among a sect of @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowElf0000000000.JournalEntryPage.C4fRQxnWgEHPPK1W]{night elf} druids called the Druids of the Pack during the War of the Satyr, over nine thousand years ago. The druids adopted a feral “pack form” inspired by the lupine @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowTheWorldOfWar.JournalEntryPage.Jm2kfPalxs8mphjd#wild-gods]{Wild God} Goldrinn, but they succumbed to the bestial rage of this form. Attempting to bring their rage under control, a druid crafted the Scythe of Elune (with the help of a night elf priestess, Belysra Starbreeze), which instead transformed the druids into the first worgen. As they fought fiercely against the satyrs, the worgen spread their curse to other night elves, leading Malfurion Stormrage to banish the worgen to the Emerald Dream.

Thousands of years later, during the Third War, a @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowKirinTor00000]{Kirin Tor} archmage named Arugal summoned worgen from the Emerald Dream to defend the human kingdom of Gilneas from the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowConflictsOfAz.JournalEntryPage.YRwQ3wrLM22odUUP]{Scourge}—but accidentally unleashed them and their curse on Gilneas.

Night elf druids (along with Belysra), feeling responsible for the worgen curse, taught Gilnean worgen a rite called the Ritual of Balance, which helps them control their transformation and retain clear minds in worgen form. The night elves’s aid and the worgen’s kinship with the humans of Stormwind ushered the Gilnean worgen into @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowTheAlliance00]{the Alliance}.

World of Azeroth.name: World of Azeroth
World of Azeroth.text:
@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.LKUtKnAXJSHoGX91 caption=false]

Azeroth is a realm not merely shaped by war, but defined by it. No region, no nation, arguably not one contiguous square mile has escaped it. Wars have raged through all the ages.

When modern citizens of Azeroth contemplate war, most think first of the long-running conflict between @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowTheAlliance00]{the Alliance} and @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowTheHorde00000]{the Horde}. This struggle is the cause of three of the great wars of modern history. Yet the Alliance–Horde struggle is but one of many conflicts: tribe against tribe, nation against nation, mortals against demons, mantid versus pandaren, naga incursions against land dwellers, the forces of nature against corruptions of the Old Gods.

This dreadful cycle has raged at least ten millennia, since the Highborne night elves drew the cosmic eye of Sargeras the Destroyer because of their exorbitant use of the Well of Eternity. The corrupted titan gathered countless demons he had imprisoned in Mardum, the Plane of Banishment, and unleashed them on Azeroth as the Burning Legion.

This War of the Ancients wreaked untold destruction and led to the devastation of the Great Sundering. Continents shattered and land sank into the oceans, reshaping coastlines. The Well of Eternity was destroyed and became the Great Sea’s all-­consuming Maelstrom.

In those grim days, extinction loomed, and the seeds of most of Azeroth’s subsequent rivalries and hatreds were planted.

The world has been at war ever since.

Yet Azeroth is more than just a giant battlefield. In villages, cities, and towns, people work, worship, celebrate, and love. Natural wonders from vast forests to lush grasslands stretch between mountain and river, hill and sea.

Life thrives and civilization endures. Secret magic and lost technologies wait to be rediscovered in the deepest dungeons—marvels that, depending on who finds them first, could improve lives or end them en masse. Villains and monsters, many unrelated to the ongoing wars, threaten the innocent.

Azeroth is a world that might never lose its need for soldiers, but more than that, it needs heroes.

Alliance and Horde.name: Alliance and Horde
Alliance and Horde.text:
An armistice has held the Alliance and the Horde in a semblance of peace since the end of the Fourth War. Yet their conflict continues through scattered skirmishes on a hundred fronts—even in regions that largely stayed outside this terrible struggle.

Some areas are under the control of one faction or the other, and members of the opposing faction are unwelcome. Most areas are contested—both factions have a presence, and open conflict sometimes erupts there. A few neutral places welcome members of both factions and frown on conflict. The druidic territory of Moonglade (in Kalimdor) is a prime example of a neutral territory; druids set aside their factional differences to learn and commune with nature together in this tranquil valley.

Kalimdor.name: Kalimdor
Kalimdor.text:
Kalimdor is the broken western remnant of the much larger continent of the same name that was torn apart during the Great Sundering. It still bears the scars of that ancient catastrophe and the more recent Cataclysm wrought by Deathwing.

The northern forests and mountains of Kalimdor bear the imprint of thousands of years of @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowElf0000000000.JournalEntryPage.C4fRQxnWgEHPPK1W]{night elf} civilization. Night elves built majestic cities before the War of the Ancients, and the ruins of cities such as Mathystra, Ameth’Aran, Ordil’Aran, and Kel’Theril still remain.

Night elves zealously defend the portions of Northern Kalimdor they still hold, as this is the heart of their former empire and the home of the World Trees. The night elves joined the Alliance to face the Horde, but a significant minority consider both factions equally distasteful. They maintain that their home territories belong to the night elves alone; @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowHuman00000000]{humans}, furbolgs, and @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowDraenei000000]{draenei} are no more welcome than @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowOrc0000000000]{orcs}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowTroll00000000]{trolls}, or @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowGoblin0000000]{goblins}. Some of these night elves keep to themselves, but others wage a guerrilla insurgency against all other groups, adding more uncertainty to areas torn by struggles between the Alliance and the Horde.

Southern Kalimdor is a blasted and broken land that bears the scars of the Cataclysm, the failed experiments of titans, the castoffs of the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowConflictsOfAz.JournalEntryPage.QX2LRHkL98AMmC55]{Old Gods}, and the ruins of empires older than the night elf civilization to the north. From flooded chasms to baking deserts, it is a place of misery, want, and ancient death, with only a few stretches of verdant forest or savanna in which life can thrive.

A defining feature of Southern Kalimdor is the remnant of the ancient qiraji empire. Fallen spires, broken towers, and sand-buried avenues are testaments to an empire formed by the the insectile qiraji, who were corrupted by the influence of the imprisoned Old God C’Thun. By accessing the prison-­laboratory of the titans, the qiraji learned secrets now buried with the rest of their nation.

Kalimdor Regions

Kalimdor stretches from the charred remains of Teldrassil in the northwest, across the Great Divide that cuts across the Barrens, and down to the southern tip of Uldum.

Ahn’Qiraj. Ahn’Qiraj, the fallen kingdom of the insectile qiraji, is a wasted ruin older than most civilizations, still containing ancient horrors linked to the Old Gods. (Contested; 17–20)

Ashenvale. Tensions between night elves in the north and west and Horde loggers in the south and east have long defined the lush forest of Ashenvale. (Contested; 5–10)

Azshara. Azshara is a region cloaked in eternal autumn, stalked by naga, and haunted by ghosts. It has been partially pacified by @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowTheHorde00000.JournalEntryPage.KTz4fgoqdKuVuqzy]{Bilgewater Cartel} goblins. (Horde; 5–10)

Azuremyst Isles. Consisting of Azuremyst Isle and the neighboring Bloodmyst Isle, the Azuremyst Isles have been under the uncontested control of the draenei since their arrival in the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowTheAlliance00.JournalEntryPage.xwHnObtfS8KGOgNp]{Exodar}. Bloodmyst Isle, though, is polluted by an arcane red mist that chokes the land and causes dangerous mutations of local fauna. (Alliance; 1–4)

Darkshore. The shadow-choked strip of coastline called Darkshore is littered with the monster-occupied ruins of ancient night elf fortifications as well as recent battlefields. (Alliance; 1–4)

Desolace. Having grown increasingly green and fertile since the climate-altering effects of the Cataclysm, the former wasteland of Desolace is now the site of constant struggle between the Alliance, the Horde, the Burning Blade, the Cenarion Circle, and multiple centaur tribes. (Contested; 5–10)

Durotar. Durotar is a harsh region of dusty badlands, deep canyons, flooding rivers, and vicious predators. It is also the new homeland of the orcs and a haven for all the Horde. (Horde; 1–4)

Dustwallow Marsh. Neither the Alliance nor the Horde has made much headway in Dustwallow Marsh, a viciously inhospitable wetland. The Alliance holds a few outposts of the now obliterated Theramore Isle, and a few small communities such as Brackenwall Village and Mudsprocket support the Horde. (Contested; 11–16)

Felwood. The corrupted forest of Felwood, full of infernally tainted elementals and rotting treants, stands between Alliance and Horde territories. It is a highly contested land; neither side wants it, but neither side can afford to cede it. (Contested; 11–16)

Feralas. Deadly clans and communities of local inhabitants, of which the Gordunni ogres are the most numerous, prevent both the Alliance and the Horde from claiming much of the resource-rich Feralas jungle. (Contested; 11–16)

Moonglade. Cenarion Circle druids and their powerful Moonglade Warden guards swiftly quash any sectarian violence that threatens the peace of the lush Moonglade vale. (Neutral; 11–16)

Mount Hyjal. Boasting the roots of the World Tree Nordrassil and the Second Well of Eternity beneath its peak, Mount Hyjal is frequently the target of countless factions, armies, and would-be warlords who desperately seek its power. (Contested; 17–20)

Mulgore. The game-rich grasslands of Mulgore are tauren’s ancestral home. While this area is relatively peaceful, it is also the home of dangerous beasts and the violent extremists of the Grimtotem tribe. (Horde; 1–4)

Northern Barrens. The vast savanna of the Northern Barrens is now separated from the south by the lava-filled Great Divide. Horde warriors coming of age use this region to prove their readiness for battle. (Horde; 1–4)

Silithus. Silithus is a blazing desert containing portions of lost Ahn’Qiraj. Despite dangers such as the all-consuming silithid, the allure of the mystical Silithyst crystal dust attracts the interest of Alliance, Horde, and independent explorers.

At the end of the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowConflictsOfAz.JournalEntryPage.mOeoKWAu3OOx8LP9]{Burning Legion}’s third invasion of Azeroth, Sargeras tried to destroy the world by plunging his enormous sword into the heart of the planet. He struck Silithus, creating a massive wound that now dominates the desert surrounding the titan’s sword. The wound has caused the lifeblood of Azeroth to seep to the surface, not just in Silithus but across the world, in the form of a mineral called Azerite. Efforts to control the damage and heal the wound continue. (Contested; 11–16)

Southern Barrens. After the Southern Barrens were blasted by Deathwing and rocked by earthquakes during the Cataclysm, many local Horde strongholds were lost or abandoned. The Alliance has since launched multiple incursions into this ill-defended region. (Contested; 5–10)

Stonetalon Mountains. The slopes of the Stonetalon Mountains are home to fortified outposts of the Alliance and the Horde. Stonetalon Peak houses caverns sacred to tauren and night elves who, despite their allegiance to opposing factions, avoid shedding blood on holy ground. (Contested; 5–10)

Tanaris. The desert of Tanaris is haunted by many of the same monsters as Silithus, but it also serves as home to the Steamwheedle Cartel goblins in communities such as Steamwheedle Port and Gadgetzan. (Contested; 11–16)

Teldrassil. Formerly one of the great World Trees, Teldrassil was burned during the War of Thorns. Night elves work to restore life to its charred remnants and rebuild the community it once held. (Alliance; 1–4)

Thousand Needles. Countless stone spires and small mesas rise from the waters of a massive flooded canyon, giving the Thousand Needles region its name. Many of these islets host camps and small communities that must deal with pirates and dangerous fauna. (Contested; 11–16)

Uldum. The wastes of Uldum, which link the larger deserts of Silithus and Tanaris, are home to the feline tol’vir—and to uncounted creations and weapons of the ancient titans. (Contested; 17–20)

Un’Goro Crater. Full of surprisingly lush greenery considering its position amid great deserts, Un’Goro Crater might have served as both home and laboratory for the titans. Its strange creatures and alien magic lend credence to that idea. (Contested; 11–16)

Winterspring. The snowy vale of Winterspring—one lair of the blue dragonflight, which watches over the flow of magic—sees frequent conflict between goblin trading posts and night elves working to reclaim their ancient fortifications. (Contested; 11–16)

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.HYhrbxOJhm7Ju2aP classes="noborder"]

Alliance and Horde in Kalimdor

Judging solely by the size of claimed territories, Kalimdor would seem solidly Horde aligned. The Bilgewater goblins dominate Azshara. Durotar is held by the orcs, and Orgrimmar serves as the capital of both the orcs and the Horde. The Mulgore plains, ancestral birthplace of the tauren and now populated by countless tribes, anchor the Horde’s claims in the southern part of the continent. Whether they’re from cities such as the tauren capital of Thunder Bluff or wandering nomadic bands, even peace-loving tauren are quick to arms when it comes to defending their communities.

Compared to those bastions, the territories of the Alliance are minuscule. Yet small doesn’t equal unimportant. Kalimdor is the ancestral home of the night elves, whose bonds to these lands are historical, cultural, and spiritual. The draenei are equally bound to and fortified within the Azuremyst Isles, where they first arrived on the world of Azeroth. The night elves and draenei fanatically defend their homelands, and their willingness to battle over neighboring territories has long prevented the Horde from cementing control over all Kalimdor.

Perhaps the fiercest conflicts occur in the forests of Ashenvale and Felwood, which stand directly between Alliance and Horde strongholds. The factions skirmish in Ashenvale over territory and its rich lumber and herbal resources. On the other hand, nobody wants the toxic and monster-ravaged Felwood, but its strategic location means neither side can allow the other to claim it.

While the Northern Barrens are firmly Horde territory on paper, guarding the large and open area is a logistical nightmare. Alliance scouting parties regularly slip into the Barrens to spy on or sabotage Horde endeavors. These missions become bloody when Alliance teams encounter inexperienced Horde warriors training on the proving grounds. Eliminating bands of soldiers is a tempting and strategically sound objective for Alliance teams.

Across the southern reaches of Kalimdor, the Alliance and the Horde maintain strongholds in scattered outposts, towns, and small cities, all of which stand in contested territories. None of these strongholds are secure enough to consider themselves safe, let alone to serve as a launching point for wider conquest.

Given the dangers that haunt Kalimdor, neither the Alliance nor the Horde would likely bother trying to expand its grasp were it not for the ancient magic and other secrets so prevalent in the region. The Alliance regularly lands military forces on the coasts of the Great Sea, hoping to overwhelm—or at least bypass—existing Horde strongholds and acquire those mystical or mysterious wonders.

Kalimdor Adventures

The adventure sites of Kalimdor range from cultural and holy places of lost or fallen cultures to hidden repositories of the most ancient powers of Azeroth.

@UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowBlackfathomDe]{Blackfathom Deeps}. The dungeon of Blackfathom Deeps, located on the Zoram Strand in Ashenvale, is detailed in chapter 6.

@UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowDiremaul00000]{Dire Maul}. Formerly the Highborne elven city of Eldre’Thalas, the vast ruin known as Dire Maul is overrun by ogres, undead, and satyrs. It is detailed in chapter 6.

Maraudon. Maraudon is a combination of elemental temple and centaur burial ground located within the Valley of Spears in Desolace. Giants, oozes, and demons roam the tunnels of this sprawling complex, as do centaur ghosts and corrupted dryads.

Master’s Glaive. Deep in the wilds of southwestern Darkshore, a colossal adamantine blade protrudes from the near-fossilized remains of a grotesque, tentacled aberration. The Master’s Glaive was the weapon of Kronn, the only survivor of a band of twenty giant soldiers sent by the titans to battle Soggoth the Slitherer, herald of the Old Gods. Kronn might have left his weapon in Soggoth’s corpse as a symbol of victory, or perhaps because he was so greatly wounded that he lacked the strength to retrieve it. Many believe the blade’s presence prevents Soggoth from reawakening. The area is occupied by Twilight’s Hammer, a nihilistic sect that seeks to revive the Slitherer—and then the Old Gods.

@UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowOnyxiasLair00]{Onyxia’s Lair.} The lair of the black dragonflight’s broodmother, Onyxia, is located in Dustwallow Marsh and detailed in chapter 6.

Ragefire Chasm. Ragefire Chasm is a cleft within the city of Orgrimmar. Despite its location in the heart of the city, it has long served as a hideout for cultists—first demonic cultists of the Burning Blade clan, and later a group called the Dark Shaman, made up of former members of Twilight’s Hammer after the cult’s fall.

Ruins of Theramore. Once a great fortified city and the Alliance’s mightiest stronghold in Southern Kalimdor, Theramore is now a blasted ruin. Destroyed by an incomprehensibly powerful mana bomb, the city is slowly being reclaimed by the Dustwallow Marsh. Salvagers of the Alliance and the Horde, as well as independent adventurers, scout partially standing buildings and any accessible underground chambers, hoping to recover weapons, goods, and treasures of old. In addition to the threats posed by rival scavengers, those who trespass on this mass grave also face ghosts and small cults and sects that maintain secret hideouts in the ruins.

Temple of Ahn’Qiraj. The ancient, sprawling Temple of Ahn’Qiraj is home to alien qiraji emperors and their secrets.

Tower of Althalaxx. In the distant past, the Tower of Althalaxx was the home of Athrikus Narassin, faithful vassal of the night elf Queen Azshara. Years of boredom and stunted ambition led Athrikus astray, and many millennia after he vanished, he reappeared as the leader of the Cult of the Dark Strand, an offshoot of the demon-worshipping Shadow Council. Athrikus was eventually defeated and his home partly burned, but the remnants of Althalaxx still attract scavengers, researchers, and adventurers. The warlock’s fiendish research and the Soul Gems that empowered him—still containing the spirits of trapped Highborne night elves—are rumored to lie deep within the spirit-haunted ruins.

Wailing Caverns. The corrupted Druids of the Fang dwell in a complex network of underground chambers and defiled waters called the Wailing Caverns in the Northern Barrens. These night elf druids came to the caverns imagining that they could connect the waters inside to the Emerald Dream to restore life and growth to the Barrens, but once inside they succumbed to the Emerald Nightmare. Corruption spread through the waters and twisted the druids into serpent cultists.

Zul’Farrak. Once the adobe-walled city of the Sandfury trolls in northwestern Tanaris, Zul’Farrak was slowly whittled away by the encroaching desert and constant war. Since the Cataclysm, it has been a sun-blasted ruin, half buried in the sands. While the surviving trolls have moved on, the ruined city isn’t wholly abandoned. The population of warbeasts formerly kept by the Sandfury has grown out of control, hives of silithid have moved in, and undead trolls lurk in the city’s deepest levels. These threats, and strange magic worked by Sandfury occultists, remain to be discovered by adventurers.

Eastern Kingdoms.name: Eastern Kingdoms
Eastern Kingdoms.text:
The Eastern Kingdoms is the eastern remnant of the ancient continent that broke apart in the Great Sundering. Before that catastrophe, these lands were held by the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowTroll00000000.JournalEntryPage.AdBTf7AxlTOG09N7]{Amani} and Gurubashi troll empires. In modern times, the Eastern Kingdoms have been the primary battlefield in the wars between the Alliance and the Horde, and the land still bears scars of those conflicts.

The northernmost portion of the Eastern Kingdoms, a distinct landmass called Lordaeron, was the seat of the human-led Empire of Arathor, which later fragmented into the Seven Kingdoms: Alterac, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowHuman00000000.JournalEntryPage.6Qdz0upjGNKOEfUj]{Dalaran}, Gilneas, Lordaeron, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowHuman00000000.JournalEntryPage.O9p7hdJXavAFDVD8]{Stromgarde}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowHuman00000000.JournalEntryPage.b5Jfulr9rBcvQYN9]{Kul Tiras} (on an island to the southwest), and @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowHuman00000000.JournalEntryPage.592An0ENopmrf0AR]{Stormwind} (far to the south). These kingdoms existed in uneasy peace alongside the high elves of Quel’Thalas and the Wildhammer clan of dwarves in the Hinterlands until first the Horde and then the undead Scourge ravaged the entire region.

The southern part of the Eastern Kingdoms, dominated by the kingdom of Stormwind and the dwarf capital of Ironforge, also holds the Blasted Lands, the site of the Dark Portal where the Horde first entered the world.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.EfoaZMGbynnHtJsb]

Eastern Kingdoms Regions

The Eastern Kingdoms are made up of three landmasses:

Lordaeron. Lordaeron in the north is divided from the rest of the Eastern Kingdoms by a narrow strait crossed by the magnificent Thandol Span, a feat of dwarvish engineering.

Khaz Modan. Khaz Modan is the central part of the Eastern Kingdoms, encompassing the region from the Thandol Span in the north to Blackrock Mountain in the south.

Azeroth. The southernmost region, stretching from Blackrock Mountain and the Burning Steppes in the north to the tip of the Cape of Stranglethorn in the south, is named Azeroth, but the name is more commonly used for the world as a whole.

The regions that make up each of these landmasses are described below.

Alterac Mountains. Once home to a small but thriving human kingdom, the resource-rich Alterac Mountains are now locked in a struggle between the Crushridge ogre clan and the noble-led criminal organization known as the Syndicate. (Contested; 5–10)

Arathi Highlands. The great strongholds of both the Alliance (Stromgarde Keep in the west) and the Horde (Hammerfall in the east) in the Arathi Highlands hold a tentative peace, one that extremists on both sides strive to sabotage. (Contested; 5–10)

Badlands. The blasted and inhospitable expanse of the Badlands is claimed by both the Alliance and the Horde but is controlled by neither. It is home to fearsome beasts, savage troggs, and members of the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowBestiaryOfAze.JournalEntryPage.jnGTp7LiVzQO8DTY]{black dragonflight}. (Contested; 11–16)

Blasted Lands. Scorched and devastated by the magic surrounding the appearance, destruction, and reappearance of the Dark Portal, the Blasted Lands are full of wandering beasts native to multiple worlds and timelines. Alliance and Horde teams occupy small outposts, ever watchful for further incursions. (Contested; 11–16)

Burning Steppes. Land traffic from the southern regions to Dun Morogh and points north must traverse the mountain passes and jagged badlands of the Burning Steppes. Dark Iron dwarves, reinforced by soldiers from Stormwind, help keep travelers safe from marauding orcs of the independent Blackrock clan. (Contested; 11–16)

Deadwind Pass. Horde invaders from Stonard in the Swamp of Sorrows occasionally attempt to take sections of Deadwind Pass. Greater threats in this gray, rotting, and haunted reach, however, are the Nightbane worgen, Deadwind ogres, and armies of ghosts. (Contested; 11–16)

Dun Morogh. The snowcapped forested mountains of Dun Morogh are the center of two major Alliance cultures, housing the dwarves’ capital, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowTheAlliance00.JournalEntryPage.oyPozuVXGusZiqIe]{Ironforge}, and the war-torn, catastrophe-shattered city of @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowTheAlliance00.JournalEntryPage.bbKM8aDik71xsqGu]{Gnomeregan}. (Alliance; 1–4)

Duskwood. Duskwood has been cursed to a twisted darkness and suffers the depredations of undead and other bloodthirsty creatures. Its many inhabitants cling defiantly to their homes and their fealty to Stormwind. (Alliance; 5–10)

Elwynn Forest. The communities of the lush hardwood Elwynn Forest—such as Goldshire and Stormwind City—are the heart of the Kingdom of Stormwind and modern human culture. (Alliance; 1–4)

Eversong Woods. The Eversong Woods—ancestral home of the blood elves—enjoy a near-perpetual spring. But portions of the forest are still scarred by the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowConflictsOfAz.JournalEntryPage.YRwQ3wrLM22odUUP]{Scourge} and suffer the constant rise of undead. (Horde; 1–4)

Ghostlands. In the Ghostlands, a portion of the Eversong Forest never reclaimed by the blood elves, the undead blight is widespread. The dangerous Amani tribe of forest trolls also maintains a stronghold in the region. (Horde; 1–4)

Hillsbrad Foothills. Although largely under Forsaken control, the Hillsbrad Foothills and surrounding plains see many of the bloodiest and most frequent battles between the Alliance and the Horde, rendering any claim over the area tentative at best. (Horde; 5–10)

Hinterlands. The mountainous Hinterlands are home of the Wildhammer dwarves and their famous trained gryphons. This region sees a constant back-and-forth between the Wildhammer dwarves and high elves on one side and Forsaken and Revantusk trolls on the other. (Contested; 5–10)

Loch Modan. Drained during the Cataclysm, the dry lake bed of Loch Modan and its fertile surroundings remain under dwarves’ control despite constant threats of troggs, kobolds, and Mo’grosh ogres. (Alliance; 1–4)

Plaguelands. The aptly named Plaguelands were badly infested by the Scourge, resulting in a region of constantly rising undead. (Contested; 11–16)

Quel’Danas. The forested isle called Quel’Danas contains the Sunwell, a source of arcane and Light energy sacred to the blood elves. Its tremendous magical power makes it an attractive target to forces both mortal and demonic. (Contested; 17–20)

Redridge Mountains. The normally idyllic Redridge mountain range, home to many Stormwind communities, sees occasional raids from Blackrock orcs and the undead Scourge. (Alliance; 5–10)

Ruins of Gilneas. After many years of changing hands, the Ruins of Gilneas have been returned to the Alliance and the subjects of Queen Tess Greymane. Horde extremists still harry its streets in violation of the treaty, and scattered remnants of the Scarlet Crusade’s occupation forces commit atrocities against both factions. (Contested; 5–10)

Searing Gorge. Despite being blackened and broken by an ancient eruption and recent industrial pollution, the Searing Gorge is a constant target for the Horde, for through it runs the only viable passage between Khaz Modan and the southern part of the continent. The powerful @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowDwarf00000000.JournalEntryPage.Ctzza0M3S3xta3Gv]{Dark Iron} dwarves live in the gorge. (Contested; 11–16)

Silverpine Forest. The massive, primeval Silverpine Forest is silent and haunted, pockmarked with homesteads and hamlets abandoned in the struggle between the Forsaken in the north and desperate pockets of living resistance in the south. (Horde; 1–4)

Stranglethorn. Stranglethorn is a patch of tropical jungle divided by a massive sinkhole. It boasts a wide variety of venomous flora and fauna, native trolls, and thriving communities of Blackwater Cartel pirates. (Contested; 5–10)

Swamp of Sorrows. Due to its proximity to the Dark Portal, the Swamp of Sorrows contains nearly as many Horde communities as it does Alliance. It is the site of some of the most frequent and largest faction battles fought on the subcontinent, even though it offers little in the way of desirable resources or terrain. (Contested; 11–16)

Tirisfal Glades. Green-skied and blight-tainted Tirisfal is a Forsaken stronghold, but the undead of the Horde are beleaguered by Scarlet Crusade soldiers and terrors of the Scourge. (Horde; 1–4)

Tol Barad. The desolate Tol Barad peninsula is home to the mystical prison of Baradin Hold, which is under the control of its powerful inmates. (Contested; 17–20)

Twilight Highlands. The Twilight Highlands are a boiling cauldron of conflict as the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowDwarf00000000.JournalEntryPage.cyFq9ds161YyDy5W]{Wildhammer dwarves}, the Dragonmaw orcs, the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowBestiaryOfAze.JournalEntryPage.DmsSoir1i1hgTyRj]{red dragonflight}, a few lingering twilight dragons, and the nihilistic Twilight’s Hammer cult vie with one another for control over the region’s fortresses and resources. (Contested; 17–20)

Westfall. Westfall was the site of much destruction across wars and catastrophes. It briefly broke away from Stormwind due to the costs of war. Strong economic assistance and renewed protection turned this fiefdom into the kingdom’s breadbasket. (Alliance; 1–4)

Wetlands. The Alliance claims the cold, gray swamp of the Wetlands, primarily because of the useful port of Menethil Harbor. A small community of night elves, Greenwarden’s Grove, and the dwarf-built fortresses of Dun Algaz and Dun Modr extend the Alliance claim over the eastern part of the swamp, but Dragonmaw orcs and a growing population of murlocs threaten the Alliance’s hold. (Alliance; 5–10)

Alliance and Horde in the Eastern Kingdoms

The conflict between the Alliance and the Horde defines the modern history of the Eastern Kingdoms. After four wars, starting with the opening of the Dark Portal and continuing intermittently over the course of almost thirty-five years, the conflict has simmered down to a tenuous truce. The Horde’s main power centers are the blood elf kingdom of Quel’Thalas in the north and the Ruins of Lordaeron, the new capital of the Forsaken. The Horde has only scattered holdings in the southern part of the region, with a few groups of orcs maintaining holdings in the Twilight Highlands, the Redridge Mountains, and the Swamp of Sorrows.

Gilneas is the only major Alliance holding in Lordaeron, but the Alliance is much stronger in the rest of the Eastern Kingdoms, with @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowTheAlliance00.JournalEntryPage.oyPozuVXGusZiqIe]{Ironforge}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowTheAlliance00.JournalEntryPage.w20Iuh5ocASVxvhS]{Stormwind}, and @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowTheAlliance00.JournalEntryPage.bbKM8aDik71xsqGu]{Gnomeregan} controlling most of the southern continent.

Despite the many horrors and indiscriminately violent groups that occupy the area—or perhaps because of them—Lordaeron has also witnessed some of the most significant strides toward peace between the Alliance and the Horde in the modern era. In the wake of Sylvanas’s departure from the Horde, the Desolate Council negotiated a peaceful turnover of the Ruins of Gilneas to the human and worgen subjects of Queen Tess Greymane, and King Danath Trollbane of Stromgarde signed treaties with Overlord Geya’rah of the Mag’har orcs. In both instances, this cooperation involves full military cooperation against shared enemies. The armies of Queen Tess and the Forsaken worked together to clear Scarlet Crusade intruders from the Ruins of Gilneas, while Danath and Geya’rah combine elements of the Kor’kron Guard and the 7th Legion into a single strike force to confront threats against both peoples.

Both situations are perilous, especially given that some members of each faction would love to see the peace fail. But if these partnerships can hold, they might provide an example of a better way forward for other factions of the Alliance and the Horde.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.apxpSAouk2r1t64r caption=false classes="noborder"]

Eastern Kingdoms Adventures

Given the ravages of the Scourge, many key Lordaeron sites are haunted, necromantic, or otherwise connected to undeath. To the south, a wide variety of adventure sites are linked to disasters caused by the greed, pride, or fear of the people living nearby.

Baradin Hold. Originally an immense fort with potent mystical defenses, Baradin Hold was repurposed as a prison for the worst criminals and dangers Azeroth—and worlds beyond—had to offer. Today, it holds power-hungry archmages, possessed Burning Legion fanatics, and demons and entities from the deep Void. Baradin’s Wardens have long since been driven off, leaving the inmates in control of the prison. While few adventurers would dare the halls of Baradin Hold, someone must travel there to ensure that the defenses still hold, that none of the inmates have escaped, and that no demon-worshipping or nihilistic factions are working to bring down the walls.

Blackrock Mountain. The many-layered dungeons beneath Blackrock Mountain include Shadowforge City, the capital of the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowDwarf00000000.JournalEntryPage.Ctzza0M3S3xta3Gv]{Dark Iron} dwarves; the Molten Core, where Ragnaros the Firelord enslaved those dwarves; and Blackrock Spire, where orcs, ogres, and trolls of the Dark Horde allied with the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowBestiaryOfAze.JournalEntryPage.jnGTp7LiVzQO8DTY]{black dragonflight} led by Nefarian.

The Cauldron. The massive dig site called the Cauldron is perhaps the greatest project of the Dark Iron dwarves. For much of its history, the Dark Iron clan forced prisoners to do much of the physical labor. The dwarves were taskmasters or drove mighty excavation machines. Since they rejoined other Alliance dwarven clans in the region, the Dark Iron dwarves have officially abandoned those practices, but some individuals and small companies refuse to alter their methods. Dark Iron dwarves employ adventurers to delve deep into the Cauldron’s subsections to retrieve prisoners and punish those who still use them as slaves. The Cauldron is home to a variety of fire-related elemental creatures, and possibly ancient creations of the titans or the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowConflictsOfAz.JournalEntryPage.QX2LRHkL98AMmC55]{Old Gods}.

Dark Portal. In the Blasted Lands, the orc warlock Gul’dan and the human Guardian of Tirisfal, Medivh, first opened the Dark Portal, allowing the orcs of the Old Horde to cross into Azeroth from the world of Draenor. All the struggle, bloodshed, and devastation of the conflict between the Alliance and the Horde stem from this initial event.

The portal also led to further interplanar conflicts and invasions by linking parallel realities and alternate histories. The greatest wizards and sages aren’t certain how the portal operates.

Although history provides substantial motivation for the Alliance, the Horde, and smaller factions to keep watch over the Dark Portal, the short span of mortal memory makes those observers few in number and unprepared for decisive action.

Deadmines. A sprawling set of underground gold mines extends beneath Westfall and northern Stranglethorn. Once a major source of Stormwind’s wealth, the mines were abandoned during the First War and later thought to be haunted, so they went largely untouched until the brigands of the Defias Brotherhood established a base there. The Deadmines are detailed in chapter 6.

Gnomeregan. Gassed and irradiated by a sabotaged effort at defending against trogg invasions, the gnomish kingdom of @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowTheAlliance00.JournalEntryPage.bbKM8aDik71xsqGu]{Gnomeregan} was occupied by troggs and the so-called “leper gnomes” who had been mutated by the catastrophe. Today, the gnomes and their Alliance allies work to retake what was theirs. From New Tinkertown, a segment of Gnomeregan already reclaimed, they plan and launch missions into the depths of the many-layered community. Outside adventurers, whether employed by the gnomes or sneaking in as independent treasure hunters, can expect to confront troggs, leper gnomes, cunning traps of mixed technology and magic, and horrors born in the deeps.

Karazhan. Karazhan is the tower of Medivh, the Guardian responsible for the opening of the Dark Portal. The tower is rumored to hold numberless magical secrets and dangerous artifacts, as well as the haunt of countless ghosts and other evil spirits.

Nethergarde Keep. The great citadel and fortified town of Nethergarde Keep was constructed on a bluff overlooking the main road through the Blasted Lands. While its primary purpose was to guard the Dark Portal, it also served as a trading hub and a laboratory from which arcane organizations could study the portal and its magic. Nethergarde fell to the Iron Horde in the most recent otherworldly incursion, and though the ruin was eventually retaken by combined Alliance and Horde forces, it hasn’t been rebuilt or refortified. Stormwind would like to reoccupy Nethergarde once any remaining dangers within are eliminated and any eldritch discoveries are cataloged and rendered safe.

Scarlet Monastery. Once the headquarters of the fanatical Scarlet Crusade, the haunted @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowScarletMonast]{Scarlet Monastery} is described in chapter 6.

Scholomance. Scholomance is a necromantic academy controlled and staffed by the Cult of the Damned on behalf of the Scourge. Adventurers might venture into the place in search of tomes containing forbidden knowledge, or they might hope to break the academy’s curse by bringing about the final death of its headmaster, a Cult of the Damned leader called Darkmaster Gandling.

@UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowShadowfangKee]{Shadowfang Keep}. Shadowfang Keep was first held by a power-hungry archmage, then by the Forsaken who used it to develop necromantic weapons, and then by worgen of the Bloodfang pack. The keep is described in chapter 6.

The Stockade. The prison of Stormwind City is called the Stockade. It has often held leaders of the Defias Brotherhood (see @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowDeadmines0000]{Deadmines} in chapter 6), as well as captured Horde spies, gnoll marauders, and other troublemakers.

Zul’Gurub. Zul’Gurub is an ancient temple-city in Stranglethorn. It was once the heart of the trolls’ Gurubashi Empire. The trolls who remain here are swift, brutal, and deeply resentful over what they have lost. Zul’Gurub holds relics of the greatest Gurubashi priests and rituals that might reawaken the avatar of their deity, Hakkar the Soulflayer.

Adventures in Azeroth.name: Adventures in Azeroth
Adventures in Azeroth.text:
The many regions of Azeroth contain ample opportunities for adventure. Some locations merit special attention due to their historic, cultural, or mystical significance.

Several of the regions covered in this chapter list such locations. A few are detailed substantially in @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowAdventuresInA]{chapter 6} and are referenced here only briefly. The summaries of other sites offer an understanding of what the dungeon or adventure site is and why it’s important. DMs can use these descriptions as springboards for expansion and development.

Northrend.name: Northrend
Northrend.text:
@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.Jw4CZhq5NSJlLSUk classes="noborder"]

Perched at the top of the world, the frigid wasteland of Northrend boasts inhabitants as unfriendly as its climate. The taunka, thick-haired cousins to the tauren, are far more territorial than their kin, though some have found common cause with the Horde. The walrus-like tuskarr see almost everyone as an enemy, and the towering vrykul—the link between titan-forged and humans—eagerly embrace any excuse for battle.

While Northrend’s ancient titan ruins, prisons, and laboratories aren’t entirely abandoned and draw the interest of the Alliance, the Horde, and other explorers, its place in history would be relegated to ancient myth and the occasional eldritch discovery—were it not that Northrend was also the lair of the Lich King and the source of the world-­threatening Scourge.

Ner’zhul’s soul was long imprisoned in Icecrown, emanating evil throughout the region, tainting the continent, raising the dead, and corrupting the world’s connection to the Shadowlands. Once that soul bound itself to Prince Arthas, it gained a physical form that enabled it to walk free once more. It was powerful enough to spread its blight and assemble the undead into a nigh unstoppable Scourge.

Arthas was finally defeated, his successor stripped of his power, and the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.items.Item.wowHelmofDominAS]{Helm of Domination} destroyed—putting an end to the Lich King once and for all. But his wickedness hasn’t entirely released its grip on the land. The @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowConflictsOfAz.JournalEntryPage.YRwQ3wrLM22odUUP]{Scourge}’s greatest strongholds are still in Northrend, though it is now more ravaging mob than disciplined army, and lingering evil remains in Icecrown. Even though the veil above Icecrown has largely healed, the links between life and death still bear the scars of Ner’zhul’s machinations.

Northrend Regions

Northrend is what remains of the northernmost region of the ancient continent of @UUID[.qaiPjLFDnOP1opTC]{Kalimdor} from before the Great Sundering. It forms a crescent arcing from the western horn of the Borean Tundra to the eastern horn of the Howling Fjord.

Borean Tundra. Along with the Borean Tundra’s frigid climate, its multiway conflicts involving the walrus-like tuskarr, the taunka, the local naga, and the undead Scourge, make the region hostile. (Contested; 5–10)

Crystalsong Forest. The inhabitants and flora of Crystalsong Forest were crystallized by an ancient accident involving the magic of elves and dragons. The forest now torments the few communities within its reaches with wretched horrors such as crystal dryads, crystal satyrs, and corporeal and spiritual undead. (Contested; 17–20)

Dragonblight. The wyrm graveyard called the Dragonblight holds countless bones, which the Scourge once sought to use to create undead frost wyrms. It is home to outposts of several cultures, but dragons appear to have departed. (Contested; 11–16)

Grizzly Hills. Despite the presence of warring furbolg tribes, the alpine-forested slopes of the Grizzly Hills have drawn settlers from both the Alliance and the Horde, as well as profit-driven business interests loyal to neither faction. (Contested; 11–16)

Howling Fjord. The jagged coastlines and high cliffs of the Howling Fjord are home to the warlike vrykul, descendants of titan servitors and progenitors of humanity. The Alliance and the Horde boast substantial presences here. (Contested; 5–10)

Icecrown. Although the mountainous, glacial region of Icecrown is no longer host to the lingering evil that was the Lich King, it remains a realm of death and gloom. (Contested; 17–20)

Sholazar Basin. Sholazar Basin is a lush jungle sprouting in the midst of frozen Northrend, occupied by myriad communities and fearsome beasts. Magical pylons, created in antiquity by the titans, protect the basin from both the icy environment and the undead Scourge. (Contested; 11–16)

Storm Peaks. The towering Storm Peaks, where the wind and the cold can kill even the most prepared explorers, are rife with ancient titan complexes. Some are still the homes of masters who have survived from bygone eras. (Contested; 17–20)

Wintergrasp. The frozen Wintergrasp valley sees some of the largest clashes between Alliance and Horde forces, as each seeks to lay claim to Wintergrasp Fortress—and the stores of titan-crafted relics locked in the Vault of Archavon. (Contested; 17–20)

Zul’Drak. The sprawling temple-city Zul’Drak, the final remnant of the Drakkari Empire, is now an icy ruin. Wandering its frozen streets are an array of undead horrors and the last Drakkari trolls, their minds shattered by the sacrifice of their animal gods. (Contested; 11–16)

Alliance and Horde in Northrend

The Borean Tundra is home to contingents of both the Alliance and the Horde, as most travel to Northrend passes through it. The great fortress of Warsong Hold serves as headquarters for the Horde on the frozen continent, while the fortified town of Valiance Keep serves that purpose for the Alliance. Smaller outposts of both factions exist across the icy expanse, and both sides watch each other warily, but overt hostilities are kept to minor skirmishes rather than full-on war. Each faction knows that it lacks the forces to decisively hold the entire tundra. Open war would deprive both sides of their only major access to Northrend and leave them open to tuskarr or taunka attack.

Beyond the Borean Tundra, both factions have established multiple strongholds across the continent, from the Alliance’s Valgarde and the Horde’s Vengeance Landing in the Howling Fjord to Frosthold and Camp Tunka’lo in the Storm Peaks. Bastions of the Alliance and the Horde can scarcely hold what territories they already have, let alone expand, due to their struggles against one another and the hazards of the merciless environment.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.ubNwRgP1WP41O5TS classes="noborder"]

Northrend Adventures

Although the Lich King is no more, his evil still scars the lands of Northrend. Many of the continent’s key locations still harbor his influence, whether through the surviving Scourge or the presence of his former allies.

@UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowAzjolnerub000]{Azjol-Nerub}. Azjol-Nerub—a sprawling underground network of corridors, crevices, and caves that was once the kingdom of the arachnoid nerubians—is detailed in chapter 6.

Naxxramas. Naxxramas is a former bastion of the Scourge and a flying necropolis that hovers over the Dragonblight. It was originally an ancient, subterranean ziggurat built by the nerubians of Northrend, but the Scourge conquered it and transformed it into a mobile citadel. The terrible necromancer (and later lich) Kel’Thuzad commanded the fortress and used it to begin the Scourging of Lordaeron.

Utgarde Keep. Towering Utgarde Keep was long a center of power for the vrykul, descendants of the titan-forged iron vrykul. Under the command of King Ymiron, these vrykul allied themselves with the Lich King and his undead Scourge. The war turned against them, and Ymiron was ultimately made undead before he was destroyed. The allegiances of the vrykul who still occupy Utgarde Keep are unknown. They conduct raids on travelers and local outposts, but the promise of ancient treasures and magical secrets makes Utgarde a tempting target for adventurers.

Vault of Archavon. Deep beneath Wintergrasp Keep, relics of the titans wait within the Vault of Archavon. The Alliance and the Horde constantly struggle over the fortress, but neither has acquired the secrets of the vault due to the immensely powerful and seemingly immortal giants and elemental revenants that dwell within.

Zone Progression.name: Zone Progression
Zone Progression.text:
In early versions of World of Warcraft, characters often followed a predictable path through the world as they advanced in level, entering more dangerous regions as their power increased. While that strict progression is no longer in place, some parts of the world are still more dangerous than others—and regions on other worlds and planes are more dangerous still. Thus, each region’s description in this chapter includes a parenthetical notation of the tier of play (1–4, 5–10, 11–16, 17–20, or endgame) during which it’s most appropriate for characters to adventure in that region. DMs can use this information along with the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowConflictsOfAz]{conflict arcs} in chapter 6 to decide where in the vast world of Azeroth their adventures will unfold—or DMs can ignore it entirely and let the players decide where their characters will roam.

Islands and Isles.name: Islands and Isles
Islands and Isles.text:
In addition to its major continents, Azeroth also boasts a number of large islands and archipelagos.

Broken Isles

The chain of Broken Isles holds remnants of multiple ancient civilizations. It once hosted the portion of the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowElf0000000000.JournalEntryPage.C4fRQxnWgEHPPK1W]{night elf} empire whose nobles dabbled with demonic forces and birthed the first naga. It is also home to a population of vrykul zealots. But it is perhaps most infamous for the Tomb of Sargeras, the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowConflictsOfAz.JournalEntryPage.mOeoKWAu3OOx8LP9]{Burning Legion}’s unholy passage to Azeroth.

Azsuna. Once the crown of night elf civilization, the island of Azsuna was corrupted by the demonic dealings of Queen Azshara. Night elf ghosts, naga, and servitors of the Burning Legion prowl the island. (Contested; 5–10)

Broken Shore. Sunken and then magically raised, the blasted Broken Shore has been partly restored through the efforts of druidic circles. Yet no druid magic can cleanse the Tomb of Sargeras or the extraplanar evil that emanates from within. (Contested; 17–20)

Eye of Azshara. The Eye of Azshara is heavily occupied by naga determined to unearth and master powerful magic. They hope to use it to support Queen Azshara’s quest to dominate and destroy other peoples. (Contested; 17–20)

Highmountain. The great peaks and deep vales of Highmountain churn with the ongoing war between local tauren and the deep-dwelling drogbar, who stole the sacred Hammer of Khaz’goroth. (Contested; 5–10)

Stormheim. The vrykul of the rocky, chasm-crossed isle called Stormheim stand united under their God-Queen Sigryn, ready to battle the Burning Legion or any other threat to what they view as holy land. (Contested; 5–10)

Suramar. Once isolated from the world by a millennia-old mystical shield, Suramar—the island home of the nightborne elves—still suffers the scars of its prior government’s alliance with the Burning Legion. (Contested; 11–16)

Val’sharah. Formerly a land of natural protection under the stewardship of night elf druids, the rich forests of Val’sharah have been corrupted by creatures of the Emerald Nightmare. (Contested; 5–10)

Dragon Isles

The Dragon Isles, the ancestral homeland of the dragons, were separate islands even before the Great Sundering, and they teem with life that has been shaped by the powerful draconic magic suffusing the isles.

Amirdrassil. A new World Tree, nurtured in the Emerald Dream and planted with the blessing of the Dragon Aspects, serves as a new homeland for the night elves after the destruction of Teldrassil in the Fourth War. (Alliance; endgame)

Azure Span. The ancient home of the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowBestiaryOfAze.JournalEntryPage.g0t7ZVVSG0Vr7TGr]{blue dragonflight}, the Azure Span, is a beautiful region of snowy peaks, misty forests, and icy tundras inhabited by tuskarr, gnolls, and furbolgs. (Contested; 11–16)

Forbidden Reach. The Forbidden Reach was created by Neltharion the Earth-Warder as a training ground for the dracthyr soldiers he created. (Neutral; 1–4)

Ohn’ahran Plains. The verdant Ohn’ahran Plains, the ancient home of the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowBestiaryOfAze.JournalEntryPage.wWBP2j6xQk2Tc6AZ]{green dragonflight}, are now inhabited by centaur tribes. (Contested; 11–16)

Thaldraszus. The mountainous heights of Thaldraszus are the seat of the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowConflictsOfAz.JournalEntryPage.2MFeGdKlqPZz0K4s#dragon-aspects]{Dragon Aspects}, who rule the isles from the city of Valdrakken. (Contested; 17–20)

Waking Shores. The Waking Shores are the ancestral home of the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowBestiaryOfAze.JournalEntryPage.jnGTp7LiVzQO8DTY]{black} and @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowBestiaryOfAze.JournalEntryPage.DmsSoir1i1hgTyRj]{red dragonflights} and a wild land rife with elemental magic. (Contested; 5–10)

Zaralek Cavern. Deep beneath the Dragon Isles, Zaralek Cavern is the laboratory where Neltharion experimented in creating life and first communed with the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowConflictsOfAz.JournalEntryPage.QX2LRHkL98AMmC55]{Old Gods}, setting him on the path to become the cataclysmic force called Deathwing. (Contested; endgame)

Kezan and the Lost Isles

The small island regions of Kezan and the Lost Isles make up the original home of the goblins. Although goblins have since become far more prevalent in other areas, they still retain control here, for themselves and the Horde. Although much of Kezan has been destroyed by volcanic eruptions, goblin communities still survive on the surface and underground. The @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowTheHorde00000.JournalEntryPage.KTz4fgoqdKuVuqzy]{Bilgewater goblins} landed on the Lost Isles archipelago after fleeing Kezan. While many of them moved to Azshara, others remain to mine local resources. (Horde; 1–4)

Khaz Algar

Khaz Algar consists of a small island (the Isle of Dorn) atop a larger subterranean expanse. Long forgotten by the outside world, Khaz Algar was rediscovered when the Worldsoul of Azeroth revealed its name to Magni Bronzebeard, accompanied by dire warnings of danger. The Council of Six, leaders of the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowKirinTor00000]{Kirin Tor} and rulers of Dalaran, agreed to teleport the flying city to Khaz Algar to address this danger, but the city was destroyed. The survivors have taken up residence in Dornogal while adventurers explore the forgotten realm.

Azj-Kahet. The deepest part of the subterranean realms below the Isle of Dorn is Azj-Kahet, the capital of the last remaining empire of living @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowBestiaryOfAze.JournalEntryPage.Vn0nqG9jIqbeeiRJ]{nerubians}. Xal’atath, the Harbinger of the Void, has forged an alliance with the nerubian queen, Ansurek, who has shaped her people into an army corrupted by the blood of the Old Gods, poised to assault the surface world. (Contested; endgame)

Hallowfall. The vast subterranean realm of Hallowfall is poised between the shallower Ringing Deeps and the depths of Azj-Kahet. It is illuminated and warmed by an immense crystal called Beledar, lodged in the cavern ceiling like an artificial sun. An expeditionary force from the distant Arathi Empire found its way to this cavern a decade ago and established a colony there, centered in the city of Mereldar. The Arathi consider Hallowfall to be a holy land, revealed to their emperor in a divine vision from the Sacred Flame. (Contested; endgame)

Isle of Dorn. The surface of Khaz Algar is the Isle of Dorn, a lush island populated by @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowEarthen000000]{earthen}. It is a verdant paradise with sweeping vistas, cascading waterfalls, and majestic mountains, with the massive fortress and earthen capital of Dornogal at its heart. (Contested; endgame)

Ringing Deeps. The colossal cavern known as the Ringing Deeps is home to the Machine Speakers, the earthen who maintain the gigantic machines built by the titans ages ago, as well as to large numbers of kobolds. (Contested; endgame)

Kul Tiras

Home to the kingdom of the same name, Kul Tiras was settled by human pilgrims from Gilneas. Although the ruling houses and the mighty Kul Tiran fleet are bound by treaty to the Alliance, political squabbles and constant pirate activity have allowed the Horde to make substantial territorial gains.

Drustvar. Under the oversight of House Waycrest, mountainous Drustvar provides ore for all Kul Tiras. Witch cults, elementals, and survivors of the Drust vrykul clan constantly endanger that vital trade. (Contested; 5–10)

Mechagon. Civil war has ravaged Mechagon, home of the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowGnome00000000.JournalEntryPage.4OFFV6SmsonDI0kZ]{mechagnomes}. The island boasts stores of not only gnomish technology but also mechanical wonders of the titans. (Contested; 11–16)

Stormsong Valley. Stormsong Valley is a forested highland that provides food and lumber to Kul Tiras. It is threatened by naga, invading Horde forces, and more. (Contested; 11–16)

Tiragarde Sound. The waters of Tiragarde Sound are the heart of Kul Tiras. The capital city of Boralus, situated on a small island in the sound, is marked by political squabbling between House Proudmoore and other noble houses, which prevents the government from taking effective action against pirate armadas and criminal gangs. (Contested; 5–10)

Pandaria

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowArtHandouts00.JournalEntryPage.bPnJmPfqMlz9uOJi classes="noborder"]

Home to the proud @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowPandaren00000]{pandaren}, Pandaria was hidden behind a veil of mists until that veil was dispersed in the Cataclysm. Pandaria recently (and barely) fought off the forces of Lei Shen, Thunder King of the mogu, a vicious titan-forged people. Although slowly recovering, Pandaria remains under threat from the Thunder King’s followers, the insectile mantid, and the influence of sha—physical avatars of negative emotions. Pandaria maintains relations with both the Alliance and the Horde, though some communities ally with one over the other.

Dread Wastes. Separated from the rest of Pandaria by the Serpent’s Spine, the Dread Wastes are the home of ravening, insectile mantid. (Contested;
11–16)

Isle of Giants. The obscure Isle of Giants is home to primordial beasts—rare or even extinct in other lands—and the Zandalari trolls who raise them. (Contested; 17–20)

Isle of Thunder. Lei Shen waged his war from the Isle of Thunder. Although the king is gone, his surviving mogu forces threaten to rise once more. (Contested; 17–20)

Jade Forest. A lush rainforest full of bamboo groves and ancient ruins, the Jade Forest has the greatest concentration of Alliance and Horde forces in Pandaria. Different villages have sided with different factions, rekindling old rivalries. (Contested; 5–10)

Krasarang Wilds. The Krasarang Wilds are home to viciously territorial saurok lizardfolk. The gloom-shrouded jungle is also subject to the Sha of Despair’s oppressive miasma. (Contested; 5–10)

Kun-Lai Summit. Despite (or perhaps because of) the mogu population, both the Temple of the White Tiger and the hideout of the Shado-Pan, two of Pandaria’s most potent groups of defenders, stand within the towering peaks of Kun-Lai. (Contested; 11–16)

Timeless Isle. Neither the divine August Celestials nor the yak-like, fire-worshipping yaungol are as strange as the Timeless Isle itself. It exists only at seemingly random interludes, vanishing from the world for months or years at a time. (Contested; 17–20)

Townlong Steppes. The Shado-Pan can scarcely contain the dangers raging across the Townlong Steppes, which include not only the clashing yaungol and mantid but also the influence of the Sha of Hatred. (Contested; 11–16)

Vale of Eternal Blossoms. The sacred Vale of Eternal Blossoms, a region of powerful nature magic and the remnants of titan experiments, has suffered the depredations of the mogu, extremist Horde factions, and the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-world-warcraft.book.JournalEntry.wowConflictsOfAz.JournalEntryPage.QX2LRHkL98AMmC55]{Old Gods}. (Contested; 17–20)

Valley of the Four Winds. Containing the lush fields of Pandaria’s breadbasket and watered by blessed rivers from the Vale of Eternal Blossoms, the Valley of the Four Winds is imperiled by mantid breaching the protective wall called the Serpent’s Spine. (Contested; 5–10)

Wandering Isle. For many generations, the boldest pandaren gathered on the back of the colossal sea turtle Shen-zin Su to venture across the world. The turtle’s back is the Wandering Isle, a small isle that traverses the seas. Its inhabitants are the descendants of a rare breed of pandaren: explorers who left their mist-shrouded homeland behind in search of knowledge and adventure. (Neutral; 1–4)

Zandalar

What was once a lush land of forests and fields is now partly sunken and ravaged by time and magic. This was the heart of the Zandalari Empire when trolls dominated most of the world. Today, it hosts the proud and resentful remnants of that mighty realm.

Nazmir. Nazmir is a stinking swamp littered with ruins and inhabited by blood trolls and occult practitioners who seek to free the Old God G’huun. (Contested; 5–10)

Vol’dun. Vol’dun is a scorching wasteland used as a place of exile by the trolls of Zuldazar. It is otherwise home only to vulpera and serpentine sethrak. (Contested; 11–16)

Zuldazar. Called the City of Gold, sprawling Zuldazar is the most ancient city in the world. It is the last remnant of the trolls’ Zandalari Empire. (Contested; 11–16)

The Great Sea

Of all Azeroth’s seas, the Great Sea warrants most attention. At its center churns the Maelstrom, an eternally swirling vortex where the Well of Eternity was destroyed during the Great Sundering. It is home to multiple underwater civilizations.

Nazjatar. An undersea city of stone structures and coral groves, Nazjatar is the center of naga power but has splintered into powerful competing factions during the absence of Queen Azshara. (Contested; 17–20)

Vashj’ir. Sunken during the Great Sundering, the ruins of Vashj’ir are home to a large naga population that seeks to steal the power of the elemental lord Neptulon the Tidehunter. (Contested; 11–16)
